## 0. Rulings applied, verdict, and what changed

### 0.1 Operator rulings (2026-11-05)

| ID | Ruling | Where it lands |
|---|---|---|
| R1 | Regen harvesting and FC charging are both hard requirements | F, H.7, H.8 |
| R2 | Path A on the current board with the BQ25798EVM | whole document |
| R3' | No circular charging loop (bus -> charger -> pack -> BT boost -> bus) and no runaway. The charger may stay powered through Run only with a fail-safe Teensy-commanded hard inhibit plus a hardware comparator backstop | B.1, B.6, F.3 |
| R4 | PCB and pack survived 2026-11-04 | D (no damage repair) |
| R5 | MCU hardware watchdog is required future work; no unattended charger session until its forced-hang test passes. **r4 consequence:** a Teensy hang inside an FC window cannot survive the next purge (F.4), so **no FC-charge window, attended or not, runs before T-W-01 passes**; R1's FC charging therefore depends on R5, and this design treats the watchdog as a precondition of FC charging, not as future work. **r9-6 (2026-11-12, operator rulings D2-1/D2-2):** R5 is the only hang defence (no hardware hang inhibit exists) and a precondition of all charger arming: no charging of any kind (regen, qualification, FC windows) runs before the R5 firmware exists and T-W-01a passes, and no FC window runs before the full T-W-01 passes | G.3, F.4, FR-04, FR-05, T-W-01a, T-W-01, T-D-14 |
| R6 | FC charging only in windows between H-20 purges. A predicted purge interrupts the window so the battery is back on the bus before the dip | F.4, H.8 |
| R7 | Regen and FC charging may run concurrently (IO CSV row 31 to be amended) | F.2, F.3, D.3 |
| R8 | The BT-current trip residual (INA253 floor ~0.1 A, residual loop up to ~0.29 A) is accepted for now | J.1 |
| R9 | The VBT->VCHG keep-alive is last resort. Design without it, give the test that decides it and any lower-drain alternative | B.5 (r9-3, 2026-11-12: the keep-alive option is withdrawn; fallback 2 is kept), H.9, H.15, T-B-09 (**superseded in r9:** B.5, H.9-H.10, H.15, T-B-09) |
| r9-1 (2026-11-12) | Tap review and permit gate: ten taps (T1, T7b, T2, T5, T6, T10, T13, T16, T17, T17r); the reduced permit under the operator stance 'trust firmware except the regen H1 AND UVB check'; the agreement term FCCP = FCC_ON AND NOT FCC_OFF; the gate on five LVC packages (U105, U106, U107, U110, U118); CE_DRV buffered by U106A, R108 47.0 kOhm; the latent faults 4a, 4b and 4c accepted with a truth-table sweep at every build; T5, T6 and T10 pairwise non-adjacent on the tap connector | A.4, A.8, B.1-B.3, B.7-B.9, F.2, F.3, F.5, J.1 |

### 0.2 Verdict

**On paper the design is feasible. No datasheet fact blocks it. The circular loop is impossible by construction in every
mode, with any single fault (section F.3), except the R8 residual, which the operator has accepted.** **r9-1 (2026-11-12, tap review and permit gate):** the claim above holds only as a register- and firmware-backed claim. In regen-armed Run the hardware keeps one check, H1 AND UVB, so with FC_CHARGE off the bus cannot feed the charger through the regen path even with firmware hung (R3). In an FC window the loop barrier is firmware only (I-9; BTB_OFF and BT_OK are removed). Single faults that no hardware detects remain and are accepted risks: a gate output stuck HIGH or an ILIM_REL short, QUAL stuck HIGH, /CE stuck LOW, and a fault that drives the shared T5 node HIGH (J.1 items 13 and 18-21; F.3). **r8-17 (2026-11-12,
D-38):** pack-voltage protection rests on firmware. A corrupted charger register is caught by the same-transaction read-back
(FR-46) and the 20 ms verify, and a pack above `LIMIT_V_BATT_MAX` 8.5 V on BT_VOLTAGE (pin 25) latches `CHG_PACK_OV`, takes
/CE HIGH through P5 (FR-47) and latches OV_BATT (FR-47(a) is a firmware requirement, not yet implemented; until then only
OV_BATT acts). The r6 hardware term OVN (the BQ29200 cell OVP through tap T22) is removed,
because a 30 AWG wire cannot be soldered practically to BQ29200 pin 8. No firmware- and register-independent pack barrier
remains, and firmware sees the pack, not each cell; the operator accepts this downgrade, so finding
vreg-corruption-no-fixed-pack-ovp is closed by operator ruling, not by hardware (F.3, J.1). The hard inhibit no
longer acts on a Teensy hang by itself (r9-6, 2026-11-12, D2-2): the R5 MCU watchdog (G.3) is the only hang defence, a hang charges for at most t_WDT + 1 ms (about 51 ms at the 50 ms RTWDOG target, J.2 item 69), and no charging of any kind runs before the R5 firmware exists and T-W-01a passes (**superseded in r9:** "no longer depends on a live MCU: a hardware heartbeat monostable drops /CE and holds ILIM_HIZ within TW_HB_MAX of a Teensy
hang (20-46 ms widened band, H.17, set by T-C-10)"), and the Run-entry qualification window is time-limited in hardware (B.1,
U111). Every inhibit node is observed at the far end, on the EVM pin itself (B.6). (**superseded in r9:** the two sentences above. The QUAL one-shot U111 and the far-end senses U203/U204 are removed or not fitted (r9-1, r9-2). The qualification release is bounded by the firmware limit T_QUAL_MAX 0.46 s (B.1, F.5 I-5), and no inhibit node is observed at the EVM pin.) The ILIM_HIZ hard converter-off depends
on EN_EXTILIM = 1, which firmware never writes and verifies every 20 ms (G.1); whether HIZ survives EN_EXTILIM = 0 is open
until T-B-21.

**r9-8 (2026-11-12, operator process decisions):** the r8 audit run 001 no longer certifies this design. The 2026-11-12 tap review and the second-round decisions remove parts on which r1-r8 fail-safe arguments, calculations and review dispositions rest: among them the heartbeat U113, the QUAL one-shot U111, the far-end senses U203 and U204 (not fitted), BT_OK (U104), BTB_OFF (U115), RGN_ON (U121) and the FCCEIL terms. In addition, three latent single faults are no longer detected by hardware (gate outputs stuck HIGH, QUAL stuck HIGH, /CE stuck LOW; J.1). The statements of this document that rest on removed parts stand only until audit run 002 re-establishes or replaces them. Until the run-002 adjudication is recorded in L.9, no revision of this document is certified (0.4, L.9).

**r9-5 (2026-11-12, plug-on outline):** the carrier is a removable plug-on board on the rectangle x 18.584-67, y 7-94 (MB frame; 48.416 x 87 mm, 4212 mm²). Samtec SSQ sockets in the 22 MB CHG holes take TSW pin strips on the CR underside, and the CR underside stands 11.05 mm above the MB at a hard stop, with no standoff, no key and no polyimide sheet (A.7). The CR is assembled by stencil, paste and reflow, with all SMT parts on the top and L4 a solid GND layer facing the MB (A.8). The tabs, the feet FT1/FT2, the bottom clearance rule, the thermal band and the r7 sheet of the r7 paragraph below are history. No electrical value changes with the outline; the placement, the region table and the geometry checks are re-derived after the new-outline generator step, TODO(generator step).

**r7 (round 4):** the carrier (CR) now extends past the 31 x 33 mm Ag105 footprint by two tabs, tab X toward the Teensy and
tab Y toward L-FC. A bonded foot supports the far end of each tab (FT1, FT2; A.7). The EVM and the EIB are unchanged in
function; both move onto one insulating EVM plate on the chassis (A.7, C EM23). Every fail-safe argument of r1-r6 holds
unchanged (the J.1 mechanical mitigation of the VCHG-IN segment holds with the A.3 W-lead dressing path of r7 review 7, which keeps every W lead >= 2 mm in plan from the pin-10 joint and the IN strip); the only EIB circuit change is the damping resistor R276 in series with E1 (A.5, B.6). Revision r7 settles six design
points:

- Side, extent and support: tab X (x 48.70-65.00, y 56.30-68.30) and tab Y (x 17.70-37.56, y 67.14-76.00) give a
  1394.06 mm² r7 outline, and FT1 and FT2 carry the tab ends (H.23(a), H.23(i)).
- EVM on or beside the CR: no; the 88.90 x 88.90 mm EVM fits neither on the CR nor beside it on the MB, so the EVM plate
  stands past the MB +y edge (A.7, H.23(l)).
- EIB merge onto the CR: no; the EVM plate stands on the chassis and the CR sits on the MB, so the two are not one rigid
  co-mount, which is a G1 condition (J.2 item 60). At the H.23(l) reference placement, seven of the eight EVM points of the
  E leads lie 64.3-129.4 mm from the CR edge, and JP12 pin 1 (E1) lies 55.8 mm from it (`round4/calc/r7_calc.py` H.23(u), revision 5 (**superseded in r8:** hand calculation): the plan
  distance from each `round4/work/evm_geometry.md` Table 1 point to the nearest r7 outline point, the tab Y corner
  (37.56, 76.00); **superseded in r7:** 69.4-130.1 mm, of which every point but E1 was measured to the tab X top edge). A merge would export the
  unbuffered ILIM_HIZ node, REGN, /CE and STAT over those lengths, so the EIB stays (B.6).
- Layer count: the CR stays a 4-layer, 1.6 mm board with every SMT part on the top side, assembled with one stencil in one
  reflow pass (r9-3, 2026-11-12; top-only booking on the plug-on outline TODO(calc)) (**superseded in r9:** double-sided at
  73.55 % top and 69.04 % bottom area use, against 101.8-109.9 % single-sided (H.23(e))).
- Retired constraints: the footprint confinement, the r6 area budget, the named bottom keep-out and the MB power-copper shadow
  retire; the bottom clearance rule replaces the last two (A.7).
- Modifications: every EVM modification (EM) and every MB modification (PM) stays necessary; the text of EM5 and EM23 changes,
  and PM0, PM1, PM3, PM4, PM6 and PM7 gain r7 steps (C, D.1).

The r7 outline is not frozen before the operator survey T-A-08 (MS1-MS8) passes. MS2 decides the EVM placement and the W-lead
maxima (A.3, A.7).

**r8 (audit run 001, `docs/reviews/charger-design/run-001-2026-11-10.md`):** the adjudicated findings change no fail-safe
argument of r1-r7. Revision r8 settles seven points:

- FLT pad bridges: R106s 1.00 kOhm 1 % between U101 FLT and the F17 pad (r9-4: the J-TAP T16 pin; the pad bridge becomes the T5-T16 cavity pair, A.8) holds the FLT sink current at <= 3.377 mA, a factor
  of 2.96 below the 10 mA absolute maximum (tps2663.pdf sec 6.1), and the FLT LOW readback at <= 0.325 V (H.23(n); A.4, A.8, B.4).
- T3 timing: the REG03-05 raise write completes 1.359 ms after the edge at 100 kHz, against the 1.5 ms FR-07 deadline; the
  REG01-07 verification follows the write as four field reads, outside that deadline (H.23(o); G.1, FR-46).
- Flash and SD admission: the flash commit and the SD close have separate gates; Idle admits on battery support, and only
  the SD close and sync may run in State 99 phase 3 (G.3, FR-43).
- W1/W2 conductor: 20 AWG stranded copper, insulation OD 1.60-1.75 mm, twisted at a 20-25 mm pitch; in the modelled
  envelope the IN peak at a hard short is 33.79 V at 290 mm, against the 36 V limit (H.23(p); A.3).
- B1 riser and stacking: a machined insulating wedge B1R replaces the B1 spot and holds the trunk on the full requirement
  profile (minimum margin 0.504 mm, H.23(s)); W5 rests on the trunk, and the stack top is 20.750 mm above the MB, which is
  information under D-H (H.23(t); A.3).
- Firmware and test definitions: the FR-12(b) pin-38 criterion separates the stuck-path test from complete discharge
  (H.23(q)); the FR-12(b3) Idle probe (FR-23 exception EX1) and the FR-23 FLT-LOW diagnostic read (EX2) become explicit
  exceptions to the FR-23 gate; T1 steps 8b-8c (F.5), T-B-16 and T-F-16 are restated (F.5, I) (**superseded in r8:** "the
  FR-48 Idle probe"; "T1 step 8b, T-B-16 and T-F-16 are restated (G.2, I)").
- Traceability: every hand calculation of the r7 closing pass is a calc row of `round4/calc/r7_calc.py` revision 5
  (H.23(u)-(w)), the r8 integration figures are revision 6 (H.23(x)), the r8 verification-round figures are revision 7 (H.23(y)), and the TPS26630 datasheet is local (`references/Datasheets/tps2663.pdf`, K).

The design is not yet *proven*, because some of the numbers that decide whether regen is captured come from no primary
document. Each one is in the test registry (section I) with a pass criterion and a named design change if it fails. The
decisive tests are:

1. **T-E-03** (VESC over-voltage behaviour with V-MOT held at 19 V): decides regen for any charger on this rig.
2. **T-B-09** (regen-restart decision, R9; r9-3: the fail branch is fallback 2; **superseded in r9:** keep-alive decision, R9): VCHG decays below the RT1987 UVLO and the BQ25798 battery-short threshold within
   0.17-0.78 s of cruise (H.9). Whether a burst then restarts fast enough is not in any datasheet. The pass criterion is the
   V-MOT peak (<= 20.5 V) with a current source into the measured C_VMOT (T-E-04 first) behind a series resistor equal to the
   input-path resistance (r3); the regen-armed budget for dead time plus response is only 0.33-0.80 ms once the 0.12-0.19 ohm
   input path is counted (H.7, H.19). The analysis says a keep-alive is **likely needed for regen in the regen-armed
   cruise mode**, and **not needed** for FC charging or for regen inside an FC window. The design carries a Run-gated
   keep-alive as a do-not-populate option (B.5) that draws nothing when parked (r9-3, 2026-11-12: the keep-alive option is withdrawn and has no footprint; T-B-09 is kept, and a failure leads to fallback 2, the fused VBT-VCHG link of B.5, or to a keep-alive redesigned in a later round).
3. **T-B-06 / T-B-10 / T-B-12** (inhibit latency, warm response, VINDPM reload after a raise): none is specified by TI.
4. **T-B-19 / T-E-11** (charge current 3.10 A accepted by the pack, and the efficiency at 19 V in): the regen capability
   margin rests on them (H.7).
5. **T-E-01 / T-E-12 / T-E-06** (purge statistics at 1 kHz, under window load and under traction swings; BT boost output
   against the FC-only bus; RT1987 hand-off delay): they size the pre-emption lead and decide whether the battery picks up a
   purge in time. **r3:** an FC-only bus cannot ride through a purge (the purging stack is its only source), so every early
   purge inside a window, and every pre-emption that misses the hand-off, is a State 99 (F.4). T_LEAD is sized from the
   measured onset-error tail against an operator-set State-99 ceiling per hour of window time. **r6:** until T-F-07/T-F-07b and
   T-E-01 have measured the battery rescue at 1 kHz, the rescue close is compiled out (`PURGE_RESCUE_ENABLED 0`) and every
   early purge inside a window is a State 99 counted against that ceiling (F.4).
6. **T-F-08** (BT_BUS close transient from an FC-only bus): decides lever 3(i) or 3(ii) in F.4 before any FC window runs
   with traction load.
7. **T-B-21** (does ILIM_HIZ < 0.75 V still stop switching with EN_EXTILIM = 0?) and **T-A-01b** (is the pin-7 tap free of
   the encoder nets?; r9-4: T-A-01b is withdrawn with tap T20 and the /CE readback): they decide whether the hard converter-off is register-independent and whether the /CE readback pin
   is clean.
8. **T-B-20** (r3: VBUS valid -> REGN -> PG_STAT -> ILIM ADC read timing, no maximum in SLUSDV2C): sets T_REGN_MAX, on which the
   Run-entry sequence is now anchored (r9-1: the far-end monitors are removed; **superseded in r9:** "and the far-end monitors").
9. **T-C-04** (r3: eFuse IN-side spike at a hard short): the r2 100 nF on U101 IN let the IN pin reach up to 134 V in the ideal
   simulation (H.19); the r3 local bulk brings it to <= 33 V, which T-C-04 confirms at reduced voltage first.
10. **T-W-01a / T-W-01** (r4: MCU watchdog forced-hang test, R5; r9-6, 2026-11-12, D2-1: split in two): **T-W-01a (forced hangs without a purge) gates every charger arming (qualification, regen and FC charging); the full T-W-01 (adds the T-D-14 purge cases) gates every FC-charge window.** With the MCU hung in a window the
   charger keeps converting until the R5 reset (r9-6: no hardware hang inhibit exists; **superseded in r9:** "heartbeat stops the charger, but"), BT_BUS stays open and FC_BUS/MOT_PWR stay closed, so the next purge (period 10.34 s)
   collapses the FC-only bus under a frozen MCU, and D-MT-EN can then re-energise the drained V-MOT node by itself (F.4
   "Teensy hang inside a window"). Only a watchdog reset that drops every EN before the stack recovers removes that path
   (RTWDOG target 50 ms against a 100-140 ms purge, G.3). The alternative is the hot-standby battery option (F.4). Until T-W-01
   passes, R1's FC charging is not available. Until the R5 firmware exists and T-W-01a passes, no charging of any kind runs, regen harvesting and qualification included (r9-6; **superseded in r9:** "regen harvesting is unaffected"). The R5 firmware is built with the rest of the new-charger firmware in the handoff after the PCB design.
11. **T-A-05b / T-E-13** (r4): the D-BC-RG OVP trip measured against the D107 TVS breakdown (D107 must never become the regen
   sink), and the Teensy BT_VOLTAGE calibration that decides whether VREG may return from the interim 8.32 V to 8.40 V without a
   nuisance OV_BATT latch at the end of every charge (H.20).
12. **T-C-09** (r6): the timer-domain latency (<= 1 ms with SD, USB and I2C stress) that the brake feed-forward, T3 and the
   pre-emption step budget now rest on (FR-45). (r8-17, D-38: T-F-17, the BQ29200 pack-OV permit test, is withdrawn with the
   permit; T-E-13 now also carries the pack-OV trip accuracy.)

### 0.3 What changed

Round 3 r0 against the round-2 record (kept for history):

| # | Change | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Permit network rewritten for R6/R7 (B.1) | R7 lets REGEN stay closed in an FC window |
| 2 | Concurrent regen + FC mode with a firmware-raised, hardware-blanked input ceiling (F.2) | R7; a static FC ceiling would trip the VESC on the 3 -> 1 m/s brake (H.7) |
| 3 | Purge scheduler and pre-emption (F.4); bus-sag comparator UVB | R6 |
| 4 | FC windows open warm from REGEN (no cold FC close) | R7 |
| 5 | No M8 keep-alive in the baseline; Run-gated keep-alive option (r9-3, 2026-11-12: the keep-alive option is withdrawn; T-B-09 is kept and its fail branch is fallback 2, B.5) | R9 |
| 6 | eFuse TI TPS26630RGER | study condition 7 |
| 7 | Carrier in the vacated CHG footprint | removes six bodge wires at the pads |
| 8-11 | SN74LVC3G06 open-drain stages from REGN; BQ25798 trickle and 2.5 V/cell findings; JP7 removal; C-D8/C-D10 are 0805 | datasheet findings |

| r8-17 | **Pack-voltage protection moved to firmware (2026-11-12, operator ruling D-38):** the r6 pack-OV permit is removed: tap T22 and pad F08, R178, D108, R179, the Schmitt inverter U123, the gate U122 and the decouplers C134/C135; ARM_OK again drives both U114 inputs, as before r6. Reason: a 30 AWG wire cannot be soldered practically to the outer toe of BQ29200 pin 8 (DRB pad 0.35 mm wide, 0.65 mm pitch to VDD), and an open T22 would read OV through R179 and refuse all charging. Pack-voltage protection rests on FR-46 (read-back after every limit write) and on the BT_VOLTAGE (pin 25) OV_BATT fault at `LIMIT_V_BATT_MAX` 8.5 V; FR-47(a) re-points `CHG_PACK_OV` to BT_VOLTAGE > `LIMIT_V_BATT_MAX` with P5 LOW (a firmware requirement), and FR-47(b) keeps the unexpected-/CE-sense rule as a carrier-inhibit trip. Charging no longer needs J-BL. Accepted costs: no firmware- and register-independent pack barrier remains; the finding is closed by operator ruling, not by hardware; firmware sees the pack, not each cell; the 8.5 V trip sits ~180 mV above the 8.32 V VREG and 146 mV below the 8.646 V ADC ceiling. ### 0.4 Review-design loop

Round 3 r0 was self-reviewed in three passes (safety, electrical, integration). Round 1 of the independent review then
produced 53 findings (about 45 distinct issues), each verified against the primaries by a second agent. All were found real.
All are applied: most as written or as amended by their verifier, ten with a different implementation, which section L
explains. Round 2 produced 44 verified findings (one blocker); all are applied (r2 table above), the differing
implementations are in section L, and the r2 closing pass re-ran `calc/r3_calc.py`, regenerated both SVGs and re-checked the
test-ID cross-references. Round 3 produced 34 verified finding keys (about 31 distinct issues, none a blocker); all are applied
(r3 table above), the differing implementations are in section L.3, and the r3 closing pass re-ran `calc/r3_calc.py` (new
section H.19), regenerated both SVGs and re-checked the FR and test-ID cross-references. Round 4 produced 32 verified finding
keys (about 31 distinct issues, none a blocker); all are applied (r4 table above), the differing implementations are in section
L.4, and the r4 closing pass re-ran `calc/r3_calc.py` (new section H.20), regenerated both SVGs and re-checked the FR and
test-ID cross-references. Round 5 produced 24 verified finding keys (about 20 distinct issues, none a blocker); all are applied
(r5 table above), the differing implementations are in section L.5, and the r5 closing pass re-ran `calc/r3_calc.py` (new section
H.21, H.11/H.14/H.15/H.18 re-booked), regenerated both SVGs and re-checked the FR and test-ID cross-references. Round 6 produced
16 verified finding keys (16 distinct issues, none a blocker); all are applied (r6 table above), the differing implementations are in
section L.6, and the r6 closing pass re-ran `calc/r3_calc.py` (new section H.22; H.8 lead table and the H.20/H.21 timing rows
re-derived), added `calc/pin_identity_check.py`, regenerated both SVGs and re-checked the FR and test-ID cross-references.
The closing consistency pass of r1 re-ran `calc/r3_calc.py`, regenerated both SVGs, checked every designator against the
EVM BOM and the MB part list, and checked that every test ID cited is defined in section I. What remains open is in
section I.

**r7:** round 4 began with a design phase, before any review round. It produced four fact-finding notes, three candidate
carrier layouts with an independent assessment of each, and the calculation H.23 (`round4/calc/r7_calc.py`). The notes are in
`round4/work/`, and the r7 table in 0.3 lists the resulting changes. The decisions are recorded in `round4/work/r7_design_basis.md`. The round-4 log, including review round 7, is `round4/review_loop.md`. **Review round 7** produced 60 verified findings (33 confirmed, 27 partially confirmed, 0 refuted, none a blocker; by the verifier's severity 10 major and 50 minor) and 7 unverified nits. All are applied (review-round-7 block in 0.3), and the differing implementations are in section L.7. The closing pass re-ran `round4/calc/r7_calc.py` as revision 4, applied the operator statement of 2026-11-10 that the MB and its PCBs have no maximum height (D-H), and applied the 10 mm switched-conductor rule as a 3-D distance (A.3).

**r8:** the final independent audit, run 001 of 2026-11-10 (`docs/reviews/charger-design/run-001-2026-11-10.md`), reviewed the r7 text in two rounds: a Codex review with finding-verifier agents and an independent first-pass reviewer, then a Codex counter-review in the same thread. It produced 13 adjudicated findings (0 blocker, 3 major, 10 minor) and seven adjacent items A-01 to A-07, each folded into one finding. The round-4 walkthrough raised one more finding, CHG-R1-W01 (the W5 and trunk vertical order). All 14 are applied in r8 (r8 block in 0.3). The agreed fix and its rejected parts in the run-001 adjudication table are binding; the dispositions that differ from the finding as written, and the choices that the agreed fix left open, are in section L.8. The r8 closing pass extended `round4/calc/r7_calc.py` to revision 6 (H.23(n)-(x); every revision-4 line unchanged), regenerated the three round-4 SVGs (R106s, the B1R wedge, the W1/W2 wire) and re-checked the test-ID cross-references of section I.

**r9 (r9-8, 2026-11-12, operator process decisions, `hardware/charger_evm_r8/decisions_2026-11-12/round2/dec_process_2026-11-12.md`):** the 2026-11-12 decisions remove parts on which r1-r8 rest, so the r8 audit no longer certifies the design (0.2). The r9 round runs in eight steps:

1. Apply the 2026-11-12 decisions to this document and to the CR netlist (`gen/sch.py`, `gen/check_constraints.py`, the `gen/layout_cr.py` part list, and `LAYOUT_DECISIONS.md` per Table 4 of `OUTLINE_CHANGE_REASSESSMENT_2026-11-12.md`).
2. Strip the removed parts (U104, U108, U109, U111, U113-U116, U121, U123/D108/R178/R179, T18/F101/R172, the EIB U203/U204/R258-R265 and the FCCEIL terms; with them the retired B.5 keep-alive and U117 option) from `round3/calc/r3_calc.py` and `round4/calc/r7_calc.py`, re-run both, and re-derive H.4, H.19, H.20, H.22 and every row whose output changes; the r7-outline H.23 rows retire (section H). This step precedes the audit, so that the audit checks the new numbers.
3. Run audit run 002 (scope and method below).
4. Write the generator for the plug-on outline, in parallel with step 3; the geometry calculation for the new outline belongs to this step, TODO(calc: new-outline geometry).
5. Place the parts on the plug-on outline, after the netlist is frozen.
6. Run the full route-race (a reference at four or more seeds, one diagnosis, tested change requests, one design-owner batch). The routability is not re-measured first on the r7 outline or on the reduced netlist (operator choice over the plain board-routing gate). The route-race needs the new region table, side flags and power geometry (`OUTLINE_CHANGE_REASSESSMENT_2026-11-12.md` section 8).
7. Run the DRC and the constraint check.
8. Prepare the fabrication package.

The operator checks the work at four points: after step 1 (a diff summary); after the audit adjudication (fix approval, after which the netlist is frozen); after step 5 (placement images, before routing); and before the fabrication package and any order. Audit run 002 covers B.1, B.3, B.6, B.7, F.2-F.5, G.2, G.3, J.1, every reopened section-L disposition (L.9, Table L.9-1) and the A.8 adjacent-pair short table, re-derived for the 10-conductor J-TAP cavity map (a T5-T6 common-mode short reproduces the SAFETY-1 release). The method is hybrid: the adversarial review loop (a Codex review, finding-verifier agents and an adjudication) on B.1, F.3, F.5, G.3, J.1 and the reopened dispositions, and a self-review on B.3, B.6, B.7, F.2, F.4, G.2 and the A.8 table. The run-002 adjudication replaces L.8 as the certification of the design and is recorded in L.9. The stale r7 layout work is in `hardware/charger_evm_r8/archive_r7_outline/`.

### A.2 Carrier header pins (the 22 Ag105 holes)

Pad coordinates and nets: `references/Scale_Car_Board_20260624.sch`, `.brd` 20260625 (element CHG at (47.498, 34.544) mm,
R180; 2.54 mm pitch, one column of 10 pins (1-10) and one column of 12 pins (11-22), 25.00 mm apart, 1.1 mm drill). Pin numbers are the Ag105 pin numbers; board coordinates are in
A.8. **r6 (finding cr-coordinate-convention-mirror-ambiguity): every coordinate in this document is an Eagle `.brd` board coordinate,
top view, origin at the MB origin, +x right, +y UP.** KiCad's PCB editor counts y downward, so a hand-typed coordinate must be
entered as -y, or (PM0) the capture is done in the frame of the imported `.brd`; the 22-hole pattern is symmetric under a y-mirror,
so a mirrored capture still fits the MB with every pin reversed in its column and only the pin-identity gate of T-A-06 catches it.

**r9-4 (2026-11-12, operator decision Leads):** the W leads stay soldered into plated through-holes on the CR. When the CR is removed, each W lead is disconnected at its existing EVM terminal: W1/W2 at the J1 screw terminal, W3/W4 at the J5 screw terminal, W7 at the J8 KK housing and W6 at J7 (termination TODO(verify: SLUUCB5E J7 type)); W5 unplugs at both IDC ends as before. No W-lead connector is fitted on the CR. The taps go to one CR connector, J-TAP (A.4). W6 and W7 move from SMT pads to plated through-holes, so every W lead is a through-hole joint on the CR.

Currents: W1/W2 carry at most the eFuse limit (2.41 A for <= 202 ms, H.5) and normally <= 1.76 A (the regen ILIM clamp
maximum, H.4). W3/W4 carry <= **3.21 A** (r5, finding ichg-upper-tolerance-omitted-in-ratings: regen-image ICHG 3.10 A + 3.5 %, the
SLUSDV2C §6.5 buck-mode ICHG_ACC upper bound at 2 A extrapolated; unspecified above 2 A, T-B-19 measures). Drops and losses in H.11.

**r7 review 7 (W-lead dressing path, D-F2; H.23(l)).** The **W-lead dressing path** replaces the straight segment from each CR hole to the tab X top edge. Every W lead leaves its CR joint inside the A.3 RTV bead and joins the **trunk**, which runs +y on the footprint along x 25.80. W3 runs up x 24.40 from its hole and pairs with W4 at y 57.00; W6/W7 join at y 59.20 and W1/W2 at y 62.60. The trunk passes onto tab Y and turns +x at y 69.60, on the -y side of the FT2 fill-hole disc. It rises to y 71.10 past the U101 courtyard and the +x pocket, and to y 71.75 past the tap pads. It leaves the CR at the tab Y +x edge (x 37.56) and reaches the MB tie base A1 at (60.50, 73.50) without crossing tab X.

From A1 the **west group** (W1, W2, W6, W7) runs to (58.00, 76.00) and straight up x 58.00 to the MB +y edge. The **east group** (W3, W4, W5) runs up x 61.00 to (61.00, 85.50), clear of D-FC-EN and C-D1, and then to the MB tie base A2 at (71.50, 88.00). It crosses the MB +y edge within 30 mm of A2. W5 rises at J101 and folds once toward -x at >= 8 mm above the CR top to (28.70, 46.83). It runs +y over the footprint interior to (28.70, 73.10), then +x at y 73.10. It steps to y 73.80 over x 42.00-44.50, clear of the tap pads, and from (28.70, 64.01) rests on top of the trunk until A1 (r8, H.23(t); stacking note below) (**superseded in r8:** and stays at its fold height until A1; the r7 review 7 close text 'at >= 15.00 mm above the MB over tab Y and down to the fold height at (47.25, 73.80), under the 3-D rule below'). From A1 it lies flat on the MB with the east group.

The **dressing rule** keeps every W lead >= 2 mm in plan from the pin-10 joint, the IN strip (C102a/b/c, R102, D107), the U101 courtyard and the +x pocket. The same 2 mm applies to every 1x10 and 1x12 post tip and every tap pad, and no W lead lies over the tab X tap field. The designed path meets the rule at the jacket edge: minimum 2.02 mm (W5), 2.08 mm (W3) and 2.09 mm for the other leads. It keeps 2.03 mm from the tap-field courtyard. **r8 (H.23(p)):** with the r8 W1/W2 insulation OD of up to 1.75 mm the worst lead is W1 at 2.017 mm from the +x pocket and the trunk half-width is 2.443 mm; the largest W1/W2 OD that keeps the 2.0 mm rule on this path is 1.787 mm. The r7 jacket envelopes are ASSUMPTIONS (half-width 2.37 mm for the trunk, 1.73 mm for the west group, 2.00 mm for the east group and the W3/W4 pair, 1.00 mm for one 18 AWG lead; TODO(measure: MS2/MS7)). The MB rework points C-D2 with R171, D-FC-EN with its EN bodge resistor, and C-D1 keep >= 1.5 mm: 4.21 mm, and 2.03 mm for W5.

W5 has two exceptions to the 2 mm rule. Over the J101 region (x 37.00-40.75) the ribbon edge lies 0.775 mm in plan from C102b, because A.8 sets the J101 region 0.50 mm below the IN strip. There the ribbon is >= 8 mm above the CR top, held by the spacer bead S1. On tab Y the ribbon overlaps the L-FC body by 0.68 mm in plan; the 3-D rule below sets the ribbon bottom there >= 15.00 mm above the MB, and in r8 the ribbon rests on the trunk at 19.850 mm above the MB (H.23(t)). The 3-D rule closes the L-FC overlap; the C102b exception stays open (J.2 item 62) (**superseded in r8:** >= 12.3 mm above the MB (L-FC body height TODO(verify: L-FC datasheet)). Both exceptions wait for an operator ruling (J.2 item 62)). r8 (H.23(y) row (5)): W5 passes over the FT2 fill hole on top of the trunk, 19.41 mm above the MB, bonded to the trunk with RTV. To re-bed FT2 after PM4 (6), cut the W5-to-trunk RTV locally over the fill hole and lift W5; re-bond W5 to the trunk after the bed cures (T-F-12, T-A-09) (**superseded in r8:** "W5 also passes over the FT2 fill hole at its fold height, so a re-bed of FT2 first lifts W5 from S2 and S3.")

The 10 mm switched-conductor clearance of the r7 rev-2 routes cannot be met on the CR. The designed path keeps 3.39 mm from the L-FC body, and W5 overlaps it in plan by 0.68 mm. The L-FC body lies 0.862 mm past the tab Y +y edge, and the 2 mm dressing rule closes every other exit from the footprint. A raster search over every plan path that keeps the 2 mm rule gives at best 5.12 mm for the trunk bundle and 9.34 mm for a single lead. From A1 on, every lead keeps 10.38-13.01 mm. The 10 mm figure has no stated pickup basis; the decision of 2026-11-10 below applies the rule as a 3-D distance (**superseded in r8:** so its acceptance on the CR is an open operator ruling (J.2 item 62)).

**r7 review 7 close (3-D switched-conductor rule, decision 2026-11-10; H.23(l)).** The 10 mm switched-conductor rule is applied
as a 3-D distance. The switched conductors are the VSW-FC and VSW-BT pours, the L-FC and L-BT bodies and the REG-FC and REG-BT
boxes. Where the plan distance d from a jacket edge to a switched conductor is < 10 mm, insulating spacers or RTV beads hold
the jacket bottom at >= H + sqrt(10² - d²) above the MB top, and at >= H + 10 mm where the two overlap in plan. H is the
conductor top: 0 mm for the pours, 1.0 mm for REG-FC/REG-BT (VQFN-HR, `TPS61288LRQQR.pdf`) and 5.0 mm for L-FC/L-BT
(ASSUMPTION from the HCM1A1305V3 size code, TODO(verify: Eaton HCM1A1305V3 drawing), MS3 caliper). The decision rests on the
operator statement of 2026-11-10 that the MB and its PCBs have no maximum height (D-H). The L-FC body controls every lead:

- The round leads W1-W4, W6 and W7 share one run from B1 (25.80, 64.50) to (50.45, 72.09). On the CR the jacket bottom must be
  >= 14.41 mm above the MB, that is 10.14 mm above the CR top; the worst point is (36.00, 71.10), 3.39 mm in plan from L-FC.
  Off the CR, from (37.75, 71.10) to (50.45, 72.09), it must be >= 14.35 mm above the MB. The required height is 5.48 mm at
  B1, 13.72 mm at y 69.60, 14.41 mm at x 36.5, 13.45 mm at x 41.5, 11.95 mm at x 44.0, 8.61 mm at x 46.7 and 3.27 mm at
  x 49.2. **r8 (H.23(s), H.23(t)):** these figures use the r7 trunk half-width 2.374 mm. With the r8 half-width 2.443 mm
  (W1/W2 OD 1.75 mm, H.23(p)) the requirement starts at (25.80, 64.450), 0.050 mm before B1, and reaches its CR maximum of
  14.433 mm above the MB (10.168 mm above the CR top) at (36.00, 71.10); it is 14.432 mm at x 36.5, 13.495 mm at x 41.5 and
  12.018 mm at x 44.0.
- W5, from (28.70, 65.67) to (47.25, 73.80), needs a ribbon bottom >= 15.00 mm above the MB. **r8 (H.23(t)):** the ribbon
  rests on the trunk there, 19.850 mm above the MB at the B3 level, 4.850 mm above that requirement; the W5 minimum
  margin over its own requirement, 1.866 mm, lies at (28.70, 64.01) (H.23(y) row (5); **superseded in r8:** "and meets its
  own requirement with 1.866 mm of margin").
  It still overlaps L-FC by 0.68 mm in plan (**superseded in r8:** The ribbon therefore rises from its 8 mm fold to
  >= 10.735 mm above the CR top (+2.73 mm).)
- From A1 on, no spacer is needed (10.38-13.01 mm in plan).

**r8 (B1 riser and CR-end strain relief, CHG-R1-D03; H.23(s)).** On the r7 trunk the requirement rises from 1.216 mm above
the CR top at B1 to 7.555 mm, reached 2.675 mm past B1 (H.23(w)(1)). A level post at B1 and the r5 jacket bead cannot both
hold: W2 reaches B1 4.26 mm from its joint, so its 5.0 mm bead ends at (25.80, 65.24), 0.74 mm past B1, where the jacket must
stand 4.538 mm above the CR top (H.23(s)). The trunk therefore climbs a ramp from the CR copper. The **B1 riser (B1R)** is a
machined insulating wedge (G10/FR-4 laminate or PEEK, ASSUMPTION) bonded to the CR top with the 0.05 mm acrylic transfer tape
of the feet (A.7). B1R replaces the 3.0 x 3.0 mm B1 bead spot. Its footprint is x 23.55-26.05, y 62.54-67.10 (11.40 mm²; the
+x edge lies on the W2 pad exclusion x 26.05). Its ramp face rises at 65 degrees from the toe at y 62.54 to an apex 9.78 mm
above the CR top at y 67.10 (H.23(s)). r8 (lateral support, H.23(y) row (4)): the 2.50 mm face supports 51 % of the 4.885 mm
trunk width; the trunk centreline x 25.80 lies 0.25 mm inside the +x face edge, so the trunk overhangs 2.19 mm on +x and
0.19 mm on -x. The H.23(s) profile check holds for a cohesive round bundle whose lowest line lies on the face, because its
lower surface then stands at or above the face plane across the whole width (0.013 mm at the +x face edge). RTV therefore
binds every trunk lead into one round bundle and bonds the bundle to the ramp face from the toe to the apex, so no lead
overhangs the face edge on its own. The wedge is not widened: a wider block in the footprint interior needs a new part-box
and exclusion check (J.2 item 68).

The leads leave the CR copper at the toe and lie on the ramp face. From the apex the trunk spans free for 10.4 mm along its
path, through T2 at a rise of 5.1 degrees, to B3. **B3** becomes an insulating post that holds the trunk jacket bottom
10.7 mm above the CR top (14.965 mm above the MB): the CR maximum of the requirement, 10.168 mm, plus a 0.50 mm design margin
(ASSUMPTION: sag, wedge and post height tolerance), rounded up to 0.1 mm. From B3 the trunk runs level to the tab Y +x edge
(x 37.56). The full profile meets the requirement plus the margin at every 0.05 mm from T1 to x 37.56. The minimum margin is
0.504 mm at T2 (25.80, 69.60), where 9.497 mm is required and 10.001 mm is built above the CR top (H.23(s)).

The 65 degree slope is chosen because it is the shallowest computed slope at which W1 and W2 still join the trunk on the CR
copper: the ramp height at T1 is 0.13 mm, below the 0.800 mm W1/W2 jacket radius. At 55 and 60 degrees the latest toe is
y 60.25 and 61.45, and W1/W2 would join a raised trunk; at 70 degrees the apex rises to 10.39 mm (H.23(s)). Lead stiffness
can only lift a lead above the ramp face, so a lead that does not follow the face still meets the 3-D rule. The T-A-06
item (8) dry fit confirms that the leads can be dressed onto the 65 degree face.

**Strain relief (r8 restatement of the r5 bead).** RTV bonds >= 5.0 mm of each lead jacket from its joint, on the CR copper
up to the toe and on along the ramp face. The wedge is bonded to the CR, so the bead keeps its CR-end function on the ramp.
W1 and W2 have 4.71 mm and 2.36 mm of copper run, so their bead continues on the ramp face. W3, W4, W6 and W7 have
5.42-17.45 mm of copper run and complete the bead on the copper. The jacket length from the joint to the apex is 15.36 mm
(W1), 13.01 mm (W2) and >= 16.21 mm for the other leads (H.23(s)). With B1R in place of the B1 spot the footprint interior
books 184.9 of 288.8 mm² = 64.0 % (<= 75 %); the tab Y booking is unchanged, because B3 keeps its spot (H.23(s)).

**r8 (W5 and trunk stacking, CHG-R1-W01; H.23(t)).** The W5 ribbon (8.89 mm wide, 0.9 mm thick, ASSUMPTION) and the
round-lead trunk overlap in plan from the trunk start at y 57.00 on the x 25.80 run to A1. W5 lies above the trunk over the
whole overlap. Below the riser the trunk top (9.150 mm above the MB) lies under the W5 fold (12.265 mm above the MB). From
(28.70, 64.01), where the trunk top passes the fold height, W5 rests on the trunk top and is bonded to it with RTV; the B3/S3
union spot carries both runs. The W5 bottom is the largest of the fold height, the W5 3-D requirement and the trunk top. The
trunk bundle thickness T_b is 4.885 mm, twice the r8 trunk half-width of 2.443 mm (H.23(p); ASSUMPTION as in H.23(l),
TODO(measure: MS2/MS7)). At the B3 level the trunk occupies 14.965-19.850 mm and W5 19.850-20.750 mm above the MB. The stack
top is 20.750 mm above the MB (16.485 mm above the CR top) at (32.80, 73.10); it is information only (D-H). W5 meets its own
3-D requirement everywhere with >= 1.866 mm of margin; the minimum lies at (28.70, 64.01), where W5 first rides on the
trunk (requirement 10.416 mm above the MB); over tab Y the margin is 4.850 mm (19.850 - 15.00) (H.23(y) row (5);
**superseded in r8:** "requirement (>= 15.00 mm above the MB over tab Y) with 1.866 mm of margin"). At the off-CR controlling points the requirement,
the trunk bottom and the W5 bottom are 13.495, 14.399 and 19.285 mm above the MB at x 41.5, and 12.018, 12.527 and 17.412 mm
at x 44.0 (H.23(t)). S1 and S2 hold the ribbon at the 8 mm fold, because both lie before the trunk start (y 57.00).

A lead that runs straight from 14.41 mm above the MB at B3 down to the MB top at A1 stands 10.751 mm above the MB at x 41.5,
against the 13.452 mm required there (H.23(w)(2), r7 basis). An insulating support therefore holds the trunk, with W5 on it,

T-F-12 measures the jacket-bottom heights over the full profile: the B1R check points of H.23(s), T2, B3 and the off-CR
controlling points. The plan raster bound (5.12 mm for the bundle, 9.34 mm for one lead) stays as information.

The **anchor rule** replaces the r5 chassis-tie rule: the unsupported lead length between two anchors is <= 30 mm, measured along the lead. The anchors are the A.3 joint beads, the B1R riser and the B3 bead on the CR (r8; **superseded in r8:** two CR RTV beads), three W5 spacer beads and two MB tie bases:

- the **B1R** riser wedge (r8, footprint x 23.55-26.05, y 62.54-67.10; it carries the CR-end bead of every lead that reaches it) and the RTV bead **B3** at (35.00, 70.80) (3.0 x 3.0 mm footprint, ASSUMPTION) on the B3 post that holds the trunk jacket bottom 10.7 mm above the CR top (r8, H.23(s)) (**superseded in r8:** RTV beads (3.0 x 3.0 mm footprint, ASSUMPTION): B1 at (25.80, 64.50) and B3 at (35.00, 70.80) (r7 review 7 close: each also an insulating spacer post that holds the trunk >= 10.14 mm above the CR top, 3-D rule above));
- W5 **spacer beads**: **S1** at (35.00, 47.69) and **S2** at (28.70, 53.42), each an RTV bead onto an insulating spacer on the CR that holds the ribbon at its fold height, and **S3** at (35.00, 73.10), which merges with B3 into one spot where W5 rests on the trunk and one bead bonds both runs (r8, H.23(t); **superseded in r8:** "each an RTV bead onto an insulating spacer on the CR that holds the ribbon at its fold height: S1, S2 and S3") (**superseded in r7:** S1 at (36.00, 46.83) and S2 at (28.70, 55.00); calc revision 4 moved them, below);
- **tie base A1**, 6 x 6 mm, centred at (60.50, 73.50) +- 1.5 mm, and **tie base A2**, 10 x 10 mm, centred at (71.50, 88.00) +- 1.5 mm, each bonded on the MB solder mask (sizes ASSUMPTION, TODO(verify: adhesive tie-base datasheet)).

The longest span between anchors is 26.0 mm, S2 to S3, with the revision-4 S2; the W5 spans are S1-S2 12.9, S2-S3 26.0, S3-A1 25.6, A1-A2 22.7 and A2 to the MB +y edge 10.6 mm, measured in plan; the r8 trunk span from the B1R apex to the B3 post edge is 10.4 mm (H.23(s)) (**superseded in r8:** 25.8 mm (B3 to A1)). Each tie-base zone (the base +- 1.5 mm) lies on the MB outside the CR shadow, clear of every MB part box (A1 0.51 mm from SNS-FC, A2 1.72 mm from CSNS-FC) and of every non-GND via. Under A1 the VBUS-FC layer-1 copper lies under solder mask; under A2 there is only the GND pour. Calc revision 4 moved S1 to (35.00, 47.69) and S2 to (28.70, 53.42). The old S2 also overlapped the W3/W4 trunk jacket by 0.51 mm. S1 now keeps 0.50 mm from the J101 region and from the divider strip and 7.33 mm from the nearest jacket. S2 keeps 1.33 mm from the W6/W7 pad exclusion and 0.51 mm from the W3/W4 jacket, against the >= 0.5 mm rule. The 3.0 x 3.0 mm footprints stay ASSUMPTIONS, and the T-A-06 dry fit confirms them. (**superseded in r8:** The S1 and S2 footprints are ASSUMPTIONS that reach 0.50 mm into the J101 region and 0.25 mm from the W6/W7 pads; the T-A-06 dry fit places them clear of both). The chassis tie past the MB +y edge is no longer exempt. It closes the last span from the last MB anchor, so it sits <= 4.4 mm past the MB +y edge for the west group (W1, W2, W6, W7; last span 25.6 mm), <= 18.4 mm for W3/W4 (11.6 mm) and <= 19.4 mm for W5 (10.6 mm). With a 2 mm margin the limits are 2.4, 16.4 and 17.4 mm, so the west-group tie sits effectively at the MB +y edge. No further MB tie base is added: a 6 x 6 mm +- 1.5 mm base, the A1 size, has no position on the west run, because C4C-FC, SNS-FC and the FC-CURR vias at (58.93, 83.57) and (60.71, 90.42) block it. The only fit is a 4 x 4 mm +- 1.0 mm base at (58.80, 95.00), 0.03 mm from C4C-FC (H.23(l)). MS2 records the tie positions against these limits. (**superseded in r8:** The chassis tie past the MB +y edge is an extra anchor with no distance limit, so the run from the last tie base to the chassis tie is exempt from the 30 mm rule. That run also meets the rule when the chassis tie sits within 4.4 mm (west group), 18.4 mm (W3/W4) or 19.4 mm (W5) past the MB +y edge; MS2 records the position.)

(**Withdrawn in r9-5:** the operator retired the film, so no strip is fitted; the lead path on the plug-on outline is TODO(design: lead group). History follows.) A **polyimide strip** (0.125 mm film with silicone adhesive, cut from the polyimide sheet stock) lies on the MB under the leads, from the tab Y +x edge to the MB +y edge. It follows the lead path within x 36.06-65.28, y 65.30-92.80 (lead envelope + 2.0 mm, via pad rims included) and stops at each tie-base footprint, so each base bonds to the MB solder mask. It covers CSNS-FC, MDAC-FC, OP-FC, ROP1-FC and SNS-FC where the leads cross them. It also covers nine untented non-GND vias (H.23(c2)): 3V3 (43.43, 71.63), (46.23, 71.63) and (61.79, 79.18); CS-MDAC-FC (49.99, 72.60); FC-CURR (51.16, 74.67), (58.93, 83.57) and (60.71, 90.42); MOSI (53.46, 73.29); and SCK (53.85, 72.14). It further covers 3V3 (51.10, 69.13) and MISO (54.00, 69.60), which W5 would cross if it touched down before A1. Both lie inside the strip extent, so the strip covers 11 non-GND vias (calc revision 4). The CR-top tips of pins 7-10 (pin 10 VCHG-IN, 0.940 mm proud, H.23(j)) get a cured dome of the BOM RTV or a Kapton patch before any lead is dressed (PM4 (6), T-F-12).

W1 and W2 keep a fixed build length of 0.30 m +- 10 mm at every placement (D-F3). A shorter W1/W2 lowers the lead inductance and raises the hard-short IN-side spike at U101 (H.5). **r8 (H.23(p)):** with the r8 W1/W2 wire of the table above (L' 0.399-0.661 uH/m from L' = (mu0/pi) acosh(s/2a) over the specified conductor, insulation OD and twist pitch) the IN peak at the lowest L' is 33.79 V at 290 mm, 33.64 V at 300 mm and 33.51 V at 310 mm, with a lead peak of up to 130 A; the margin to D107 VBR(min) 36 V is 2.21 V at 290 mm. The OUT-ring quarter period is <= 0.711 us, below the 1 us fast-trip response. The statement that no W1/W2 pair reaches 36 V holds only inside this modelled envelope (20 AWG 19/32 or 7/28, OD 1.60-1.75 mm, pitch 20-25 mm, 290-310 mm, the H.19(b) source grid); thin-wall PTFE at 290 mm would reach 38.23 V. The r3-r6 basis of H.5, H.19 and T-C-04 still holds. The r8 wire was not evaluated at a shortened route, so W1/W2 are never shortened (**superseded in r8:** on the unsourced 0.5 uH/m basis: cut to the 199.5 mm route, W1 gives 34.4 V; cut to the r7 rev-2 route of 181.6 mm, it gives 34.9 V, 1.1 V below D107 VBR(min) 36 V. At 290-300 mm the spike stays at 32.8-32.9 V, so the r3-r6 basis of H.5, H.19 and T-C-04 holds). The W1/W2 slack is a service loop anchored on the EVM plate. W3/W4, W6 and W7 keep the 0.30 m cap until MS2 and then take their route maxima; corridor fallbacks (ii) and (iii) still fail.

The route of W5 is a minimum-fit check, not a build maximum: route + a 20 mm 3-D allowance for the J101 rise and fold and the J201 drop (ASSUMPTION, T-A-06). The 0.30 m factory cable leaves 82.1 mm of slack at the reference placement and 100.2 mm in fallback (i). The slack is a service loop anchored on the EVM plate beside the EIB, and no slack lies over the CR. At 310 mm each, the W1/W2 pair has 20.65 mOhm (37.2 mV and 66.9 mW at 1.80 A), 0.66 mOhm above the H.11 figure at 0.30 m. At the 200 mm route maxima the W3/W4 pair has 8.38 mOhm (26.0 mV and 80.5 mW at 3.10 A; 26.9 mV and 86.3 mW at 3.21 A).

The USB corridor width is the Teensy 4.1 receptacle silkscreen outline from the MB `.brd`, not the plug overmold. The overmold width, thickness and length, the boot width and the bend direction are TODO(measure: MS2). W3/W4 use the 4.97 mm channel between the EVM right edge (x 88.50) and the corridor. W5 is routed around the channel over the EVM plate, so W3/W4 and W5 do not share it. The channel criterion is a clear width over y 118.04-138.73, between the EVM right edge with any clamp body and the measured plug envelope, of >= the measured W3/W4 pair OD + 1.0 mm (MS2). When it fails, corridor fallback (i) applies (A.7).

**r9-4 (2026-11-12, tap connector).** The ten tap conductors T1, T7b, T2, T5, T6, T10, T13, T16, T17 and T17r run through one Molex Micro-Fit 3.0 dual-row 2 x 5 header at 3.00 mm pitch, J-TAP. J-TAP is a through-hole part, soldered by hand as the last CR joint; its P/N is TODO(verify: Molex 43045 series), and its orientation (vertical or right-angle, from the placement) and its PCB pegs or locks are TODO(verify: Molex 43045 drawing). All ten cavities are used, with no spare. The mating cable is the Molex cable assembly 2147581101; its circuits, rows, single- or double-ended form, wire gauge, length and housing P/N are TODO(verify: Molex 2147581101 drawing). The housing polarization is required: a 180-degree flip would put the T6 wire on the T10 circuit. The A.8 cavity map assigns the cavities; A.8 also gives the adjacency rules, the adjacent-cavity short table, the open-lead table and the J-TAP placement rules. The assembly wires are discrete, so T1/T7b and T17/T17r are twisted by hand on the assembly. The assembly wire gauge must suit the R170 and R171 joints at C-D6 and C-D2 (T-A-05; TODO(verify: Molex 2147581101 wire gauge)). J-TAP is unplugged, with all supplies off, before the CR is lifted (D.1 PM6). Only T1 and T2 remain soldered on the MB. The tap review of 2026-11-12 removes thirteen taps: T3, T4, T8, T9, T11, T12, T14, T15, T18, T19, T20, T21 and the F24 option. Their rows in the table below are kept as history and marked removed.

**r7 dressing rule:** wires from tab X stay at y > 56 until x > 63. No tap wire passes over the REG-5V box (x 50.97-62.31, y 36.87-54.51: the LM1084 leads, body and tab), over CO-5V or over a CR header post (**superseded in r7:** "never pass over the LM1084 body", scoped to wires from tab X). The straight lines of T1 and T7b cross the REG-5V box (**superseded in r7:** "T1, T7b and T5"; T5 now sits at (58.42, 58.94) and its straight line clears the box). A tab X wire whose straight jacket crosses another pad, R175, the REG-5V box or CO-5V takes the **gap path**. The gap path leaves the pad into the adjacent inter-row gap (y 60.21, 62.75 or 65.29) and runs toward +x in that gap to x 64.77. x 64.77 lies half a pitch past column 6 and beyond the 64.50 mm courtyard edge; only there does the wire turn to its MB point (**superseded in r7:** "These three wires are dressed toward +y in the inter-row gaps, never across neighbouring pads"; the r7 dressed lengths were computed on a pad -> (63.50, pad y) path that ran over the row-1 pads). The gap y 60.21 carries 8 wires (T1, T7b, T4, T5, T12, T13, T16, T17r), the gap y 62.75 carries T6 and the gap y 65.29 carries 7 (T2, T11, T14, T15, T17, T21, F24). One 26 AWG jacket (OD ~1.0 mm, ASSUMPTION) fills a 1.04 mm gap, so the further wires of a gap stack above it; no stripped conductor extends past its own pad. The residual row is checked by the same rule. The straight T8 path from F09 to J2.31 crosses the REG-5V box and CO-5V and passes over the pin-1 post. T8 therefore takes the **upper lane** (calc revision 4): from F09 (28.98, 35.80) toward +y to (28.98, 37.55), along y 37.55 to x 43.43, down to (43.43, 34.64), along y 34.64 to x 63.50, then to J2.31 (89.2 mm dressed, 82.8 mm straight). The jacket (radius 0.5 mm, ASSUMPTION) keeps 0.50 mm from the F22 pad and lies inside the CR low edge (0 mm). It keeps 1.73 mm from the REG-5V box, 2.13 mm from CO-5V and 2.05 mm from the pin-1 post square (1.22 mm from its 1.9 mm CR pad land). It passes over the comparator band at y 37.55 over x 28.98-42.43, a wire over parts that is not booked as area, and it crosses the T18 option path. (**superseded in r7:** the review-7 **low-edge lane**, from F09 toward -y to y 34.40, 86.0 mm dressed; its jacket overhung the CR low edge by up to 0.24 mm and passed 0.15 mm below the F10 and F22 pads. A low-edge lane is infeasible by 0.59 mm: the jacket centre needs y >= 34.64 to stay on the CR and y <= 34.05 to keep 0.5 mm from the pads.) The straight T9 path clears the REG-5V box, CO-5V and every header post (r8-17, D-38: T22 removed). The tap wires are fitted after the FT1 bed has cured (PM4 order, A.7). T18 could not follow the dressing rule from tab X, so F22 sits on the footprint low row. Its straight path (10.54 mm) passes beside the pin-1 post, 0.240 mm from the post square, and crosses that post's 1.9 mm CR pad land; the wire is dressed over the CR top there. The F22 pad courtyard is 5.33 mm from the J101 box. The T18 joint at CO-5V pad 1 sits 0.172 mm (centreline end) from the REG-5V box, so F101 and R172 at that joint receive a temperature-derating check in T-A-05.

+-2 mm, `calc/r3_calc.py` H.22(i)): EVM right edge x = 1017 px; TP49 (970, 308), TP33 (941, 441), JP21 pin 2, the upper post (AGND), (902, 408) (r7: pin 1 is the lower square post; **superseded in r7:** JP21 pin 1 (902, 408)), JP14 pin 2
(869, 432), TP38 (822, 474), TP27 (490, 300), JP12 REGN pin (598, 862), TP36 (740, 812), JP17 /CE pin (727, 752) px (y down in the
render). **JP13/JP14/JP21** sit top-right in a row under the "ILIM_HIZ SET" legend, left of TP33 and above TP38; **JP17** ("CHARGE
ENABLE") is centre-bottom, directly above TP36 (/CE) and TP35 (TS). **Drawn placement:** the EIB pad column runs vertically 7 mm off

**r7 (vector EVM positions, H.23(k)):** the EVM points now come from the SLUUCB5E rev E vector layer figures (Figs 4-1 to 4-4), in the EVM frame of `round4/work/evm_geometry.md` Table 1 (mm, top view, origin at the lower-left board corner, +y up). If the clamp friction is exceeded, the lateral stops bound the motion at 0.3 mm (A.7). Both values are far below the smallest slack within a build maximum, 6.4 mm in plan for E8, so the loop areas and the pickup ratios above stay valid.

**r7: R276 (E1 damping, H.23(k)).** The EIB carries **R276 10.0 ohm 1 % 0603 (CRCW060310R0FKEA, the R273 MPN)** in series with E1 at the EIB E1 pad, between the E1 lead and the EIB REGN node (C205). Without R276, E1 with its E8 return and C205 (100 nF) is a series LC at 1.471 MHz (85 mm) or 1.430 MHz (90 mm), against the 1.5 MHz BQ25798 switching frequency (JP24/EM19). On the DC wire resistance the undamped Q is 19.3 (85 mm) and 19.1 (90 mm), or 25.5 and 25.6 with the E8 return at its 20 mm maximum. With the skin-effect resistance (Rac/Rdc 1.71 at 1.43 MHz) these fall to 13.1 and 13.0 (18.4 and 18.5). All are upper bounds, because the model omits the proximity effect and the frequency dependence of the C205 ESR. With R276 the Q is 0.108 (85 mm) and 0.111 (90 mm): the loop is overdamped (zeta 4.6 and 4.5). R276 with C205 is also a 159 kHz low-pass, so a 1.5 MHz REGN ripple reaches C205 at 0.106 of its EVM amplitude; T-C-16 checks the ring. E8 is the only DC ground of the EIB (A.6), so the E1 loop current returns through it. Without R276, the E8 drop at f0 is 20.0-31.4 mV per 10 mV of REGN ripple with a return of the E1 length, and up to 41.7 mV with the E8 return at its 20 mm maximum (E8 partial inductance 19.09 nH at its 20 mm maximum; `round4/calc/r7_calc.py` H.23(v), revision 5, on the H.23(k) loop; **superseded in r8:** 20-31 mV per 10 mV of REGN ripple (E8 partial inductance 19.1 nH at its 20 mm maximum; hand calculation on the H.23(k) loop)). That drop shifts EIB AGND, which carries the Q201 hold, against TP49 (r9-2: the U203/U204 REF nodes are DNP; **superseded in r9:** which carries the U203/U204 REF and the Q201 hold). It therefore draws on the E3 (75 mV) budget (r9-2: the E4 (48 mV) budget lapses with the E4 lead; **superseded in r9:** the E3 (75 mV) and E4 (48 mV) budgets) of `round4/work/eib_merge_failsafe.md` Table 8. With R276 the drop is 0.170-0.176 mV per 10 mV of ripple (H.23(v); **superseded in r8:** 0.17 mV). The static drop across R276 is 1.02 mV at the H.15 E1 load (0.102 mA, held, R254 only, REGN 4.8 V) and at most 3.96 mV (0.396 mA, released into the regen clamp, REGN 5.2 V). In the held states Q203 is off and Q201 sets the hold level, so the drop changes nothing. In the released states the drop lowers the ILIM_HIZ release level by at most 1.786 mV, which lowers IINDPM by at most 2.23 mA. This is the safe direction for the converter and the eFuse (less input current). For regen absorption (H.7) it is the adverse direction, but 2.23 mA is 0.13-0.17 % of the 1.33-1.76 A regen clamp, so no H.7 margin changes. The gate drives are unaffected at the mV level.

Parts fitted on the EVM itself (not on the EIB): **R256 200 kOhm and C252 2.2 nF C0G (0603) tacked between the JP21 header
posts, pin 1 (ILIM_HIZ) to pin 2 (AGND)** (r3, finding r256-c252-agnd-landing-unspecified: JP21 pin 2 is the AGND end of the
"ENABLE HIZ" shunt position, SLUUCB5E Fig 4-6, so the parts land on AGND and not on PGND, SLUUCB5E layout note 7); **R272
47.0 kOhm** from the /CE pad of the vacated R42 footprint to **TP27 (REGN)** with a <= 10 mm Kynar link L1, and **R272b
47.0 kOhm** from the **TP36 (/CE)** loop base to the **JP12 REGN pin** with its own <= 15 mm Kynar link L2 (r3, finding
ce-pullup-link-sense-divider-fails-low). The two pull-ups share no joint and no conductor, so /CE stays >= 4.17 V with either
one open (H.19); with both open, /CE floats (r9-2, 2026-11-12: R263 and U204 are DNP, so /CE has no defined pull, against the SLUSDV2C rule that /CE must be pulled HIGH or LOW; the fault is latent and only T-C-05 metering of R272 and R272b finds it; the drift direction is TODO(verify: SLUSDV2C IIN_BIAS_CE direction); **superseded in r9:** R263 pulls /CE LOW and U204 announces it) (B.6, J.1 item 13). R272b is deliberately not on the EIB: there it
would pull the EIB side of E6 up and make a lifted E6 read "/CE HIGH", masking a stuck-LOW /CE (r9-2: E6 is not fitted, so this reason is historical; R272b stays on the EVM unchanged). Identify every point by net with
a meter before soldering (T-A-02).

### A.6 Ground scheme (single-point bonding, r2)

- **Power star:** CR GND plane, tied to MB GND at CHG pads 4 (VIN-) and 14/15 (VBAT-). W4 returns between pads 14 and 15. **r6
  (finding a6-w2-not-beside-star-pads):** since r5, W2 sits at (27.7, 61.2), ~18.4 mm from pad 4 and ~8.0 mm from pad 14, so the
  input return reaches the star through the CR GND copper: a >= 2.5 mm L1 GND pour (2 oz) runs from W2 to pads 14/15, routed
  outside the H1/UVB/CHG divider bottoms and the R105/IMON ground end (so the 1.76 A input return does not pass under an analog
  return), with the L2 plane below it; T-A-06 checks this copper. On 2 oz copper the extra ~8 mm adds < 1 mOhm (no budget change). (r9-5: the W2 and pad positions are re-placed on the plug-on outline and the CR outer copper is 1 oz (D-29); the W2-to-star resistance is TODO(calc: generator step), and T-A-06 checks this copper.)
  The BQ25798EVM joins PGND and AGND at net-tie NT1 (SLUUCB5E Fig 4-5, next to C41/AGND) and senses current high-side only (R2,
  R13 and internal RSNS; study §1.1 H1), so VIN- = VBAT- is the requirement R-GND and is met. The pack negative is PCB ground
  by design (operator, 2026-11-04).
- **Logic return:** the CR plane itself, bonded to MB GND at CHG pads 4/14/15 (T7 omitted in r2). The divider bottoms of H1 and
  UVB are on the CR plane. T7b and T17r are shields bonded at the CR end only, so no tap wire carries motor or charger return
  current. A plane offset delta shifts the H1
  trip by only about 0.07 x delta (both inputs see it), so 10 mV costs 0.7 mV.
- **Kelvin for BT_OK (withdrawn in r9-1, 2026-11-12: U104, T8, T9, R140-R144 and C140 are removed, so the CR has no Kelvin tap; history):** the INA253 BT output is 6-34 mV at the threshold, so a few mV of offset matters. The INA253 output is
  referenced to its own GND/REF1/REF2 pins at SNS-BT (`.sch` net GND includes SNS-BT.GND, .REF1, .REF2). The U104 reference
  divider bottom (R142) therefore returns to the **T9 wire landed on the SNS-BT GND/REF1 pad**, twisted with T8. R143 (100
  ohm) ties R142's bottom to the CR plane, so an open T9 shifts the trip only to about 22 mV instead of floating it; with T9
  intact the plane offset couples with a ratio of about 2e-4. T-E-10 measures the residual offset under load.
- **EIB and EVM: one DC ground each, no parallel return (r2).** The EIB's DC ground is E8 at TP49 (EVM AGND). The four ribbon
  GND conductors (3, 9, 12, 14; position 6 is the key, r3; 9/10 swapped in r4) are bonded to the CR plane at J101 and reach EIB AGND only through R273 10 ohm: the EIB
  supply and signal returns (<= ~1 mA, H.15) drop <= 10 mV across it, while the share of the 1.4-1.6 A net EVM ground current
  that would otherwise cross the EVM AGND copper, E8 and the ribbon (finding estimate 0.1-0.3 A through 25-40 mOhm) falls below
  ~2 mA (10 ohm against W2 || W4 ~4 mOhm). W7's GND conductor is bonded at the CR end only (J8 pin 1 empty) and W6's likewise, so
  I2C and TS reference the EVM through the power returns: offset <= ~20 mV at 3.1 A (H.11), against the BQ25798 0.4 V VIL margin
  and the TS divider ratio. TI asks that ILIM and TS ground terminals stay away from high-current returns (SLUUCB5E layout note
  7); R256/C252 sit across the JP21 posts (ILIM_HIZ to AGND, r3), away from PGND. **T-F-11** measures the residual signal-ground currents (pass < 20 mA
  DC in any signal-ground conductor, < 2 mV AGND-PGND).
- **Analog taps referenced to the CR plane (r5, finding imon-vchg-ground-offset-under-charge-current):** the eFuse IMON voltage
  (R105 to the CR plane, T17r bonded at the CR end) and the CHG_VOLTAGE divider are read by the Teensy against its own AGND. The
  CR plane is bonded to MB GND at CHG pads 4/14/15, which carry the charger input return (<= 1.76 A) and the net EVM ground
  current (~1.5 A), so any MB-GND drop between those pads and the Teensy AGND appears directly on pin 22 at 1.31 A per volt
  (5 mV = 6.5 mA, 15 mV = 19.6 mA, i.e. 13-40 % of the provisional +-50 mA FR-11 band; H.21) and on pin 38 at x8.87. **T-F-15**
  measures the offset on the vehicle under charge current; FR-11 carries the measured offset in its threshold; if it exceeds
  10 mV at 1.7 A input, the fallback is a Kelvin IMON return: R105's ground end lifted off the plane and returned through T17r
  landed at the Teensy AGND end (instead of the CR end) with a 100 ohm tie to the CR plane, as T9/R143 did for BT_OK in r8 (r9-1: T9 and R143 are removed; the fallback keeps its own 100 ohm tie).
- **r9-5 (plug-on outline; the topology is unchanged):** the CR L2 GND plane and the L4 solid GND layer cover the whole outline and bond to MB GND only at CHG pads 4/14/15, now through the mated SSQ/TSW contacts. No standoff, foot or fastener joins the CR to the MB; the friction of the 22 contacts holds the CR. L4 faces the MB under its solder mask across an air gap of >= 1.5 mm (A.7), so the untented MB via rings (H.23(c2)) touch no CR copper; no polyimide sheet is fitted. The insulating EVM plate, the W2/W4 returns and the E8/R273 paths are unchanged, so the single-point scheme above holds as written.
- (**superseded in r9-5:** **r7 (tabs, feet and the EVM plate; the topology is unchanged):** the CR L2 GND plane continues without a break into tab X and tab Y. Every tab-side pad, part and bottom passive therefore returns to the same plane, which still bonds to MB GND only at CHG pads 4/14/15. The far-end feet FT1 and FT2 are non-conductive (PA66 or PBT blocks on neutral-cure RTV beds) and add no ground contact between the CR and the MB. The MB vias are not tented (H.23(c2)); the polyimide sheet and the L4 solder mask keep the tab undersides off the exposed via rings. The EVM plate is insulating, and no fastener, clamp or adhesive bonds EVM copper to the plate, the CR or the chassis (checked in T-A-02). The single-point scheme above therefore holds as written: the EVM ground reaches the CR only through W2 and W4, and the EIB ground reaches the EVM only through E8 at TP49 and the CR only through R273.)

### A.7 Mechanical

- **r9-5 plug-on outline and mounting (2026-11-12; operator decisions, `hardware/charger_evm_r8/DESIGN_STATE_2026-11-12.md` Table 1, `hardware/charger_evm_r8/OUTLINE_CHANGE_REASSESSMENT_2026-11-12.md`).** The CR is a removable plug-on board. Its outline is the rectangle x 18.584-67, y 7-94 in the MB frame (48.416 x 87 mm, 4212 mm²), with no tab, no chamfer, no concave corner and no hole other than the plated holes of the netlist. The bullets of this section from "r7 outline" to "Feet effect and the fitting decision" describe the r7 outline and are history (each marked superseded in r9-5), except where a bullet carries its own r9-5 statement (outline freeze, pin identity, MB vias, area). The EVM, EIB and USB-corridor bullets at the end of the section stay live.
- **Mating connector (r9-5, `hardware/charger_evm_r8/decisions_2026-11-12/cr_decision_mating_connector_2026-11-12.md`).** The MB carries Samtec SSQ-110-01-L-S in the x 45.998 column (pins 1-10) and SSQ-112-01-L-S in the x 20.998 column (pins 11-22). Each socket body (insulator 8.51 mm) sits on the MB top, and its square tail (2.64 mm) passes through the MB, with a 1.04 mm protrusion at a 1.6 mm MB (ASSUMPTION, TODO(measure: MS6)). The CR carries TSW-110-07-L-S and TSW-112-07-L-S with their 2.54 mm bodies on the CR underside. Post C (5.84 mm) points down into the sockets, and tail B (2.54 mm) passes up through the CR, with a 0.94 mm protrusion above a 1.6 mm CR. Both parts use standard-force contacts (-01) and plating -L (10 uin Au on the mating surfaces, matte Sn tails). All 22 positions are populated; the 11 NC positions add retention and alignment. With the sockets on the MB, the live MB contacts stay touch-safe while the CR is removed.
- **Stack (r9-5).** The stack has a hard stop where each TSW body seats on its SSQ face. The CR underside therefore stands 8.51 + 2.54 = 11.05 mm above the MB top, and the CR top 12.65 mm (CR 1.6 mm). The insertion depth is 5.84 mm, inside the SSQ range of 3.68-6.35 mm. The CR mass and the cable loads rest on the connector insulators, not on the joints. TSW mated with SSQ is rated 6.3 A per pin with two positions powered (Samtec F-226 current table); the 4-of-6 powered case at pins 14/15/18/19 (1.93 A each) is TODO(verify: Samtec derating curve). The SSQ is rated for 100 mating cycles.
- **Key (r9-5).** The CR has no mechanical key (operator ruling). A CR rotated by 180 degrees about the CHG centre (33.498, 50.514) lands over J-BL, J-FC and J-BT (21.70 mm tall). Its pins begin to engage at 11.05 + 5.84 = 16.89 mm, 4.81 mm below the block tops, so the blocks stop the rotated CR before any contact. **Rule:** the engagement-start height (seated underside plus post insertion) stays below 21.70 mm; a taller stack needs a real key. The pin-1 silkscreen arrow and the `calc/pin_identity_check.py` capture gate (D-02, T-A-06 step 0) stay.
- **Standoffs (r9-5).** No standoff is fitted in this revision. The friction fit of the 22 contacts holds the CR (operator ruling, `hardware/charger_evm_r8/decisions_2026-11-12/dec_standoffs_2026-11-12.md`). A later support, for example a 3-D printed one, is outside the scope of this revision; the re-run site search of that record is kept for it.
- **Assembly sequence (r9-5; PM4).** The SSQ sockets are soldered to the MB first, with the bodies flat and square. The TSW strips are then plugged into the sockets, and the finished (reflowed) CR is set on the TSW bodies. The TSW tails are soldered from the CR top while the strips are plugged, so the strips align to the real MB holes at the true height. The CR is then unplugged and inspected. The MB underside at both CHG columns is clear and reachable with an iron (operator).
- **Air gap and MB parts under the CR (r9-5).** The outline covers 67 MB parts (59 fully, 8 partly) plus the CHG footprint, among them L-FC and L-BT (5.0 mm, TODO(verify: Eaton HCM1A1305V3; the HCM1A1307V3 sibling is 6.5 mm), MS3 caliper), REG-5V (4.83 mm), REG-FC, REG-BT and both boost switching nodes. **Rule:** an air gap of >= 1.5 mm separates the lowest CR feature, THT tails included, from the tallest MB part below it. Over L-FC and L-BT the stack gives 11.05 - 5.0 = 6.05 mm, less any CR underside feature. The gap basis counts the CR bow only (IPC-6012 0.75 % of 87 mm, about 0.65 mm, TODO(verify: IPC-6012 class figure)), not the MB bow or the connector seating tolerance. Every CR underside tail (TSW, W1-W4, the tap connector) stays outside the L-FC, L-BT and REG-5V shadows + 1 mm. The bodge-part heights under the outline are TODO(measure: operator, MS3).
- **No bottom-side SMT (r9-5).** All SMT parts are on the CR top (parts and assembly decision of 2026-11-12). The CR underside carries only the TSW bodies, the THT tails and the L4 GND under solder mask. The bottom clearance rule, the bottom keep-out, the polyimide sheet, the feet FT1/FT2 and the FT2 fill hole therefore retire.
- **MB vias (r9-5).** The 368 MB vias stay untented (H.23(c2)). No insulating film covers them, because the operator retired the polyimide sheet entirely. The air gap and the solder-masked L4 GND face of the CR are their only cover.
- **Heat under the CR (r9-5).** REG-5V (0.40 / 0.63 / 1.08 W), the FC boost (1.17-2.20 W at 14.6 W input; eta 0.85 is a model value, TODO(verify: TPS61288 Fig 7-3)) and the BT boost (TODO(calc: BT channel operating point)) lie under the CR. The sensitive-part window and keep-outs of A.8 replace the tab X thermal band.

- (**Superseded in r9-5; history.**) **Foot construction and bedding (r7).** Each foot is a PA66 or PBT block of height h_f = 2.54 mm - t_bed - t_bond = 2.19 mm
  at t_bed 0.30 mm and t_bond 0.05 mm (block tolerance +0/-0.05 mm). The CR-side bond is a 0.05 mm acrylic transfer tape
  (TODO(verify: tape datasheet, temperature rating)). (**superseded in r7:** h_f = 2.54 mm - t_bed = 2.24 mm with an RTV bond
  of unstated thickness, cured before seating.) The header bodies and the feet both stand on the sheet, so t_bed does not
  depend on the MB, CR or sheet thickness. The tape bonds each foot before seating, the header bodies set the CR height, and
  no wet adhesive is present while the 22 MB joints are soldered.

  The tolerance budget of t_bed (H.23(i)) has four contributors: the header body +-0.13 mm (TODO(verify: Samtec TSW
  drawing)), the CR local bow (IPC-6012 0.75 % of the lever: +-0.118 mm at FT1, +-0.066 mm at FT2), the block
  +0/-0.05 mm and the tape 0-0.05 mm. The nominal bed is 0.300 mm and the mean is 0.350 mm. The worst case is
  0.052-0.648 mm at FT1 and 0.104-0.596 mm at FT2; the RSS bands are 0.171-0.529 mm and 0.200-0.500 mm. The worst case
  therefore falls outside the 0.15-0.45 mm bed range on both sides. A foot that is too tall becomes a hard prop and
  preloads the joints; a foot that is too short leaves a bed thicker than the stiffness range of H.23(i).

  The measured gate PM4 (2d) dry-seats the CR on the sheet after the feet are taped and before the 22 joints are
  soldered. A 0.05 mm feeler must not enter under any header body; at each foot a 0.15 mm feeler must enter and a
  0.45 mm feeler must not. A Monte-Carlo estimate with uniform contributors (ORDER OF MAGNITUDE) passes 79.7 % of FT1
  builds (2.2 % too tall, 18.1 % too short) and 85.8 % of FT2 builds (0.2 % and 14.0 %). A rejected foot is re-made.
  The 0.15-0.45 mm bed range is therefore a gated range, and "the feet take no preload" holds for a build that passes (2d).

  As the placement aid, the CR bottom silkscreen carries the outline of each foot body, a long-axis tick on FT1 (long axis
  along x) and a ring around the FT2 fill hole (A.8). FT2 is square, so the outline also sets its orientation. A pin of
  0.9-1.0 mm through the CR fill hole and the foot hole locates FT2. PM4 (2c) measures the three edge distances that the
  A.7 placement tolerance bounds (FT1 0.294 / 0.304 mm, FT2 0.250 mm).

  After the 22 MB joints are soldered and inspected, a flowable alkoxy-cure silicone RTV bed fills the gap between each foot
  and the polyimide sheet (nominal 0.30 mm, gated 0.15-0.45 mm). FT1 is bedded with a syringe through its lane at the tab X top edge, before the W1-W4 leads are dressed and before W5-W7 and the
  tap wires are fitted (PM4 order: W1-W4 joints in step (2b) before seating, the feet taped (2c) and gap-checked dry (2d), 22 MB joints, inspection, FT1/FT2 beds, cure, T-A-09, then the W1-W4 dressing, W5-W7 and the taps). The +y side of FT2
  lies behind the L-FC body, so FT2 is bedded through a 1.0 mm NPTH fill hole at the foot centre (28.00, 73.250). The hole
  passes through tab Y and the foot. The RTV is injected from the CR top with a 21-22 G blunt needle (OD <= 0.82 mm) seated
  in the CR hole, until it appears at the FT2 -y, -x and +x faces; that witness, sighted from under the tab, is the FT2 fill
  inspection (the +y face lies behind L-FC). FT1 is complete when RTV shows along its -y and +x faces, sighted from the
  tab X tip. The hole lies 1.500 mm inside the foot body edge, and the CR top
  keeps a 2.0 mm copper and part keep-out disc around it (0.5 mm ring, 1.750 mm inside the r7 outline, booked in H.23(e)).
  L2-L4 keep a >= 0.5 mm copper pull-back around the hole (L2 solid GND, L4 GND pour). Under
  the hole the MB carries GND pour under solder mask (nearest non-GND rim 7.18 mm, via pad 9.89 mm, part box 3.26 mm from the
  hole edge). Each bed cures for the RTV datasheet through-cure time of a 2.0 mm path from an open edge (the FT2 centre), and
  for at least 24 h, before the T-A-09 bond check (**superseded in r7:** >= 24 h alone). The beds use the flowable
  alkoxy-cure RTV of E only. Acetoxy-cure and oxime-cure RTV are excluded (acetic acid and 2-butanone oxime attack copper),
  and a non-flowing paste is excluded (it does not wick into the gap).
  TODO(verify: RTV datasheet: alkoxy cure, copper corrosivity, viscosity, deep-section cure rate, temperature rating,
  adhesion to polyimide without primer).
- (**Superseded in r9-5; history.**) **Foot removal and bond fallback (r7; r8 re-made foot and repair access, H.23(r)).** The polyimide sheet is the sacrificial
  layer: removal means cutting the bed and peeling the sheet, and in the baseline the MB solder mask is never bonded. The bond
  of the bed RTV to polyimide is qualified before the CR is soldered, by the T-A-09 step 0 bond coupon (r8). If the coupon
  fails, the sheet gets a cut-out within the foot keep-out coordinates (FT1 x 59.220-64.220, y 65.405-68.005; FT2
  x 25.500-30.500, y 70.750-75.750), never sized to an as-found foot, and the bed bonds to the MB solder mask. The FT1 cut-out
  is no larger than its 5.0 x 2.6 mm keep-out: it exposes no non-GND copper rim and no via pad, and the sheet still covers the
  MPPT-DISABLE trace by 0.794 mm (H.23(i)). The FT2 cut-out is its 5.0 x 5.0 mm keep-out over GND pour only.

  The cut-out removes the sheet stack, film and PSA, under that foot, while the header bodies keep their seat on the sheet.
  An unchanged foot would then leave a bed of 0.275-0.575 mm and a bed stiffness down to x0.783 of the gated minimum (FT1
  11.13 against 14.22 N/mm, FT2 27.83 against 35.56 N/mm at E 1 MPa; H.23(r)). The foot is therefore re-made at
  h_f' = h_f + t_rm, where t_rm is the measured thickness of the removed stack, film and PSA together, read to +-0.01 mm:
  2.315, 2.340 and 2.365 mm at t_rm 0.125, 0.150 and 0.175 mm (block tolerance +0/-0.05 mm, H.23(r)). The sheet is 0.125 mm
  of polyimide film plus a silicone PSA whose thickness is not stated (TODO(verify: polyimide tape datasheet)); the fallback
  uses the measured t_rm, never a nominal figure. The PM4 (2d) feeler gate is repeated with the re-made foot (pass estimate
  79.7 % at FT1 and 85.8 % at FT2, ORDER OF MAGNITUDE, H.23(r)). A sheet that lifts from the MB mask in T-A-09 is a PSA
  failure, not an RTV failure: the sheet is re-pressed and T-A-09 repeated before this fallback.

  **Repair access after soldering (r8, H.23(r)).** After the 22 MB joints are soldered, the sheet under a foot cannot be
  removed without lifting the CR. At FT2 the +y face lies 0.75 mm from the tab Y +y edge and 1.612 mm in plan from the L-FC
  body (5.0 mm tall, ASSUMPTION), so no tool and no new foot pass on that side; the slot under the CR is 2.540 mm high, and
  the -x face lies 8.30 mm from the tab Y -x edge, under tab Y (r9-3: no SMT part on the tab Y bottom; **superseded in r9:**
  under the tab Y bottom parts (height cap 1.0 mm)). The cut-out fallback is
  therefore executable only before the 22 joints are soldered. After soldering, a failed bed is re-bedded by RTV injection
  only, FT2 through its fill hole and FT1 through its lane at the tab X top edge. A bond to polyimide that fails after
  soldering needs the CR desoldered (22 joints) before the cut-out fallback.
