  peeling the sheet, and in the baseline the MB solder mask is never bonded. If the T-A-09 bond check fails on polyimide, the
  sheet gets a cut-out within the foot keep-out coordinates (FT1 x 59.220-64.220, y 65.405-68.005; FT2 x 25.500-30.500,
  y 70.750-75.750), never sized to an as-found foot, and the bed bonds to the MB solder mask. A sheet that lifts from the MB
  mask in T-A-09 is a PSA failure, not an RTV failure: the sheet is re-pressed and T-A-09 repeated before this fallback. The FT1 cut-out is no larger than its 5.0 x
  2.6 mm keep-out: it exposes no non-GND copper rim and no via pad, and the sheet still covers the MPPT-DISABLE trace by
  0.794 mm (H.23(i)). The FT2 cut-out is its 5.0 x 5.0 mm keep-out over GND pour only.)
- (**Superseded in r9-5:** no tabs and no feet; the plug-on CR modes and contact loads are TODO(calc: generator step), T-F-18.) **Tab stiffness and pin loads (r7, H.23(i); ORDER OF MAGNITUDE).** These figures assume a 20 GPa laminate, a clamped root and
  an RTV modulus of 1-3 MPa (ASSUMPTION, TODO(verify: RTV datasheet)); MS5, MS6 and T-F-18 decide. The unpropped resonance
  figures are upper estimates (clamped root). For tab Y the clamp along the pin-11 row y 64.484 is held by pin 11 alone within
  the tab width, so the tab Y figures are the least conservative. Tab X has a tip stiffness of 35.8 N/mm and 63.2 N/mm at the
  foot, against an RTV bed of 14-128 N/mm; its first mode is 1664-2353 Hz unpropped. Tab Y has 266.3 / 603.8 N/mm against a
  bed of 36-320 N/mm; its first mode is 4531-6407 Hz unpropped. The propped first modes are neither upper nor lower bounds.
  With k_s = E A / t (t_bed 0.30 mm) they are 1924-3336 Hz (tab X) and 4726-7204 Hz (tab Y). The bonded-thin-layer (Gent)
  factor 1 + 2S^2 raises k_s up to x8 at FT1 (S 1.90) and x23 at FT2 (S 3.33); with it the propped first modes are
  3235-7190 Hz (tab X) and 7905-17112 Hz (tab Y). (**superseded in r7:** "every resonance figure is an upper estimate".)
  The MS5 comparison uses the lowest unpropped figure, tab X 1664 Hz. The worst header-pin load at 30 g is 0.208-0.322 N
  without the feet and 0.168-0.297 N with them (r6 CR alone 0.067-0.134 N). The with-feet pin loads are upper estimates on
  the bed axis, because a stiffer (confined) bed unloads the pins. A 10 N push at the tab X tip loads the worst pin with
  2.69 N without FT1 and 0.52-1.99 N with it. At the tab Y tip (28.00, 76.00) the figures are 3.05 N and 1.63-2.82 N
  (**superseded in r7:** 3.06 N and 1.64-2.83 N).
- (**Superseded in r9-5; history.**) **Feet effect and the fitting decision (r7, H.23(i); ORDER OF MAGNITUDE, bed confinement not modelled).** The feet are
  fitted by default by operator ruling. Their effect on the distributed load is small: at 30 g they cut the worst-pin load
  by 7-21 %. Their effect on a tip push is larger. FT1 takes 2.41-8.79 N of a 10 N tab X tip push and cuts the worst-pin
  load by 26-81 %. FT1 also props the softer tab (35.8 N/mm), whose unpropped first mode 1664-2353 Hz lies inside the MS5
  band of 0.1-8 kHz. FT2 takes 0.82-5.09 N of a 10 N tab Y tip push and cuts the worst-pin load by 7-47 %. Tab Y is stiff
  (266.3 N/mm, unpropped first mode 4531-6407 Hz). FT2 is therefore kept as a margin against handling loads at the tab Y
  far edge until MS5 and T-F-18 report. When the MS5 spectrum shows no MB excitation above the logger noise floor within
  2.3-8 kHz (0.5-2 times the tab Y unpropped band, clipped at 8 kHz), FT2 may be omitted by operator ruling. Its
  footprint, keep-out and fill hole then stay on the CR.

  5 mm above the level of TP33 (r6 placement, A.5, A.9). W3/W4 enter EVM J5 below the EIB; the dry fit (T-A-06) confirms >= 3 mm
  between the EIB and the J5 wire entry, else the EIB moves up to 5 mm higher (E8 and E3 stay within their maxima).
- **EVM mount (r7).** The BQ25798EVM has no mounting holes: the corner circles are fiducials (SLUUCB5E Figs 4-1 to 4-4; BOM
  FID1-FID6; `round4/work/evm_geometry.md` section 3), and a hole drilled at a bumpon centre would cut the ground pour and 7-17
  stitching vias. The **EVM plate** is an insulating plate, fixed to the chassis, that carries the EVM and the EIB. The stock
  bumpons H1-H4 (3M SJ-5303, 11.18 mm diameter, 5.08 mm tall) stay fitted and rest on the plate. Two nylon clamp bars, or four
  corner L-clamps, with 0.5 mm silicone pads press edge lips of <= 2.0 mm; the clamps are notched at J8 and stay clear of
  TP48/TP49, the terminal wire faces and the fiducials. No fastener or adhesive bonds EVM copper to the plate, the CR or the
  chassis, and the EVM is not drilled. Positive lateral stops (edge fences, locating pins or the clamp lips) sit at the
  EVM board edges with at most 0.3 mm of play per axis, clear of FID1-FID6, the terminal wire faces and J8. The clamp
  preload holds the EVM by friction against the MS5 peak acceleration times the MS7 mass; the stops bound the motion if
  the friction is exceeded or the pads relax. The preload is limited so that each bumpon compresses by no more than
  1.0 mm. This keeps the 2.4 mm terminal tails at least 1 mm off the plate (2.68 mm nominal; MS7 confirms the tail
  protrusion and the board thickness). Plate, clamp and stop geometry: TODO(design: from MS2, MS5 and MS7). J2 stays removed (EM7), and
  W1-W7 stay cable-tied to the chassis at 0.10 m intervals. T-A-02 checks the clamp fit, the stop play, the bumpon
  compression and the insulation of the EVM copper (TP49, J1 pin 1) to the plate and the chassis (> 1 MOhm with W1-W7
  disconnected). T-F-18b repeats these checks after the vehicle run.
- **EIB mount (r7).** The two M3 x 10 mm nylon standoffs stand on the EVM plate, so the EVM and the EIB share one mounting
  plate. The EVM is held by friction on compliant bumpons, so the E leads see a small relative motion (0.03-0.12 mm at
  30 g, ASSUMED materials; at most the 0.3 mm stop play; A.5). Each E lead keeps at least 3 mm of slack within its A.5
  build maximum and is tacked to the EIB with an RTV dot within 10 mm of its pad. T-F-18b inspects the E-lead joints
  after the vehicle run. The r6 placement rule (pad column 7 mm off the EVM right edge, E3 5 mm above TP33) is
  unchanged. At the reference placement the EIB bottom edge lies 4.84 mm from the J5 body top (>= 3 mm, H.23(l)). The E-lead
  build maxima follow A.5 (E1 90 mm, E5 65 mm; H.23(k)).

### A.8 CR layout constraints (for the KiCad capture, PM0)

**r9-5 (2026-11-12, plug-on outline; `hardware/charger_evm_r8/decisions_2026-11-12/stackup_fabrules_decisions_2026-11-12.md`).** The hole table and the pin identity below are unchanged. The following rules govern the capture on the plug-on outline:

- **Outline:** x 18.584-67, y 7-94 (A.7); courtyards >= 0.5 mm from it; a 0.40 mm router copper keep-out band inside it (fab copper to edge 0.381 mm).
- **Fab rules:** an OSH Park-only rule file: annular ring 0.1016 mm, via diameter >= 0.4572 mm, hole >= 0.254 mm, hole-to-hole 0.127 mm (OSH Park recommendation, no OSH Park minimum), copper to edge 0.381 mm, plated hole to inner copper 0.254 mm, mask web 0.1016 mm. The PCBWay minima no longer apply, so a PCBWay order needs a re-check. The only via is 0.6/0.3 mm. Track and clearance: rule minimum 0.127 mm, router net-class default 0.1524 / 0.1524 mm, and 0.127 mm only at local necks (for example the J1 and CHG pin gaps). Unused inner pads are removed on every through-hole pad; a pad stays on any layer where it connects, zone ties included. Whether OSH Park needs non-functional pads on connector holes for barrel anchoring under repeated mating is TODO(verify: OSH Park). The silkscreen text size is TODO(design owner: the 0.8 / 0.15 mm house rule against the OSH Park minimum).
- **Vias in pads (D-37, D-36):** the routing first uses no via on an SMD pad or in its mask opening. Plain unfilled vias in SMD pads are used only if that attempt fails, and each such via is listed for operator review. Filled and capped vias are excluded. The U101 exposed-pad thermal vias are exempt (U101 thermal pad bullet below).
- **Assembly:** the r9-3 assembly rule below (stencil, solder paste and reflow oven, all SMT parts on the top side) with passives 0402 minimum and 0603 preferred (r9-3 / D-44: no 0402 part remains; every chip passive is 0603 or larger), IC pitch 0.65 mm preferred minimum and U101 (TPS26630RGER, VQFN-24, 0.5 mm) the one approved 0.5 mm exception; through-hole parts are hand-soldered after the reflow.
- **Stack-up and copper:** the Stack-up (r9-5) and Copper bullets below.
- **Sensitive-part window:** the 0.1 % dividers, the comparator inputs and the references sit preferably in y 30.8-66.86, >= 10 mm in plan from the REG-5V body and 5V pour rim, >= 5 mm from the L, REG and VSW boxes of both boosts, >= 2 mm from SNS-FC and SNS-BT and >= 5 mm from U101, with each divider pair adjacent and aligned (`hardware/charger_evm_r8/outline_change_2026-11-12/mbparts.md` section 2.3). The window is a preference, not a gate: a part placed outside it carries a listed exemption. The free area of 1783.6 mm² is an upper bound, because the U101 keep-out is not subtracted.
- **Shadow zones:** L-FC, L-BT, the two VSW pours, REG-FC, REG-BT and REG-5V with its 5V pour, each grown by 3 mm. They no longer constrain routing, because L4 is solid GND everywhere, but they bound the THT-tail positions (A.7).
- **Regions:** the pad coordinates (W1-W4, W6/W7, U101, J101), the per-region table and the area bookings below are r5/r7 placement targets on the old outline. Their electrical distance rules stay binding. The region table and the coordinates on the plug-on outline are TODO(generator step: `gen/layout_cr.py` region table, side flags and power geometry). **r9-4 J-TAP cavity map (2026-11-12, operator decision; accepted conditional on the permit-gate decisions, which are taken).** Columns 1 to 5 run along the header; rows A and B. A cavity is named by its row and column (J-TAP A1 to B5). The physical pin numbers are TODO(verify: Molex 43045 header and 43025 housing drawings) at layout time. Table A.8-T1 gives the map.

| Row | Col 1 | Col 2 | Col 3 | Col 4 | Col 5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | T1 | T7b | T17r | T5 | T13 |
| B | T6 | T2 | T17 | T16 | T10 |

The map meets these rules, where adjacency includes the opposite-row cavity:

- T5, T6 and T10 are pairwise non-adjacent (permit-gate decision 5). A T5-T6 short defeats the FCC_ON AND NOT FCC_OFF agreement term, a T10-T6 short holds QUAL HIGH, and a T5-T10 short ties two push-pull outputs onto one EN net.
- T1 and T2 are not beside T5 or T10, so a 10 kOhm V-MOT or VBUS feed cannot lift a high-Z EN or QUAL pin at an MCU reset.
- T1/T7b and T17/T17r occupy adjacent cavities (the twisted pairs).
- The housing polarization excludes a 180-degree flip, which would put the T6 wire on the T10 circuit.

The permit-gate decision recommends that T5, T6 and T10 are also not diagonal to each other. T5 (A4) is diagonal to T10 (B5), so the recommendation is not met. The map is not changed; the diagonal is an open item for operator confirmation (J.2 item 63). A search of all 1664 feasible 2 x 5 maps (mirror images counted once) found none with fewer than two severity-2 pairs, and in every one T13 separates T5 from T10 (`hardware/charger_evm_r8/decisions_2026-11-12/round2/tap_connector/order.py`, `enum25.py`). Empty cavities guard better than GND cavities. R175 sits at the CR end, so T6 beside GND would short the Teensy 3V3 with no limiting resistor, and T17 beside GND would pass proof (d) falsely. A 2 x 6 housing with GND guards scores no better than the adopted 2 x 5 map. The r7 tab X assignment, its six exclusions and the H.23(g) check that follow are history only.

**r9-4 J-TAP placement rules (design owner).** The layout meets these rules:

- J-TAP sits on the +x side of the CR, because every far end lies at +x (J1, J2, C-D2, C-D6).
- The T2 run to C-D2 (body x 67.42-69.74 at y 69.9) is kept short.
- Each run stays inside its A.4 maximum: T1 0.15 m to C-D6 at (97.8, 17.9), T2 0.10 m, J1 taps 0.12 m and J2 taps 0.15 m; the lengths are TODO(calc: H.23(g) successor).
- Finger access to the latch is kept free.
- The J-TAP THT tails are counted in the 11.05 mm CR-to-MB bottom clearance, TODO(calc).
- The T16 header-pin tail is the only exposed copper of `CHG_EFUSE_FLT` (the R106s rules below).

(**Superseded in r9-4; history only.**) The assignment minimises the straight-length sum under six adjacency exclusions:

- no two of T3, T4 and T5 (the RT1987 EN taps) on orthogonally adjacent positions;
- F07 (T6, the raw Teensy 3V3) beside R175, with no GND (T7b, T17r) and no EN (T3, T4, T5) neighbour;
- T10 (`CHG_QUAL`) not beside T21 (`CHG_HB`);
- T1 and T2 (the V-MOT and VBUS divider taps) not beside a raw Teensy-pin pad;
- T1/T7b and T17/T17r on adjacent positions;
- T18 off tab X.

has R175a and F12 (T11). R175a is the Teensy 3V3 supply node (J1.29), not a GPIO, so the T2 exclusion holds; the F03-R175a row of
the short table below gives the back-feed. F20 (T20) and F21 (T21) lie over the FT1 body (A.4). The pad envelope is x 50.050-64.250, y 58.190-67.310 (courtyard
x 49.800-64.500, y 57.940-67.560; margins to the outline: right 0.500, top 0.740, low 1.640 mm), and the low pad edge lies
2.233 mm from the MB 5V copper rim (rule >= 2.0 mm). F22 (T18) at (41.68, 35.80) runs 10.54 mm straight to CO-5V pad 1, beside
(not over) the pin-1 post (0.240 mm from the post square), and its pad courtyard lies 5.33 mm from the J101 region.

**r9-4 J-TAP adjacent-cavity short table.** A bridge at the hand-soldered header tails, a stray strand or a contact bent against its neighbour shorts two conductors; a crimp in the wrong cavity puts its conductor on the neighbour's circuit. The 2 x 5 map has 13 orthogonal pairs, and Table A.8-T2 lists them. The contention figures take about 40 ohm per i.MX output driver (ASSUMPTION, as in the r7 table). The severity weights are a design judgement: 1 = announces itself, 2 = reset-time or readback hazard, 3 = silently masks a protection. The T-F-12 cavity check detects every pair before the first power-up; the last column names the detector in service.

| Pair (cavities) | Consequence of a short | Detector in service |
|---|---|---|
| T1-T7b (A1-A2) | R170 carries <= 2.0 mA; H1 IN+ reads 0 V; no regen release (safe) | H1 state against V-MOT (T-C-02) |
| T7b-T17r (A2-A3) | GND to GND; none | - |
| T17r-T5 (A3-A4) | pin 31 HIGH sinks into GND (about 80 mA of driver contention); the FC_CHARGE EN net is held LOW; no FC window opens (safe) | the FC window does not open (V_chg, `CHG_IIN`) |
| **T5-T13 (A4-A5), severity 2** | In normal operation pin 34 reads the pin-31 level and U102 contends through R126 (<= 3.3 mA). During an MCU reset (pin 31 high-Z) with a brake in progress, U102 HIGH drives the EN net through R126 (1 kOhm) against the 10 kOhm EN bodge; the net rises to about 3.0 V, above the VEN_R maximum 1.4 V, so FC_CHARGE closes during the reset | readback plausibility outside a reset; T-F-12 before power-up |
| T6-T2 (B1-B2) | R171 back-feeds <= 2.0 mA into the Teensy 3V3; UVB and H1 IN- see 3.3 V; UVB drops | announces itself (UVB LOW, T-C-02) |
| T2-T17 (B2-B3) | VBUS drives pin 22 through R171: about 1.3 mA of clamp injection, TODO(verify: i.MX RT1062 injection limit); pin 22 reads full scale; UVB drops | announces itself (`CHG_IIN` implausible, UVB LOW) |
| T17-T16 (B3-B4) | With FLT released, the pin-35 pull-up raises pin 22, which then reads a current. With FLT asserted, both pins read LOW and the eFuse is already off | announces itself (`CHG_IIN` implausible) |
| T16-T10 (B4-B5) | pin 35 reads the QUAL level, so it shows an eFuse fault while QUAL is LOW. An asserted FLT sinks pin 33 through R106s (<= 3.4 mA). A real eFuse fault is masked only while QUAL is HIGH | announces itself (FR-08) |
| T1-T6 (A1-B1) | R170 back-feeds <= 1.64 mA into the 3V3 (19.7 V V-MOT); H1 IN+ sees 3.3 V, so H1 never asserts; no regen release (safe) | H1 state against V-MOT (T-C-02) |
| T7b-T2 (A2-B2) | VBUS shorts to GND through R171 (<= 2 mA); UVB drops | announces itself (UVB LOW) |
| T17r-T17 (A3-B3) | pin 22 reads 0 A, so proof (d) passes falsely. The pair is twisted, so this risk is the same in any connector | the `CHG_IIN` against I2C IBUS cross-check (firmware-rules decision 4a) |
| T5-T16 (A4-B4) | as the r7 row F06-F17: pin 35 reads fault whenever pin 31 is LOW; R106s limits the FLT current (<= 3.377 mA, H.23(n)) | announces itself (FR-08); T-C-05c |
| **T13-T10 (A5-B5), severity 2** | In normal operation pin 34 reads the QUAL level and U102 contends (<= 3.3 mA). During an MCU reset (pin 33 high-Z) with a brake in progress, U102 lifts QUAL; with P5 LOW and FCC_OFF true, the gate releases. This is the QUAL-stuck-HIGH case of the reduced gate, bounded to the reset | readback plausibility outside a reset; T-F-12 before power-up |

Whether the two severity-2 pairs matter depends on the pin 31 and pin 33 states during an MCU reset (pad keeper against the pull-downs, TODO(verify: IMXRT1060RM)). FR-49 and T-D-01 are not extended to those reset levels (firmware-rules decision 5), so the two pairs rest on the T-F-12 cavity check before power-up and on readback plausibility outside a reset (J.2 item 63).

**r9-4 J-TAP open-lead table.** Table A.8-T3 gives the effect of one open or unplugged cavity. A partly mated plug behaves as the open case for each cavity. A contact bent against its neighbour behaves as the row of Table A.8-T2 for that pair.

| Tap | Effect of an open cavity | Detected |
|---|---|---|
| T1 | its divider pulls H1 IN+ to 0 V; no regen release (safe); the regen harvest is lost | H1 readback against V-MOT and V_rgn |
| T7b | shield unbonded; noise only | no |
| T2 | UVB drops and with it H1U (r9-1; was H1q); no regen release (safe) (A.4) | yes, UVB LOW |
| T5 | about 1.0 V at the tap (R187 3.30 MOhm against the U120 1.45 MOhm divider); FCC_OFF and FCC_ON both read LOW: no qualification, no FC window (safe) | function lost |
| T6 | the CR and EIB 3V3 is lost and the gate is unpowered; the r4 design intends this to be fail-safe, TODO(verify: B.7 on the reduced gate) | plausibility signature only |
| T10 | R123 47 kOhm holds QUAL LOW; qualification never releases (safe) | the qualification read fails |
| T13 | pin 34 (`INPUT_PULLDOWN`) reads no brake, so FR-07 never posts the raise; hardware H1 AND UVB can still release | no; accepted cost (firmware-rules decision 4b) |
| T16 | pin 35 (`INPUT_PULLUP`) reads no fault; an eFuse fault is masked (FR-23 and FR-48 blind) | no; accepted cost (firmware-rules decision 4b) |
| T17 | pin 22 floats or sits near 0 V; proof (d) would pass falsely and FR-11 is blind | the `CHG_IIN` against I2C IBUS lead-alive agreement (firmware-rules decision 4a): proof (d) only after agreement in the same charger power cycle, else T10 falls back to proof (b); no Teensy-end pull |
| T17r | shield unbonded; noise only | no |

**r7 adjacent-pad short table (finding tabx-tap-pad-adjacency-unanalysed, H.23(g); superseded in r9-4 by the J-TAP tables above, history only).** The pad gap is 2.54 - 1.50 = 1.04 mm. Each
row assumes one hand-solder bridge or one stray strand across that gap. The 6 x 4 grid has 38 orthogonal pairs. Seven of them
contain a spare position and cannot bridge: (50.80, 61.48)-(53.34, 61.48), (53.34, 61.48)-(55.88, 61.48), (50.80, 66.56)-(53.34, 66.56),
(53.34, 66.56)-(55.88, 66.56), (53.34, 58.94)-(53.34, 61.48), (53.34, 61.48)-(53.34, 64.02) and (53.34, 64.02)-(53.34, 66.56). The
other 31 pairs and the residual-row pairs are listed below. A **push-pull pad** is a pad whose tap wire runs straight to a Teensy
output pin. The CR series resistors of A.4 sit behind the pads, so they do not limit a bridge between two tap wires. r8: R106s
(1.00 kOhm, B.4) sits between the U101 FLT output and the F17 pad, so it limits the current that a bridge at F17 drives
into FLT; it does not limit the contention between the two tap wires (H.23(n)). The
contention figures take about 40 ohm per i.MX output driver (ASSUMPTION, not measured). The T-F-12 tap-to-tap check detects
every row before the first power-up; the last column names the detector in service.

The r5 order (E3 at one end, E8 at the other) could not meet its own E5/E7/E1 maxima from any placement that kept E3 <= 20 mm from TP33 and E8 <= 25 mm from TP49, because TP49 sits above TP33 and TP36 41 mm below it; r6 keeps E8 and E3 together at the top and runs toward TP38 and TP36 (A.5 table, H.22(i)). Isolation rules kept: **E1 (REGN)** has an empty position on both sides and is four pitches from E2 (ILIM feed) and two from E5 (/CE drive): an E1-E2 bridge would feed REGN onto ILIM_HIZ through R21 = 0 ohm and bypass Q203 + R255 (the single-switch release EM3 removed); **E7 (STAT)** has an empty position on both sides: an E6-E7 bridge would lift STAT/pin 6 to ~3.8 V and make /CE self-latching, an E7-E8 bridge would hold pin 6 at "charging" (both now impossible by adjacency: E6 and E8 are four and six pitches away); **E8-E3** are separated by an empty position (a bridge would ground ILIM_HIZ: held, safe, but it would mask a lifted E3). Remaining adjacent pairs: E3-E4 and E4-E2 (all on the ILIM_HIZ node, as in r5) and E5-E6 (both on /CE, as in r5) (r9-2: the E4 and E6 pads carry no lead; the pads, the pad order and the isolation pairs are unchanged). **r9-3 (2026-11-12):** `FCI_OK` is retired with the U117 option and R137. It is not an input of the r9 gate mapping, and no
gate input is reserved for it; where `FCI_OK` appears in the block above, in the truth table below or in F.1, it is history.

What each term does (r9-1):
- `H1U = H1 AND UVB` is the one hardware check the operator keeps. H1 proves V-MOT > 1.089 x VBUS, so D-MT-EN is reverse-biased and, with FC_CHARGE off, the bus cannot feed the charger through the regen path even with firmware hung (R3). UVB makes a lost VBUS tap (which forces H1 HIGH) drop the release, because UVB's divider hangs on the same T2 wire. Cost: no regen harvest while VBUS < 13.4 V, a fault state in Run. H1U has no REGEN and no NOT FCC term: during a burst V-MOT > VBUS reverse-biases D-BC-FC whatever FCC does.
- `FCCP = FCC_ON AND NOT FCC_OFF` (agreement term, permit-gate decision 1): U119 and U120 must agree before an FC window releases the converter. A stuck-HIGH U120 output or a shorted R188 alone (SAFETY-1) then no longer releases the converter in regen-armed cruise with BT on the bus. A stuck-HIGH U119 output ('proven off') makes FCCP = 0 and disables FC windows, a safe and self-announcing failure. The term does not cover a fault that drives the shared T5 node itself (T5 shorted to T6 or to another HIGH lead, pin 31 stuck HIGH): both comparators then agree on a real HIGH. The J-TAP pin order (decision 5) is the only hardware mitigation (A.8, J.1 item 21).
- **No hardware loop barrier in an FC window.** BTB_OFF and BT_OK are removed. Firmware enforces I-9 (FC_CHARGE and BT_BUS never HIGH together), with `FAULT_SWITCH_CONFLICT` as the backstop. A window has no microsecond UVB shed (VINDPM 14.5 V and the 1 kHz firmware act on a sag) and no hardware ceiling blank: after a raised image, when H1 falls, RFC_OFF = 0 restores the FC clamp (0.65-0.95 A, if the BQ25798 re-reads the pin, T-B-07), and VINDPM 18.2 V, the firmware T4 restore posted by the pin-34 falling edge (FR-07) and OC_FC bound the draw (J.1 item 23).
- `QF = QUAL AND FCCN AND NOT P5` releases ILIM_HIZ for the qualification read only while the charge inhibit is on (P5 LOW, so /CE HIGH) and FC_CHARGE is proven off. The NOT P5 term replaces the one-shot's CLR = P5N: without it, QUAL HIGH with P5 HIGH would release the converter with charging enabled and the bus feeding the charger in Run (R3). There is no hardware time limit: firmware drops QUAL when the read completes, bounds it by T_QUAL_MAX 0.46 s with a latching backstop, and drives QUAL LOW at least one tick before P5 rises (FR-04, I-5; firmware-rules decisions 1 and 2; J.1 item 14). A QUAL stuck HIGH in hardware is latent (J.1 item 19).
- `CE_DRV = P5` through the U106A buffer (permit-gate decision 3): U106A drives CE_DRV push-pull into R130, so CE_DRV stays a driven LOW when pin 5 is high-Z (reset, boot), also with a ribbon 4-5 short against the STAT pull-up (A.3 W5; TODO(audit r9)). R108 stays 47.0 kOhm. With no ARM_OK term, /CE follows P5 alone; a hung MCU with P5 HIGH keeps /CE LOW until the R5 watchdog resets it (G.3).
- Latent single faults with no in-service readback (permit-gate decisions 4a-4c): a stuck-HIGH output of U118A, U118B, U110A or U110B, or the ILIM_REL net shorted to 3V3 (R131A and R131B hang on one net, so one CR-side fault opens both EIB switches); QUAL stuck HIGH; /CE stuck LOW. Pin 34 reads back the raw H1 only. The T-C-01 truth-table sweep and T-C-05 run at every build (J.1 items 13, 18-20).

The r8 bullets below are history where they name a removed term (BTB_OFF, BT_OK, H1q, H2c, FCCEIL, the ceiling blank, QQF, ARM_OK, RGN_ON); the pack-voltage bullet stays live:
- **Withdrawn (r9-1):** `BTB_OFF AND BT_OK` in H2c was the **loop barrier for every mode with FCC = 1** (F.3). BTB_OFF is an analog threshold below
  the RT1987's own turn-off level, so no EN level that can leave D-BT-EN conducting reads as "off".
- **Superseded in r9-1 by H1U:** `H1q` was the loop barrier for regen with the pack on the bus. `UVB` in H1q makes a lost VBUS tap (which forces H1 HIGH)
  drop the permit: UVB's divider hangs on the same T2 wire. Cost: no regen harvest while VBUS < 13.4 V, which in Run is a
  fault state anyway.
- **Withdrawn (r9-1):** `(UVB AND FCCEIL) OR (H1 AND RGN)` in H2c: UVB sheds the charger in microseconds if the FC-only bus sags (early purge,
  traction overload, FC boost dropout), **except** while H1 proves V-MOT > 1.089 x VBUS **and** D-BC-RG is commanded on, i.e.
  VCHG-IN is fed from V-MOT and D-BC-FC and D-MT-EN are reverse-biased, so the FC is not loaded. A sag during a raised burst
  therefore does not cut the converter mid-brake. **r2:** without the RGN term, a brake with REGEN LOW and FCC HIGH (State 98
  `J` with REGEN 0, or D-BC-RG in an OTP latch with its EN still HIGH, RT1987 DS-00 §17.8) set H1, bypassed the UVB shed and the
  FCCEIL blank and removed the FC clamp leg while VCHG-IN was fed from VBUS alone (finding h2c-h1-term-not-rgn-qualified). The
  OTP-latch case keeps RGN HIGH; there VCHG-IN follows neither source above VBUS - 35 mV, the charger draws from VBUS through
  D-BC-FC, and the FC image register, VINDPM 14.5 V and OC_FC bound it (no loop: BT_BUS LOW). T-F-09 covers REGEN LOW.
- **Withdrawn (r9-1; no hardware blank):** the **ceiling blank:** in an FC window, if firmware has raised the registers to the regen values (FCCEIL LOW) and V-MOT falls
  back toward VBUS (H1 = 0), H2c = 0 and the converter stops until firmware has restored the FC values and confirms with FCCEIL
  HIGH.
- **Superseded in r9-1 by QF:** `QQF` released ILIM_HIZ for the ADC qualification read only while the charge inhibit is on (CLR = P5N), only for tw_QQ, and
  only with FCC LOW (the Run-entry topology). A QUAL pin stuck HIGH (pin 10 fault, T10 tap shorted HIGH) can then retrigger
  QQ on a P5 fall only in regen-armed topologies, where /CE HIGH (P5 LOW) and the VINDPM 19.0 V soft layer still bar charging
  (F.3 single-fault row, T-D-13).
- **Withdrawn (r9-1, U113 removed):** `ARM_OK` qualified both the charge enable and the converter release: no heartbeat, no charging and no switching.
- **Pack-voltage protection (r8-17, 2026-11-12, D-38; finding vreg-corruption-no-fixed-pack-ovp)** has no term in the permit
  logic; it rests on firmware. The charger's VREG is a volatile register on a bus with no CRC: a single-bit address error turns a
  VINDPM write (0x05, written on every mode change) into a REG01 write that sets VREG to 16.00 V (0xBE or 0xB6 -> VREG_10:8 = 110b
  with REG02 0x40), and a REG09 or REG00 write into 13.44 V or 10.88 V (H.22(a)); the BQ25798 VBAT_OVP follows VREG (103-105 %,
  SLUSDV2C §6.5), so it moves to ~16.5 V with it. Four firmware layers stop such a corruption (F.3). First, firmware reads REG01:02 and
  the written register back in the same transaction group after every limit write (FR-46), so a corrupted VREG lives for one
  transaction, not 20 ms. Second, the 20 ms slot-5 verify (REG00-0A) catches anything FR-46 missed. Third, the BT_VOLTAGE
  reading (Teensy pin 25) latches `CHG_PACK_OV` and takes P5 LOW above `LIMIT_V_BATT_MAX` 8.5 V (FR-47(a)); P5 LOW takes /CE
  HIGH through CE_DRV. Fourth, the OV_BATT fault at the same limit latches State 99. FR-47(a) is a firmware requirement, not yet
  implemented; until then only OV_BATT acts on a pack OV. A hung MCU is covered only by the R5 watchdog reset (r9-6, 2026-11-12, D2-2: no hardware hang inhibit exists; pack OV over the at most t_WDT + 1 ms of hang-time charging rests on the BQ25798, J.2 item 69; **superseded in r9:** "A hung MCU is still covered in hardware, because the heartbeat stops and ARM_OK falls.") The r6 hardware term OVN (BQ29200
  OUT on tap T22 through R178, D108, R179 and the Schmitt inverter U123, gated into ARM_OK by U122) is removed. A 30 AWG wire
  cannot be soldered reliably to the outer toe of BQ29200 pin 8 (DRB pad 0.35 mm wide, 0.65 mm pitch to VDD), and a T22 left open
  would read overvoltage through R179 and refuse all charging. The operator accepts the costs (J.1 item 11). First, no firmware- and
  register-independent pack barrier remains, so live but faulty firmware that corrupts VREG and also fails the FR-46 and FR-47
  checks can overcharge the pack. Second, firmware sees the pack voltage, not each cell, so a cell imbalance is not detected.
  Third, the 8.5 V trip sits ~180 mV above the interim 8.32 V VREG and 146 mV below the 8.646 V ADC ceiling. As a result,
  charging no longer needs the balance lead J-BL plugged in. The BQ29200 stays fitted (OVP-only, `CBAL_DISABLE`); its OUT
  (net BAL-NOK) is again an orphan.
- **`FCC_OFF`, `FCC_ON` (r6; RGN_ON removed in r9-1; finding fcc-rgn-lvc-threshold-vs-rt1987-en-band):** the RT1987 can turn on anywhere up to
  VEN_R 1.4 V and is guaranteed off only below VEN_F 0.6 V (DS-00 EC p.7), while a plain SN74LVC input reads 0.8-2.0 V either way.
  FCC is used with both polarities (r9-1: FCC = 0 is the unsafe reading for QF and RFC_OFF, FCC = 1 for FCCP; **superseded in r9:** FCC = 0 is the unsafe reading for W, H1q, QQF and RFC_OFF; FCC = 1 for H2c), so each use now has
  its own comparator whose threshold lies on the safe side of the RT1987 band: FCC_OFF only below REF/3 (0.39-0.44 V), FCC_ON
  only above 1.75-1.88 V (**superseded in r9:** FCC_ON and RGN_ON only above 1.75-1.88 V). Any intermediate EN level (a pin left `INPUT_PULLUP`, ~1 V, H.22(h)), an open tap or a comparator in
  POR reads FCC_OFF = FCC_ON = 0 (r9-1): FCCP = 0, QF = 0 and RFC_OFF = H1U (FC clamp kept unless a brake proves V-MOT > 1.089 x VBUS); RGN_ON is removed with U121 (**superseded in r9:** FCC_OFF = FCC_ON = RGN_ON = 0: W = 0 and H1q = 0, QQF = 0, RFC_OFF = H1R = 0 (FC clamp kept), H2c = 0). (**superseded in r9:** U115 BTB_OFF was
  already built this way for D-BT-EN.) The comparators add their 2-4 us propagation delay (SBOS300C §6.10) to the FCC paths (**superseded in r9:** FCC/RGN paths),
  against the RT1987's own EN response; F.4 step A now reads "FCCP = 0 within the U120 propagation delay" (r9-1; r6: H2c).
- `RFC_OFF` keeps the FC clamp (0.65-0.95 A, H.4) in hardware whenever FCC = 1 and not (H1 AND UVB) (r9-1, operator option (b), harvest kept; **superseded in r9:** not (H1 AND RGN)). A brake inside an FC window with REGEN LOW therefore lifts the FC clamp while VCHG-IN is fed from VBUS alone (the r2 hazard, finding h2c-h1-term-not-rgn-qualified), which the operator accepts (J.1 item 22); firmware confines REGEN LOW with FCC HIGH to State 98 (FR-49, firmware-rules decision 3b). It acts at any charger POR, and at
  run time **if** the BQ25798 re-reads the pin continuously (T-B-07; SLUSDV2C §7.3.4.3 says "at POR", the pin table says
  "lower of pin and register").

Truth table (r9-1, 2026-11-12; X = don't care; the FCC column means a driven EN net: FCC = 1 gives FCC_ON = 1, FCC_OFF = 0, and FCC = 0 gives FCC_ON = 0, FCC_OFF = 1; 'mid' is an EN level of 0.45-1.74 V or an open T5; H1U = H1 AND UVB, FCCP = FCC_ON AND NOT FCC_OFF, QF = QUAL AND FCCN AND NOT P5, GATE = H1U OR FCCP, ILIM_REL = GATE OR QF, /CE = NOT P5, RFC_OFF = FCCN OR H1U; REGEN is not a gate input):

| 0 | X | X | 0 | 0 | H1U | 0 | H1U | HIGH | 1 | Idle / Init: REGEN and FCC LOW, so the charger has no input power |
| 0 | 0 | X | 0 | 1 | 0 | **1** | **1** | HIGH | 1 | Run-entry qualification: pin released, charge inhibited (/CE HIGH and EN_CHG = 0 written first); no hardware time limit (firmware T_QUAL_MAX 0.46 s, latching) |
| 0 | 0 | X | 1 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | LOW | 1 | firmware slip (QUAL with P5 HIGH): the NOT P5 term keeps the converter off |
| 0 | 0 | 1 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | LOW | 1 | regen armed, cruise: converter off (EN_EXTILIM = 1, T-B-21) |
| 0 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 0 | 1 | 0 | 1 | LOW | 1 | regen burst: converter on, regen clamp; D-MT-EN reverse-biased |
| 0 | 1 | 0 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | LOW | 1 | regen with the bus below UVB, or T2 lost (H1 forced HIGH, UVB LOW): off |
| 1 | 0 | X | 1 | X | 1 | 0 | 1 | LOW | 0 | FC window charging, FC clamp in hardware; loop barrier firmware only (I-9); a bus sag (UVB 0) does not shed it |
| 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 | X | 1 | 0 | 1 | LOW | 1 | brake inside an FC window: converter on, regen clamp |
| 1 | 1 | 0 | 1 | X | 1 | 0 | 1 | LOW | 0 | brake inside an FC window with the bus below UVB: converter on, FC clamp (0.65-0.95 A); harvest limited, V-MOT may reach the VESC cut (safe) |
| 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 | X | 1 | 0 | 1 | LOW | 1 | brake inside an FC window with REGEN LOW (State 98, or a D-BC-RG OTP latch with EN HIGH): the gate does not see REGEN, so the FC clamp lifts while VCHG-IN is fed from VBUS (the r2 hazard, accepted, J.1 item 22) |
| 1 | 0 | X | 1 | X | 1 | 0 | 1 | LOW | 0 | raised image, V-MOT back near VBUS: **no hardware blank**; FC clamp if the pin is re-read (T-B-07), VINDPM 18.2 V and the firmware T4 on the pin-34 falling edge bound the draw |
| 1 | X | X | 0 | 1 | per H1U and FCCP | 0 | GATE | HIGH | per FCCN, H1U | QUAL HIGH with FCC HIGH: QF = 0 (FCCN = 0), masked |

| X | X | X | **0** (FR-47) | 0 | per mode | 0 | GATE | HIGH | per mode | firmware pack OV (BT_VOLTAGE > `LIMIT_V_BATT_MAX` 8.5 V): `CHG_PACK_OV` takes P5 LOW, so /CE goes HIGH and charging stops in every mode; needs a live MCU and a valid pin-25 reading (r8-17, D-38) |
| mid | X | X | X | X | H1U | 0 | H1U | per P5 | H1U | D-BC-FC EN at an intermediate level or T5 open: FCC_OFF = FCC_ON = 0, so no FC release and no qualification release; regen release only through H1U, with D-BC-FC reverse-biased |
| 0, U120 stuck HIGH | 0 | 1 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | LOW | 1 | SAFETY-1 masked by the agreement term: FCC_OFF = 1, so FCCNN = 0 and FCCP = 0 |
| X | X | X | X | X | X | X | **1** (stuck) | per P5 | X | gate output stuck HIGH or ILIM_REL shorted to 3V3: converter released in every mode, VINDPM the only stop on a loop in regen-armed cruise; latent (J.1 item 18), T-C-01 / T-C-05 at every build |

Node T2C is the CR end of the single VBUS tap (T2 through R171). The H1 and UVB dividers load it together, so the two are
solved as one network in `r3_calc.py` H.1/H.2 (including the coupling through R116 when UVB switches).

- **H1 trips** (worst case: 0.1 % dividers, Vos +-9 mV, VHYS 2-8 mV, CMRR 54 dB, both UVB states): rise 17.31 V / fall 17.01 V
  nominal at VBUS 15.9 V (ratio 1.089, hysteresis 0.30 V); fall >= 16.81 V (guard 0.91 V over VBUS); at VBUS 16.39 V fall
  17.34-17.76 V and rise <= 18.05 V; at VBUS 15.2 V (loaded FC-only bus) fall >= 16.05 V (guard 0.85 V).
- **UVB trips:** fall 13.33 V nominal (band 12.89-13.78 V), rise 13.72 V (band 13.26-14.16 V), including REF drift over 0-45 C
  and the CMRR term (re-solved with R116 10.0 MOhm in r2). The fall band sits 0.34 V below the FC VINDPM floor (14.5 V - 2.6 % =
  14.12 V, T-B-13) and the rise band 1.04 V below the loaded FC-only bus (assumed >= 15.2 V, T-E-08).
- **Withdrawn (r9-1, U104 removed; history):** BT_OK trip: 19.75 mV nominal; 6.0-33.5 mV worst case = 0.06-0.34 A of BT boost forward current. The INA253A1
  zero-current output can reach 10 mV (SLOS954A §6.5 swing to GND +10 mV max, §7.5), so with an unselected R142 a false "not OK"
  at zero current is possible on an in-spec board. **r3 (finding btok-selftest-floor-overlap):** (1) **R142 is select-on-test
  per unit:** T-E-10 measures the Kelvin floor with a DMM, T-C-03 measures U104's actual falling and rising trip, and R142 is
  chosen (H.19 table, 0.604-1.40 kOhm) so that the falling trip >= floor + 4 mV and the rising trip <= 29 mV (the 0.29 A R8
  bound); the static Vos/VHYS spread then drops out and only ~0.5-1 mV of drift remains over 0-60 C. (2) A BT_OK self-test
  failure refuses **FC windows only**, never regen arming (H1q has no BT_OK term; FR-12).
- **Withdrawn (r9-1, U115 removed; history):** BTB_OFF threshold: 0.39-0.44 V worst case (REF tolerance, drift, Vos, hysteresis), 0.16 V below VEN_F min 0.6 V
  (RT1987 DS-00 EC p.7). With pin 28 driven LOW the input sits at 3 mV; with the Teensy in reset (EN net held by the 10 kOhm
  bodge pull-down) the EN net is at 3 mV and IN- at 7 mV; with pin 28 accidentally `INPUT_PULLUP` the EN net reaches about
  1.02 V, which may keep D-BT-EN on, and U115 reads it as "may be on" (permit removed). **r2 (finding btb-pullup-backdrives-en):**
  with R119 1.00 MOhm, an open 10 kOhm EN bodge pull-down plus pin 28 high-Z (reset, bootloader) left only the RT1987's own
  REN_PD (475-985 kOhm, EC p.7) against the pull-up and lifted EN to 1.06-1.63 V, inside or above the enable band: BT_BUS could
  turn on during an MCU reset. With R119 10.0 MOhm that case gives 0.15-0.30 V (< VEN_F min 0.6 V); the open-tap detection
  still works (TLV3012 bias pA), and the R119 current shifts the U115 input by only 3.3 mV. T-D-01 checks it. **r6:** U105
  sections 1 and 3 are spare, inputs tied to GND (section 1 was the FCC inverter, replaced by U119). **r9-1:** U105 section 1 forms FCCNN = NOT FCCN for the agreement term; only section 3 is spare (B.3).
- **FCC_OFF / FCC_ON / RGN_ON (r6, H.22(h); r9-1: RGN_ON and the tap T4 are removed, so the pin-30 figures below are history, TODO(calc: H.22(h) r9 re-run); the T5 node is unchanged):** FCC tap open: 0.97 V (R187 against the 1.45 MOhm U120 divider) -> FCC_OFF "may be on",
  FCC_ON off; tap connected with pin 31 high-Z and the 10 kOhm EN bodge open: EN 0.31-0.48 V, below VEN_F min 0.6 V (the switch stays
  off; FCC_OFF may read "may be on", the safe side); pin 31 or pin 30 left `INPUT_PULLUP` (~22 kOhm pad pull-up, TODO(verify: PJRC
  core pinMode / IMXRT1060RM PUS), T-D-01): EN 1.02 V / 0.95 V, every comparator reads the safe value. Driven LOW: ~10 mV. Driven HIGH:
  > 3 V against a 1.88 V maximum trip. The R187 current shifts the U119 input by 10 mV.
- **Input protection:** an open divider bottom (R110, R112 or R115) would put up to 22 V on a comparator input through about
  0.5-1 MOhm. The BAV199 pairs (D104-D106) clamp each input to 3V3 + one diode (36 uA at 22 V) and keep it inside the TLV3012
  7 V absolute maximum, which TI says must be enforced externally beyond (V+) (SBOS300C §6.1 note 2). BAV199 leakage
  (nA class at 25 C) on the 50-90 kOhm divider nodes shifts the trips by < 1 mV; T-A-07 measures it hot.
- **Tap faults:** R170/R171 at the MB joints make every tap wire a 10 kOhm-sourced signal: a tap shorted to GND draws 2.2 mA
  (48 mW in an 0805) instead of shorting the V-MOT node or the bus.

**r9-1 (2026-11-12):** five LVC packages remain (U105, U106, U107, U110, U118; permit-gate decision 2, `ramifications/gate.md`). The only CR readback left is H1 -> pin 34 (R126 1 kOhm, T13). The H2c (pin 16, R127) and BT_OK (pin 23, R128) readbacks are removed, and the far-end senses are not fitted (r9-2), so no gate output and no EVM-side inhibit node is read back (J.1 items 13, 18-20). The paragraph below is history except for the ribbon drivers, which now leave the CR from U106A (CE_DRV), U110B (ILIM_REL) and U106B (RFC_OFF), and for the edge-rate exception, which the r9-1 note after it restates.

Readbacks to Teensy (all `INPUT_PULLDOWN`, i.MX RT1062 pad pull-down ~100 kOhm, TODO(verify: i.MX RT1060 RM, T-C-07), so a
dead or unpowered source reads LOW): H1 -> pin 34 (R126 1 kOhm), H2c -> pin 16 (R127), BT_OK -> pin 23 (R128); the far-end
ILIM_HIZ sense and the far-end /CE sense are retired (r9-2, 2026-11-12: U203/U204 DNP on the EIB; R125, R148 and the ILIM_SENSE/CE_SENSE nets deleted on the CR; **superseded in r9:** U203 -> pin 33 (EIB R265 **470 ohm** (r4) + CR R125 1 kOhm) and U204 -> **pin 7** (EIB R264 **470 ohm** (r4)
+ CR R148 1.00 kOhm, tap T20 at the vacated MB ROS pad (r9-4: tap T20 is removed, ROS stays fitted and pin 7 stays undriven, A.4); r2, finding eib-pin8-backpower-unpowered-outputs)). Ribbon drivers:
CE_DRV (R130), ILIM_REL_A (R131A), ILIM_REL_B (R131B) and RFC_OFF (R132) leave CR through 100 ohm series resistors to damp the
0.30 m flat cable. **Edge rate (r2 restatement, finding lvc-slow-edges-reset):** every plain SN74LVC input sees a CMOS-speed
edge (<= 10 ns/V, Recommended Operating Conditions of every SN74LVC datasheet used here) **in normal operation**: no RC filter
sits in front of a plain logic input, and TLV3012B push-pull outputs switch in 10 ns typ (SBOS300C §6.10). **Exception:** when a
Teensy pin goes high-Z (reset, boot, flashing) or a tap opens, CHG_ARM (R108 47 kOhm) and FCCEIL (R124 47 kOhm) fall only through
their pull-downs, about 0.4-0.5 us/V through the 0.8-2.0 V band, so CE_DRV, ILIM_REL and H2c may chatter for microseconds while
ARM_OK is still HIGH (r6: the FCC/RGN EN nets now reach the logic only through the U119-U121 comparators, push-pull outputs, so they
leave this list; r8-17, D-38: the r6 BQ29200 OUT input through the U123 Schmitt input is removed). The prior state is the enabled one and every chatter
edge moves toward the safe state, so no new hazard arises; the exception is accepted and tested (T-D-01: 20 resets with P5 HIGH,
no LOW-to-HIGH glitch on ILIM_REL and no new /CE LOW edge). Fallback if T-D-01 fails: Schmitt buffers (SN74LVC3G17) on CHG_ARM and
FCCEIL at the CR inputs. The two RC-timed nodes are the SN74LVC1G123 Rext/Cext pins, which are designed for it,
and its A/B inputs are Schmitt inputs.

**r9-1 (2026-11-12, edge-rate exception restated):** FCCEIL (R124), ARM_OK, H2c and the SN74LVC1G123 parts are removed, so the sentences above that name them are history. When pin 5 goes high-Z, CHG_ARM falls through R108 47.0 kOhm into U105 2A and into the plain LVC input of the U106A buffer (not into U114); U106A drives CE_DRV push-pull, so the ribbon and U201 1A see a CMOS-speed edge. CE_DRV and ILIM_REL may chatter for microseconds, and no ARM_OK term holds them; every chatter edge still moves toward the safe state (/CE HIGH; QF can rise only if QUAL was HIGH before the reset, and the RT1987 EN pull-downs then leave the charger unpowered). The **T-D-01 scope point and its Schmitt fallback move to the U106A input** (fallback: a Schmitt buffer on CHG_ARM ahead of U105 2A and U106 1A). QUAL (pin 33, R123, into the plain U107 A input) is not added to T-D-01: firmware-rules decision 5 rules that the RT1987 EN pull-downs keep the charger unpowered through any reset or boot. No RC-timed node remains on the CR.

**r4 residuals of the higher D107 VBR (r5: restart-mode independent):** a V-MOT excursion above the D-BC-RG OVP trip removes the
regen path; if the part latches (EC p.7, §17.7) it stays off until REGEN EN is toggled, and if it auto-restarts (Table 1) it
re-soft-starts into VCHG-IN by itself once V-MOT falls below the trip, so the charger may see a POR and resume converting without
the firmware having toggled REGEN. **Firmware rule (FR-30, r5):** any V_chg collapse below 10.2 V and return with REGEN HIGH is a
charger POR whatever the RT1987 did: P5 LOW on the detecting tick, the clamp-latched / harvest-lost flags, and re-qualification
through T9 (T1 steps 4-9 from the REGN marker) before P5 rises again (I-3); a toggle of REGEN EN at the next safe point re-arms a
latched part. Harvest is lost meanwhile; an excursion above 35 V exceeds C-D8/C-D10 and approaches the RT1987 40 V absolute maximum
whatever D107 is, and D107 is not credited for it (J.2).

Fault behaviour: overload above I_OL is regulated at I_OL for 129-202 ms (tCL_PLIM), then latch; above 2 x I_OL (4.1-4.8 A)
the fast-trip turns the FET off in 2.2-4.5 us; a hot short above I_SCP (45 A) in 1 us (§6.6). D103 clamps OUT on each of
these turn-offs and on the OVP shutoff. **IN side (r3):** the input current keeps rising during the 1 us response, so the
energy in the 50-150 nH MB VCHG-IN path at turn-off corresponds to 40-117 A, not 45 A (H.19); C102a/C102b take it (IN <= 33 V
in the ideal simulation) and D107 backs them up. The overload case (4.1-4.8 A) adds only a few volts. The limit sits above the 1.76 A regen clamp maximum (margin 0.30 A) and above OC_FC
(1.4 A), so in an FC window a charger-side short latches OC_FC (State 99) first: a firmware stop, not a boost death.
**Unprotected segment (r2, finding w8-unfused-hot-lead):** the board-side VCHG-IN segment (C-D8, C-D10, MB trace, the pad-10
pin, the CR VCHGIN copper, U101 IN) is upstream of the eFuse and has **no current limit for all of Run** in the always-powered
design: the RT1987 SCP is active only during soft-start ("both the SCP current limit and shutdown functions are disabled after
tON", DS-00 §17.5), so only OTP (~140 C) remains. Bus-fed fault current passes the INA253s and is bounded by the OC_FC/OC_BT
single-sample firmware latches; the CAL 470 uF + VESC bulk discharge through D-BC-RG is not bounded and may exceed the RT1987
20 A / 10 ms peak rating. Mitigation is mechanical: W8 deleted (no flying lead on this segment), CR copper from the pad-10 pin to
U101 <= 5 mm and solder-masked (A.8), inspection T-F-12 (J.1).

### B.5 Keep-alive option (R9; **withdrawn in r9-3**) and fallback 2

**r9-3 (2026-11-12): the keep-alive option is withdrawn.** U112, C152, D101 and R_KA have no footprint and no BOM line, and the supply tap T18 with F101 and R172 is removed (PM7). The rows below are history. T-B-09 is kept, because the H1·UVB release keeps regen-armed cruise. On a T-B-09 failure the path is fallback 2, the fused link below, or a keep-alive redesigned in a later round. (**superseded in r9:** Fit only if T-B-09 fails. Source: battery-derived 5 V rail at CO-5V (T18).)

| Ref | Part | Connection | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|

| D101 | **withdrawn (r9-3, 2026-11-12), no footprint** (**superseded in r9:** BAT54HT1G, 30 V 0.2 A Schottky) | (**superseded in r9:** U112 VOUT -> anode; cathode -> R_KA) | - |
| R_KA | **withdrawn (r9-3, 2026-11-12), no footprint** (**superseded in r9:** 680 ohm 0.25 W 1206) | (**superseded in r9:** D101 -> `VCHG`) | (**superseded in r9:** VCHG held at 3.63-4.46 V, H.10) |

(r9-3: the next two sentences give the drain of the withdrawn keep-alive and are history; the Run-time standby draw that follows them stays valid.) Drain 0.65-1.28 mA plus 0.06-0.08 mA **only while REGEN is closed (Run)**; 0.5-2.3 uA parked. The round-2 M8 (1 kOhm from VBT,
always on) drew 1.2-1.7 mA continuously (29-41 mAh/day). The Run-time standby draw of the always-powered regen design itself is
3.5-5.0 mA from the bus (56-80 mW, H.15, r3 recount with the REGN loads and R272b), which the energy statistics must carry in every build (r9-3: the keep-alive option is withdrawn; **superseded in r9:** whether or not the keep-alive is fitted).
**Second fallback (r5: a fused link, never a plain 0 ohm bridge; finding fallback2-pack-unfused-on-w3-and-bridge-rating):** (r9-3, 2026-11-12: with the keep-alive withdrawn, this is the only hardware fail branch of T-B-09 and T-B-01; it keeps the name fallback 2.)
remove D-BT-SQ (a 3 x 3 mm 12-VDFN at (29.72, 50.04): a chip jumper cannot bridge VIN-VOUT under it) and fit a **fused link
from C-D12 pad 1 (VBT, (34.29, 50.04)) to C-D11 pad 1 (VCHG, (26.16, 50.29))**, ~8 mm across the vacated site, before the CR is
fitted, Kapton over the exposed joint. The fuse is placed where pack energy enters the newly exposed net, so one part protects all
of it: the VCHG pour, C-D11, header pins 18/19, the CR VCHG copper, W3, EVM J5, JP5 and the EVM BAT ceramics, which in the
baseline are fed only by the current-regulated charger (D-BT-SQ blocks VBT -> VCHG, DS-00 §17.6). **Fuse requirements, all read
from the chosen part's datasheet in T-A-05 (no MPN before then):** nominal >= 5 A (3.21 A ICHG maximum at <= 75 % derating,
H.21); DC voltage rating >= 16 V (2x the 8.4 V pack maximum; 32 V acceptable, not required); interrupting rating >= the
prospective pack fault current measured in **T-A-05c** (pack DCIR by pulse step, never a dead short; H.21 shows 120-420 A for
10-60 mOhm); I2t below the short-time limits of the C-D11 pads, the 0.64 mm header pins, the 18 AWG W3 and the CR VCHG pour;
a 1206-2410 class body or a fuse plus a >= 20 AWG link spanning the ~8 mm, link rated >= 6 A. If no SMD fuse meets the
interrupting rating, fallback 2 is not permitted without a current-limiting eFuse in the link (a second TPS26630-class part on
its own small carrier, limit >= 3.5 A). The pack then sits on the BQ25798 BAT pin. Parked drain is the BQ25798 battery-only quiescent, 17-24 uA with ADC off (IQ_BAT_ON) or 11-16 uA in ship mode
(IQ_BAT_OFF), SLUSDV2C EC p.8. **Trade-off (r4 restatement, finding fallback2-dbtsq-disconnect-claim):** in the baseline
BT_SEQUENCE_ENABLE is never turned off (IO CSV row 32) and D-BT-SQ conducts VCHG -> VBT whenever VCHG > VBT (RT1987 DS-00
§17.6), so it never disconnects a forward fault; a charger power-stage short is bounded by the eFuse and the FR-33 REGEN/FCC drop
in the baseline **and** in this fallback. What the fallback loses is D-BT-SQ's **reverse block**: the pack then sits on BAT, so
the parked BAT draw and the OTG/backup never-write rules (G.1: REG0B-REG0D, REG47, REG0F EN_BACKUP 0) become load-bearing for
pack drain and pack-sourced outputs. The r3 text ("the hardware pack disconnect is lost") misstated the delta. **r5:** losing the
reverse block also turns the VCHG/W3/EVM-BAT nodes from charger-limited into **pack-fed**: a chafed W3, a W3-W4 short at J5 or a
cracked MLCC on that net (C-D11, the EVM BAT/SYS ceramics) becomes a pack short circuit, bounded only by the link fuse above
(T-A-05c, T-F-12, T-B-16). **r6 (finding dbtsq-short-unfused-pack-on-vchg): the baseline reaches the same topology with one fault, a
shorted D-BT-SQ FET, and then has no fuse at all.** The design answers it by detection, not a baseline fuse: with D-BT-SQ healthy,
VCHG decays below 3 V within <= 0.78 s whenever the charger is not converting (Idle, or regen-armed cruise with ILIM held, H.9), and
with it shorted VCHG sits at the pack voltage, a difference of > 4 V (r9-3: the keep-alive option, which would have held VCHG at <= 4.46 V, is withdrawn; **superseded in r9:** even with the keep-alive fitted (<= 4.46 V)). FR-48 checks it in
Idle (an ACK from 0x6B with VCHG-IN unpowered means the BQ25798 runs from BAT; the VBAT ADC, which works in battery-only mode with
ADC_EN = 1 above 2.9 V, SLUSDV2C §7.3.10, confirms it against pin-25 V_batt) and every second of regen-armed cruise (VBAT ADC, REG3B,
Table 7-63). A confirmed short latches `CHG_DBTSQ_SHORT`: P5, REGEN and FCC LOW, windows and regen refused, and a request to the
operator to power down and disconnect the pack before touching W3 or the EVM; the motor path is unaffected. The exposure window
is therefore one cruise second or one boot, not a power cycle. A fuse in series with W3 on the CR was considered and not adopted
(L.6): it would add resistance in every regen burst and protect only the CR-to-EVM part of the net. T-D-15 tests the detection.

The E1 lead, its E8 return and C205 form a series LC near the 1.5 MHz BQ25798 switching frequency (JP24, EM19). At the 90 mm E1 maximum f0 is 1.430 MHz (1.471 MHz at the r6 85 mm). The undamped Q is 19.1 (19.3 at 85 mm), an upper bound from the DC wire resistance; the skin-effect Rac gives 13.0. With R276 the Q is 0.111 (zeta 4.5, overdamped). R276 x C205 is a 159 kHz low-pass: a 1.5 MHz REGN ripple reaches C205 at 0.106 of its EVM amplitude (T-C-16). **E1 load (r7 correction):** E1 carries only the EIB REGN loads, namely the gate pull-ups R252 (Q201) and R254 (Q202), the Q203 gate-source resistor R271 and, while released, the feed through Q203 and R255. R272 and R272b sit on the EVM and draw from REGN there, not through E1. I_E1 is 0-0.111 mA held and 0.272-0.396 mA released (REGN 4.8-5.2 V). The R276 drop is 1.02 mV at the H.15 E1 load (0.102 mA, held, R254 only) and at most 3.96 mV (released, regen clamp, REGN 5.2 V). That drop lowers the released ILIM_HIZ level by at most 1.786 mV, which lowers IINDPM by 2.23 mA (the safe direction for the converter and the eFuse; 0.13-0.17 % of the 1.33-1.76 A regen clamp, so no H.7 effect). Held levels do not change: Q203 is off and no feed flows. R276 open acts as an E1 lead off (fault table, first row); R276 shorted restores the undamped r6 circuit, which is also a pickup-budget fault on E3/E4 through the shared E8 return (A.5); T-A-02 meters R276 at 10.0 ohm +-1 %, and T-C-16 fails a shorted R276 (predicted C205/TP27 ratio 7.8-8.8 against the 0.2 limit) |
| J201 | 2x7 **1.27 mm** header mating the W5 cable assembly (r4), keyed | ribbon W5; r9-2: pins 11 and 13 end on the DNP R265/R264 pads (no fitted connection) | - |

REGN exists whenever the converter can run (SLUSDV2C §7.3.4.1), so the stages are biased exactly when they are needed. While
REGN is absent /CE and ILIM_HIZ read 0 V. **REGN is absent not only when the charger is unpowered (r3):** after VBUS valid it
comes on only 150 ms (typical, no maximum) after VBUS_PRESENT_STAT (SLUSDV2C §7.3.4 step 5) while I2C answers from 20 ms (step
4); it is off whenever EN_HIZ = 1 (§7.3.6.5), which the charger sets itself on a failed poor-source qualification (§7.3.4.2),
on IBUS_OCP and on VSYS_SHORT, and which firmware sets in the I-6/T9 retries; and the eFuse latch removes EVM VBUS while pin 38
(board side of U101) stays high. Holding ILIM_HIZ below 0.75 V by pin, by contrast, keeps REGN on (§7.3.4.3). FR-08(b) and the
safe-direction "permit stuck LOW" rule are therefore gated on `regnExpected` (FR-23), which is TRUE only once REGN is proven
(PG_STAT = 1; r9-2: the /CE-sense proof is gone with U204; **superseded in r9:** or a /CE-sense HIGH with P5 LOW) or must exist by now (T_REGN_MAX after VBUS_PRESENT or the last EN_HIZ clear,
with EN_HIZ 0, FLT HIGH, fresh I2C); (r9-2: FR-08(a) and the sense-based FR-08(b) have no input with U203/U204 DNP; `regnExpected` stays only where the r9 FR-08(b) I2C trip uses it; the r3 text that follows is history) FR-08(a) is gated only on V_chg > 10.2 V and FLT HIGH, because an ILIM sense HIGH without
REGN can only be a fault (r3, findings t1-ce-check-before-regn, fr08-powered-predicate-ignores-regn, ce-sense-gating-before-regn).
2N7002K and BSS84 thresholds, on-resistance, Ciss and off-state leakage at 2-3 V are not in the library: T-A-03.

### B.9 What the carrier and the EIB need from the firmware

The hardware above needs these firmware behaviours, specified in G.2 (r9-7, 2026-11-12: rewritten for the reduced permit gate; the heartbeat, the QUAL one-shot, the far-end senses and FCCEIL are removed): QUAL (pin 33, a level release request with no hardware time limit) raised only with P5 LOW after EN_CHG = 0 is verified and PG_STAT = 1 is seen, dropped when the qualification read completes and in any case at T_QUAL_MAX 0.46 s by the FR-45 backstop (`CHG_QUAL_OVERRUN`), and driven LOW for at least one 1 kHz tick before every P5 rise (FR-04, I-5, T1, T9); the I2C latch trip on a charger that converts with P5 LOW (FR-08(b)) and the H1 plausibility check (FR-08(d)), both with the `regnExpected` gate (FR-23); the pin-34 ISR on both edges (FR-07); the T3 raise only with REGEN read back HIGH, and no FC_CHARGE HIGH with REGEN LOW outside State 98 (T3, FR-49); the CHG_IIN cross-check against the IBUS ADC and the lead-alive rule of the T10 proof (d) (FR-11, `CHG_IIN_LEAD`); FC_CHARGE/BT_BUS never HIGH together (FR-06, I-9); REG14 never written (FR-03); pin 34 `INPUT_PULLDOWN`, pin 35 `INPUT_PULLUP`, pin 22 `INPUT_DISABLE`, and the freed pins 10, 16, 17, 21 and 23 `INPUT_PULLDOWN` with the boot `UNEXPECTED_LEAD` read (FR-01); and an I2C bus clear at boot and after any bus-busy timeout (FR-07). **r5:** the qualified brake feed-forward and BRAKE state (FR-41), the independent pre-emption backstop (FR-42), flash writes only in quiescent states with the watchdog windowed on `rtwdogShort` (FR-43) and the STAT path plausibility check that pairs with EIB R275 (FR-44). **r6:** the 1 kHz timer domain for the window-time-critical set (FR-45), the same-transaction read-back of every limit write (FR-46), the `CHG_PACK_OV` latch on BT_VOLTAGE above `LIMIT_V_BATT_MAX` (FR-47(a); r8-17, D-38; r9-7: the unexpected /CE-sense trip FR-47(b) is withdrawn with its input), the D-BT-SQ short check (FR-48) and the boot pad check that keeps every RT1987 EN pin a driven output (FR-49). (**superseded in r9:** "the heartbeat toggled only by a completed 1 kHz monitor tick (FR-28, r3)"; "QUAL raised only after EN_CHG = 0 is verified and REGN is proven, and LOW on every P5 change (FR-04, I-5, T1), the two far-end senses compared in the dangerous direction with the heartbeat timeout HB_dead, the one-shot length TW_QQ_MAX and the `regnExpected` gate (FR-08, FR-23)"; "readback pins `INPUT_PULLDOWN` (FR-01)"; "with the watchdog windowed on the heartbeat (FR-43)"; "with the unexpected /CE-sense HIGH kept as a carrier-inhibit trip".) The R5 watchdog fed only by a completed 1 kHz monitor tick (FR-28) and the R5 build flag that gates every charger arming (FR-05) stay as r9-6 states them.

### D.2 Firmware-visible pin changes

Pin 5 changes meaning (MPPT_DISABLE LOW = Ag105 MPPT inhibited -> CHG_ARM LOW = BQ25798 charge inhibited); both are LOW =
safe, so the boot level in `setup()` stays LOW. Pin 6 polarity inverts (Ag105 HIGH = charging -> BQ25798 LOW = charging,
SLUSDV2C Table 7-11). **r9-7 (2026-11-12, tap review and firmware-rules decisions 5 and 7):** the reduced permit gate uses Teensy pins 5 (`CHG_ARM`), 33 (`CHG_QUAL`, an `OUTPUT` driven LOW early in `setup()`; moved from pin 10, the default SPI CS0), 22 (`CHG_IIN`), 34 (`CHG_H1_RB`, `INPUT_PULLDOWN`) and 35 (`CHG_EFUSE_FLT`, `INPUT_PULLUP`), plus the pin-31 net through tap T5. Pin 7 carries no tap; it keeps its FR-01 setting and is never driven (CSV row 7 "No longer in use" stands). Pin 8 and its encoder net are not touched (r2). The freed pins 10, 16, 17, 21 and 23 are `INPUT_PULLDOWN` with a boot read (FR-01, `UNEXPECTED_LEAD`); pin 21 keeps this mode until the EWM_OUT_B question (G.3) is decided. (**superseded in r9:** "**Pin 7** (was ENC_ENABLE, undriven since 2026-08-16) becomes the /CE far-end readback input (`INPUT_PULLDOWN`, no pull-up on its net after PM10); pin 8 and its encoder net are not touched (r2); pin 21 becomes the heartbeat output. Readback pins 7, 16, 23, 33, 34 are `INPUT_PULLDOWN`.")
**r6 (finding fcc-rgn-lvc-threshold-vs-rt1987-en-band):** every RT1987 EN pin (27, 28, 29, 30, 31, 32) is a driven `OUTPUT` from early in
`setup()`, never `INPUT_PULLUP` and never left with a pad keeper; FR-49 reads each pad's IOMUXC setting at boot and refuses charger
arming on a mismatch.
**The EVM must not be connected until the CSV is amended and firmware with the new pin map is flashed** (fw v37 State 98 `4`
toggles pin 5 raw; study §2.8).

## F. Operating modes, transitions, R6/R7 design

### F.1 Images (registers, G.1) and symbols

- **Regen image:** VINDPM 19.0 V, IINDPM 1.70 A (clamped by the pin to 1.33-1.76 A), **ICHG 3.10 A** (conditional on T-E-11
  and T-B-19; 2.50 A until then, with the H.7 margin stated for both), EN_CHG 1.
- **Raised image (inside an FC window, T3):** IINDPM 1.70 A, ICHG 3.10 A, VINDPM_STAGE1 **18.2 V**, ratcheted to 19.0 V once
  V-MOT is above it (T3).
- **FC image:** VINDPM 14.5 V, IINDPM = governor value <= 0.90 A (G.1; the window cap is in stack power against the H-20
  P_MAX, H.12), ICHG 1.60 A, EN_CHG 1.
- Switch vector: FC_REG, BT_REG, FC_BUS, BT_BUS, MOT_PWR, REGEN, FC_CHARGE, BT_SEQ.
- Hardware qualifiers present in every armed row: none (r9-1, 2026-11-12: ARM_OK is removed with U113; **superseded in r9:** ARM_OK (heartbeat)), (r9-3: FCI_OK and the U117 option are retired; **superseded in r9:** FCI_OK (= 1 unless U117 is fitted)).

### F.3 R7: concurrency, RT1987 ORing and the loop proof

**What the RT1987 datasheet says (DS-00 §17.6 p.16, EC p.7):** an enabled RT1987 regulates VIN - VOUT = VFWD (35 mV typ) while
I x RON < VFWD; "if VIN decreases (or VOUT increases) such that VIN - VOUT falls to less than VFWD, the ideal diode gate drive
will force the internal MOSFET off"; a fast comparator trips within tFRC (0.5 us typ) at VIN - VOUT < VFRC (-50 mV typ). All
three figures are typical only.

D-BC-FC (VIN = VBUS) and D-BC-RG (VIN = V-MOT) both drive VCHG-IN. In an FC window with MOT_PWR closed, D-MT-EN also feeds V-MOT
from VBUS, so the FC reaches the charger by two paths. When regen lifts V-MOT above VBUS:
1. D-MT-EN sees VIN - VOUT < 0 and blocks VBUS -> V-MOT;
2. VCHG-IN follows V-MOT (less the D-BC-RG drop); once VCHG-IN > VBUS - 35 mV, D-BC-FC's gate is forced off, and at -50 mV the
   fast comparator turns it off within about 0.5 us;
3. from then on the charger draws only from V-MOT, i.e. from the motor.

**The operator's understanding is correct**, with two qualifications: the cut-off happens within tens of mV of VBUS, not at a
margin, and every figure is typical only. T-B-12 measures the FC current into the charger as a function of V-MOT - VBUS.

**Consequence: the FC-window ceiling must rise during strong braking.** The FC image cannot balance the 3 -> 1 m/s, 12 A brake
(18.9 W peak): its input limit is 11.2 W and its ICHG limit 12.0 W worst case (H.7), so V-MOT would climb to the VESC cut
(21.35 V). The 2 -> 1 m/s brake (11.1 W) is marginal on the FC image (+0.8 %). So **H1 and the T3 raise cover both brakes:**
when H1 is HIGH with the FC image active, firmware writes the raised image from the pin-34 rising-edge interrupt (r9-1: FCCEIL is removed; **superseded in r9:** FCCEIL LOW first).
**r4 correction (finding fc-window-raise-ignores-governor-floor):** after H1 rises, RFC_OFF lifts the FC pin clamp, so until T3
lands the register IINDPM is the only absorption limit, and the governor writes IINDPM = min(0.90 A, G) with the window open down
to G = 0.30 A. Because G subtracts a 2 s peak-hold of traction current, IINDPM sits near 0.30 A exactly when a brake follows an
acceleration. Integrated over the 1.5 ms FR-07 latency from the H1 rise maximum 18.05 V at 0.4 mF (H.20): **IINDPM 0.30 A gives
20.72 V at 18.9 W and 21.43 V at 23 W (past the cut); IINDPM 0.90 A gives 18.91 V and 19.65 V** (0.97 mF: 19.21 / 19.54 V at
0.30 A, 18.43 / 18.76 V at 0.90 A). The r3 figures (18.5 V at 1.5 ms, 19.75 V for the 3 ms r0 budget) were wrong under any
model (the 3 ms value integrates to 19.62 V at 0.90 A). **Fix at the cause, the brake feed-forward (FR-41; r4, rewritten in r5).** Every motor command passes the single
`vesc.setCurrent()` chokepoint (ino ~13078-13106). **r5 (findings ff-brake-edge-clears-peakhold-on-ripple,
gov-cmd-proxy-abs-closes-window-on-brake, ff-iindpm-step-overlaps-traction-ocfc) corrects three defects of the r4 rule:** it fired on
any negative command (ripple, undershoot recovery and standstill dither cross zero routinely: fw v37 HIL 1x ripple 0.55-0.64 A, a
0.32 m/s undershoot below a 0.4 m/s brake target), it cleared the traction peak-hold on that edge and parked IINDPM at 0.90 A while
traction could return (aux 0.15 + 0.90 + 0.5 A = 1.55 A > OC_FC 1.4 A), and it stepped IINDPM to 0.90 A while bus-side traction was
still flowing (the drive law crosses zero as a ramp, DRIVE_CTRL_DD 0.214 A per m/s, and the VESC executes the reversal after one
781 us UART frame, the 2 ms motor channel hold and an unmeasured current-loop lag; a residual of > 0.16-0.25 A trips the FR-14(d)
1.20 A shed and > 0.36-0.45 A an OC_FC sample, H.21). The r5 rule:
1. **Qualified by magnitude, same tick, no duration test.** The feed-forward and the BRAKE state (G.1, FR-41) start on the tick a
   command drops below **-I_ff, I_ff = 1.0 A** (above the 0.64 A ripple; below the 8.6 A upper bound at which a brake makes more
   regen power, 16.5 W at 0.4 mF, than IINDPM = G >= 0.30 A absorbs before T3 lands, H.21(a); TODO(calibrate: T-G-02d)). An
   N-tick or V_rgn-rising qualifier was not adopted: it would delay the raise past the first 1.5 ms, the race the feed-forward
   exists to cover. Commands in (-I_ff, 0] change neither IINDPM nor the peak-hold, and the governor's command proxy is
   traction-only (max(0, I_cmd), FR-14(a)), so a light brake neither closes the window nor drives G negative.
2. **The negative command goes to the VESC unmodified on its normal tick** (no hold-off, no zero-command insertion, the drive law
   untouched). From the brake edge the 1 kHz timer domain (FR-45, r6; "the 1 kHz monitor" in r5) ramps IINDPM **measurement-gated**: IINDPM_next = min(0.90 A, IINDPM_now +
   (I_cap - m_ff - I_fc,raw)), with I_fc,raw the pin-40 INA253 sample, IINDPM_now the last read-back value and m_ff (provisional
   0.10 A, TODO(calibrate: T-F-04b, T-B-24)) covering one tick of traction decay, the INA253 error and the register-to-current
   latency; a step is written only when it grows by >= 50 mA (bounded traffic, FR-07). Because the charger draws <= IINDPM_now,
   I_fc stays <= I_cap - m_ff whatever the residual traction or the VESC lag: H.21(b) gives max I_fc 1.04-1.10 A for residual
   traction 0.30-0.65 A decaying over 2-10 ms. H1 can rise only after bus-side traction has reversed (V-MOT must climb ~2 V above
   VBUS, >= 0.74 ms at 18.9 W, 0.4 mF), and by then the rule has reached 0.85-0.90 A, above the race floor (0.448 A at 18.9 W,
   0.706 A at 23 W, 0.4 mF, H.20). If I_fc,raw exceeds I_cap - m_ff while a step is in flight, IINDPM is written back to G the same
   tick (queue head), ahead of the FR-14(d) shed, so a near-miss costs harvest rate, not brake absorption.
3. **The traction peak-hold is never cleared on the brake edge**; it decays only after the command has been <= 0 for its full 2 s
   hold time, so G keeps subtracting it through and after the brake.
4. **The chokepoint is symmetric (brake-to-traction reversal).** While a window is open and the written IINDPM exceeds G (G computed
   from the retained peak-hold and the proxy of the pending positive command), a positive command is not released: the chokepoint
   sends 0 A (never the stale negative command) and posts IINDPM = min(0.90 A, G) at the queue head; the positive command goes out
   when that write is ACKed and read back. With no ACK within 1 ms, P5 LOW first (hard inhibit), T5 starts, then the command is
   released. The hold is <= ~1 ms and leaves the drive law and its gains untouched (unlike a slew limit, it does not reshape the
   drive-law output); the FR-14(b) timeout slew limit stays for its own readiness-failure case only. The BQ25798 IINDPM step-down
   settling after the ACK is not in SLUSDV2C: T-B-24 measures it and, if it exceeds ~1 ms, the measured value is added to the hold.
5. **Reversal headroom (BRAKE-exit close only; r6, finding ff-headroom-admission-contradicts-single-g-test).** Admission and normal
   close use only the F.4 test G. The headroom test is evaluated only when a qualified feed-forward has raised IINDPM above G, i.e. in
   BRAKE and at BRAKE exit: if aux + IINDPM_written + max(I_trac,peak, I_cmd-proxy) + I_ripple > I_cap at BRAKE exit, the window
   closes through T5 (IINDPM_written <= 0.90 A, the value the measurement-gated ramp actually reached). The feed-forward still fires
   whatever the result (brake safety first). With aux 0.15 A and IINDPM_written 0.90 A it passes only for peak-hold + ripple
   <= 0.15 A (H.21(c)), so a window with traction in its last 2 s closes after a qualified brake; the step-4 gate is the backstop, not
   the only protection. **It is not an admission term:** at admission and under normal governing IINDPM = min(0.90 A, G) already
   bounds aux + charger + traction + ripple to I_cap - margin, so a separate headroom term would protect nothing and would remove FC
   charging from cruise (the r5 wording "is admitted, and kept open after a feed-forward, only while ..." could be read as an
   admission rule; it is withdrawn). Host tests pin the choice (FR-22).

The feed-forward values are FC-image values (r9-1: FCCEIL, the blank and I-7 are removed; **superseded in r9:** so FCCEIL stays HIGH legitimately (no blank, I-7 intact)); while H1 = 0 the FC pin clamp
(0.65-0.95 A) still bounds the charger's FC draw. The r4 sentence "the traction load is zero, so the OC_FC/P_MAX margin is not
consumed" was true only with the motor current already at zero and is deleted. T3 keeps its H1 trigger and staging. **Backstop:** the
0.30 A window floor stays, on the recorded assumption that every regen path passes the chokepoint (host test: `vesc.setCurrent`
and any brake call appear only there; bench: no VESC-autonomous braking in T-E-03/T-G-01). If that assumption fails, the window
close threshold becomes G < I_floor + H_adm with I_floor = (P_brake,max / 18.05 V - (20.5 - 18.05) x C_VMOT,min / 1.5 ms) / 0.88
= 0.45 A at 18.9 W / 0.71 A at 23 W, 0.4 mF (H.20), re-derived from the T-E-04 capacitance. Once raised, VINDPM holds V-MOT at
18.2 V (stage 1) and then 19.0 V, and the input capability (20.8 W stage 1, 21.8 W at 19.0 V, H.7) covers 18.9 W.

**The unload transient of the raise (T-B-12):** VINDPM written above the present V-MOT makes the charger cut its draw while its
VINDPM loop settles, so V-MOT climbs at the full regen current (2.6 V/ms at 0.4 mF). The r0 single block (VINDPM 19.0 V before
IINDPM) left 1.97 V = 0.74 ms of headroom for the loop to reload; the staged r1 raise (IINDPM, ICHG, then VINDPM 18.2 V, whose
-2 % minimum clears the H1 fall maximum 17.76 V so H1 never drops while holding) leaves 2.79 V = 1.06 ms at 0.4 mF and 2.58 ms
at 0.97 mF. The BQ25798 VINDPM loop response is not specified; T-B-12 measures the V-MOT peak with a current source into
0.4/0.97 mF. **r2 (finding warm-response-pass-criteria-inconsistent):** T-B-09, T-B-10 and T-B-12 now share one budget,
t_d + tau <= (20.5 V - VINDPM_max(image) - I_regen,pk x R_PATH_RG,max) x C_VMOT / I_regen,pk with I_regen,pk = 1.1 A and t_d
counted from V-MOT crossing VINDPM_min. **r3 (finding input-path-ir-drop-omitted):** VINDPM regulates the BQ25798 VBUS pin, and
V-MOT sits higher by the input current times R_PATH_RG = 0.12-0.19 ohm (D-BC-RG RON, MB VCHG-IN copper and vias, CR copper, eFuse,
W1/W2, EVM R2, JP3, ground return; H.19), so the budget is **0.33 ms (0.4 mF) / 0.80 ms (0.97 mF) in regen-armed cruise** (r2
without R_path: 0.41 / 0.99 ms) and 0.63 / 1.52 ms for the raised stage 1 (r2: 0.70 / 1.71 ms). The primary pass criterion of all
three is the measured V-MOT peak <= 20.5 V on a current source into the T-E-04 capacitance **through a physical series resistor
equal to R_path,max (0.19 ohm) between the source node and EVM J1**, scored at the source side; the stiff voltage step stays only
as a diagnostic. T-F-13 measures R_path on the board and feeds it back into `r3_calc.py`.

**Why the raised ceiling cannot load the FC:** it is applied only while H1 AND RGN = 1, i.e. V-MOT > 1.089 x VBUS with
D-BC-RG commanded on, where D-BC-FC and D-MT-EN are reverse-biased and VCHG-IN follows V-MOT. (**superseded in r9:** If V-MOT falls back (H1 -> 0)
before firmware restores the FC image, the blank (`(UVB AND FCCEIL) OR (H1 AND RGN)` = 0) stops the converter in hardware.
With REGEN LOW (State 98 `J`, REGEN 0) H1 no longer bypasses the UVB shed or the ceiling blank (r2, T-F-09).) The normal end of a burst is slow: VINDPM holds V-MOT while regen fades, then V-MOT
decays at 14-20 V/s (VESC housekeeping, regen_dynamics §1.1). The only fast case is an abrupt VESC stop with the raised image
active: V-MOT falls at up to 4.4 V/ms (1.76 A into 0.4 mF) and H1 falls (r9-1: the bounds are those of the next paragraph; **superseded in r9:** the blank removes the converter within the inhibit
latency, and the FC carries at most one pulse of <= 1.76 A for that latency (H.13 allowance 157-173 us at 1.80 A before
D-MT-EN conducts; T-B-06 measures the latency)). A pulse that coincides with a 1 kHz OC_FC sample can latch OC_FC: a nuisance
State 99, safe (J.2 item 5).

**r9-1 (2026-11-12): the hardware blank is removed.** GATE = H1U OR FCCP and RFC_OFF = FCCN OR H1U: inside a window FCCP keeps the converter released whatever H1 does, so a raised image after H1 falls is no longer stopped in hardware. The bounds are: RFC_OFF falls with H1U, and Q202 restores the FC clamp (0.65-0.95 A) if the BQ25798 re-reads the pin (T-B-07); VINDPM 18.2 V above the bus; the firmware T4 restore, posted at the queue head by the pin-34 falling edge (FR-07, firmware-rules decision 3a); OC_FC 1.4 A (single sample, a nuisance State 99). T3 requires REGEN read back HIGH, and outside State 98 FR-49 refuses FCC HIGH with REGEN LOW (decision 3b), so the REGEN-LOW brake case above (the r2 hazard) is reachable only in State 98 or through a D-BC-RG OTP latch with its EN HIGH; RFC_OFF option (b) accepts it (J.1 item 22). The paragraph above is history where it names H1 AND RGN, FCCEIL and the blank (J.1 item 23).

**Loop impossibility in the concurrent mode (proof).** A circular charging loop needs pack energy to reach the charger input.
From the `.sch` net list, the pack (VBT) connects to: REG-BT/L-BT/SNS-BT (-> VOUT-BT -> SNS-BT -> VBUS-BT -> **D-BT-EN** -> VBUS),
the LM1084 (-> 5 V logic only), BAL BQ29200 (cell taps only) and D-BT-SQ (VCHG -> VBT only, TRCB blocks VBT -> VCHG). The only
pack -> VBUS element is therefore D-BT-EN, including the TPS61288 body-diode passthrough, which also flows through SNS-BT and
D-BT-EN. In the concurrent mode BT_BUS is LOW, and a disabled RT1987 "completely isolates VIN and VOUT" (DS-00 §17 p.14). The
charger input energy is then FC energy (VBUS via D-BC-FC, or VBUS -> D-MT-EN -> V-MOT -> D-BC-RG) or motor energy (V-MOT via
D-BC-RG); neither contains pack energy, so no loop exists whatever REGEN, FCC, H1 or the registers do. (**superseded in r9:** Hardware enforcement:
H2c needs **BTB_OFF** (the D-BT-EN EN net below 0.39-0.44 V, under the RT1987's own VEN_F minimum 0.6 V, so no EN level that can
leave D-BT-EN conducting reads as off) **and** BT_OK (measured BT boost current < 0.06-0.34 A).) Firmware enforcement: I-9 (the
FCC and BTB EN nets are never HIGH together; the BT_BUS setter refuses while FCC is HIGH and the FCC setter refuses while BTB is
HIGH), backed by the existing single-sample `FAULT_SWITCH_CONFLICT`. (**superseded in r9:** **Residual (R8, accepted):** a shorted D-BT-EN passing less
than the BT_OK threshold (and less than the firmware floor + margin trip, about 0.12 A) sustains a loop bounded by that current
for the window duration.) During a brake in the window the FC path is reverse-biased, so a shorted D-BT-EN cannot feed the
charger through D-BC-FC while V-MOT > VBUS (**superseded in r9:** ; the C7 qualifier (`NOT FCC` in H1q) keeps H1 from bypassing H2c). **r4 (finding
fr11-trips-on-concurrent-regen):** FR-11's power balance cannot run during a brake or under traction (the motor feeds the charger
and the FC carries traction), so it is one-sided and evaluated only in quiet intervals (**superseded in r9:** ; during a brake the loop barrier is
BTB_OFF, BT_OK, FR-10 and FR-34/FR-38, which sense the pack path itself, plus, in the raised region, the reverse-biased D-BC-FC.
A sub-BT_OK leak during a brake or cruise is caught only by FR-10 (R8 residual, J.1)). The r9-1 paragraph below states the live barrier.

**r9-1 (2026-11-12): no hardware enforcement remains in the concurrent mode.** BTB_OFF (U115), BT_OK (U104) and the C7 qualifier (NOT FCC in H1q) are removed. The proof above (BT_BUS LOW isolates the pack) holds as stated, but BT_BUS LOW is now enforced by firmware only: I-9 (both setters refuse), the single-sample `FAULT_SWITCH_CONFLICT` as the backstop, and the R5 watchdog for a hang (G.3). A shorted D-BT-EN in a window is caught only by the firmware I_BT floor + margin trip, FR-10 and FR-11 in quiet intervals; FR-34 is removed with BT_OK, so the R8 residual widens to the firmware trip level (J.1 items 1 and 23). During a brake in a window the reverse-biased D-BC-FC still keeps a shorted D-BT-EN from feeding the charger while V-MOT > VBUS. The hardware sentences above that name BTB_OFF, BT_OK, H2c, H1q and FR-34 are history.
