### F.4 R6: purge scheduler and pre-emption

**Prediction source.** The H-20 controller purges on its own timer. The 22 Pi bags show a period of **10.34 s**, a depth to
about 1.8-2.3 V and a duration of 100-140 ms (`docs/reviews/fw36_regen_2026-11-04/README.md` §2; 50 Hz data at low FC load, so
+-20 ms per edge). The brochure (`references/H20-Small-Stacks-Brochure.pdf`) gives no purge interval. Whether the interval
depends on stack load is unknown, and an FC window roughly doubles the stack power: T-E-01 measures >= 20 intervals at window
load. fw v30 already detects a purge-class dip on FC_VOLTAGE (pin 24) at 1 kHz (`docs/fw30_fc_purge_uv.md` §5). The scheduler
(FR-15):
1. timestamps each purge onset as the first 1 kHz sample with V_fc below `PURGE_DETECT_V` (6.0 V, between the loaded knee about
   7.8 V and the purge floor, TODO(calibrate: T-E-01)) after a fall of more than 1 V within 20 ms;
2. predicts the next onset as last onset + median of the last 5 intervals (per load bin if T-E-01 shows load dependence);
3. declares the schedule **locked** after 3 consecutive intervals whose **prediction error** (onset - t_pred, against the model
   actually in use) lies inside the asymmetric band [-`PURGE_EARLY_MAX`, +`PURGE_LATE_MAX`], and unlocks **only on checks that
   compare the model with observed onsets**: a prediction error outside that band or a missed prediction. **r4 (finding
   purge-lock-tolerance-exceeds-tlead):** the r3 symmetric +-100 ms `PURGE_JITTER_MAX` admitted onsets up to 100 ms early as "in
   tolerance", while an onset earlier than ~79 ms before t_pred already beats the battery path (A + B + D wait + 2 x tD_ON + tON
   = 21.4 ms after window close at T_LEAD 100 ms, r6 timing), a certain State 99. Now **`PURGE_EARLY_MAX` = T_LEAD - T_HANDOFF_MAX - T_MARGIN
   = 100 - 27.4 - 17.6 = 55 ms** (T_HANDOFF_MAX = t_exec 4.0 ms + tD_ON,max 16 ms + tON 1.4 ms + step-E dwell and check 6 ms,
   H.20; **r6, finding loop-budget-5ms-breaks-1ms-tick-deadlines: t_exec = T_TICK_MAX (step A) + 2 ms (the D wait, inside which the
   B/C writes run) + T_TICK_MAX (the step-D boundary) = 4.0 ms with the 1 ms timer domain of FR-45; r5's 3.8 ms summed the B write
   serially and counted no boundary latency, and a 5 ms `loop()` tick would have made t_exec ~12 ms; the margin goes 17.8 -> 17.6 ms
   so PURGE_EARLY_MAX stays 55 ms, H.22(f)**), enforced by a `static_assert` built on `RT1987_T_D_ON_MS`, `T_TICK_MAX_MS` (r6) and the T_LEAD constant, so a longer tD_ON (T-E-06) or tON
   (lever 3(i)) breaks the build or shrinks the early tolerance automatically; an early error beyond it unlocks **and logs a
   near-miss whether or not a window was open**. `PURGE_LATE_MAX` stays 100 ms (TODO(calibrate: T-E-01)): a late onset costs
   duty, never safety. The same band applies to the charge-based and load-bin models, whose error is also onset - t_pred. **r3 (finding scheduler-unlock-on-load-starves-windows):** the r2 unlock on any uncommanded
   stack-load change > 0.3 A is deleted: outside windows the FC current follows traction through the share loop, so on UDDS and
   full-scale FTP-75 it would unlock on most accelerations and seldom stay locked for the 31 s relock. Instead the load enters
   the predictor, chosen by T-E-01 (>= 20 intervals with windows opened mid-interval and with traction-like swings, interval
   fitted against elapsed time, integrated stack charge and load bin):
   - **time-based** (load-independent within the r4 band [-PURGE_EARLY_MAX, +PURGE_LATE_MAX]): t_pred = last onset + median interval; load is ignored;
   - **charge-based:** t_pred from the remaining coulombs (median Q per interval - Q since the last onset), with window rule (b)
     projecting that remainder at the worst-case window rate I_cap (1.20 A bus-equivalent, converted to stack current), so the
     window's own load cannot pull the onset inside T_LEAD;
   - **load-bin based:** on a bin change switch to that bin's median; while moving between bins use the shortest median among
     the bins crossed since the last onset; unlock only if a bin has fewer than 3 observed intervals.
   A missed prediction within 2 s of a load change > 0.3 A is counted separately (telemetry), so T-E-01 / T-G-04 can tell
   whether the chosen model holds; load steps caused by a window opening or closing stay exempt (r2);
4. (r9-4, 2026-11-12: withdrawn with the F24 `PURGE_SENSE` option and T-E-02; V_fc stays the onset source; **superseded in r9:** optionally uses the purge-valve tap (T-E-02) as the onset source instead of V_fc.)

**Window rules (r2, findings window-reopen-rule-limits-fc-duty and fc-window-budget-vs-h20-pmax).** A window opens when all of
these hold: (a) the schedule is locked; (b) t_pred - now >= T_LEAD + T_WIN_MIN, where T_WIN_MIN covers T2 entry + T5 exit + the
BT_BUS close transient settle (placeholder 1 s, TODO(calibrate: T-F-08 / T-E-06)); windows may therefore re-open mid-interval,
not only after a purge; (c) V_fc has been above `V_FC_ARM_THRESH` 7.0 V for 200 ms since the last purge end; (d) the admission
test G >= 0.30 A + H_adm (below); (e) no regen burst in progress (H1 rb LOW); (f) T-E-12's readiness margin is known; (g) the
churn bound allows it: at most N_open = 3 window entries per purge interval (TODO(calibrate: T-F-08)), and after a close for
traction or governor reasons 0.5 s with no setpoint increase and G above the open threshold; **(i) (r4, R5 gate) the MCU watchdog
is fitted, the R5 build flag is set (T-W-01a passed; r9-6, 2026-11-12, D2-1: the same flag gates every charger arming, FR-05) and the full T-W-01 with the T-D-14 purge cases has passed (a second build flag set only after that test, reported in telemetry); (j) (r4) `soft_layer_missing` is
clear and no charger trip latch stands; (h) (r3, finding
window-ignores-ems-intent-and-termination) the Pi asks for charge: `charge_goal` > 0.05 (the existing v4 command field and the
fw v32a threshold; no protocol change) and the `chgFull` latch is clear.** `chgFull` sets when REG1C CHG_STAT reads 111b
(termination done; also 110b if TOPOFF_TMR is ever made non-zero, SLUSDV2C §7.3.9.1) and clears only when the pack voltage
falls below VREG - VRECHG (200 mV default, §7.3.9.1 / REG0A; BQ25798 VBAT ADC primary, pin-25 V_batt cross-check), when
`charge_goal` goes from <= 0.05 to > 0.05 (the Pi's deliberate re-request), or at Run exit. There is **no IBAT admission
term** (before a window the charger is only regen-armed and IBAT is ~0, so such a term would deadlock, as the Ag105 bootstrap
did) and **CV (100b) does not close a window** (CV taper is where the last part of a 2S charge goes in; closing there would make
R1's FC charging unreachable near the top of the pack). Whether an IINDPM-governed window ever reaches 111b is open (termination
is declared only outside DPM, §7.3.9.1): T-B-15 decides; if not, a firmware CV-taper termination sets `chgFull` after IBAT
< ITERM + 40 mA for 10 s with CHG_STAT = 100b (TODO(calibrate: T-B-15)). A window **overrides the EMS share command** (the
latch owns BT_BUS LOW, FC_BUS HIGH); the Pi models it as share = 1.0, reported in telemetry (FR-20).

**One admission/close test** (the same expression in both places, in stack power): G = I_cap - I_aux,meas - max(I_trac,peak,
I_cmd-proxy) - I_ripple - margin, with I_cap = min(OC_FC margin 1.20 A, (P_MAX,bus - 1.0 W) / V_bus) = 1.200 A at 15.2 V
(H.12: the H-20 brochure P_MAX 23.416 W stack is 19.90 W bus at ETA_BOOST 0.85, i.e. 1.25 A at 15.95 V and 1.31 A at the loaded
15.2 V bus, so OC_FC 1.4 A sits above the characterised stack range). Open only if G >= 0.30 A + H_adm (H_adm about 0.10 A,
TODO(calibrate: T-F-04b)); close if G < 0.30 A; the governor writes IINDPM = min(0.90 A, G). **r6 (finding
ff-headroom-admission-contradicts-single-g-test): G is the only admission test.** No headroom term is needed at admission, because
IINDPM = min(0.90 A, G) already bounds aux + charger + traction + ripple to I_cap - margin; the only other close predicate tied to
the charger limit is the FR-41(viii) reversal-headroom close at BRAKE exit (F.3 item 5), which applies only after a feed-forward
has raised IINDPM above G. Using max(peak-hold, commanded
proxy) closes the window before a commanded step lands; FR-14(b) still holds the setpoint. **r5 (finding
gov-cmd-proxy-abs-closes-window-on-brake): the proxy is traction-only, I_cmd-proxy = max(0, I_cmd) x k_proxy / eta** (the r4
\|I_cmd\| counted a 12 A brake as ~13.6 A of FC load, so G went to about -12.6 A, every brake closed the window and the R7
concurrent mode was unreachable; during a brake V-MOT is above VBUS, D-MT-EN and D-BC-FC are reverse-biased and the motor draws
no FC current). k_proxy is duty-weighted (~V_bemf/V_bus, i.e. bus-side, not motor-side current), calibrated in T-F-04b including
a standstill launch. **Precedence (r5):** the FR-41 BRAKE state (entered at a command below -I_ff, left after the command has
been >= 0 for one 20 ms governor slot with H1 rb LOW) overrides this test: inside it the G-based close is suspended and no
IINDPM below the feed-forward value is written; **every non-G close stays live in BRAKE** (the purge pre-emption at
t_pred - T_LEAD, the FR-42 backstop, FR-14(d) raw I_fc > 1.20 A -> P5 LOW, charge_goal, `chgFull`, `FC_CHG_MAX_MS`, T7 and every
latch), and FR-14(d) and the purge pre-emption override BRAKE. On BRAKE exit G is re-seeded with the retained peak-hold, and a
positive command passes the FR-41 step-4 gate before IINDPM falls below 0.90 A. The r1 separate 1.30 A sum is
retired (it admitted windows the governor closed on its first update). A Pi-commanded window IINDPM ceiling (so the EMS can
trade charge rate against the convex H2 cost near P_MAX) is a **protocol extension, flagged, not part of v5** (FR-32).

The window closes at `t_pred - T_LEAD`, on G < 0.30 A, on a traction-demand increase (the setpoint hold of FR-14), **when
`charge_goal` drops to <= 0.05 (same tick), when `chgFull` sets (within one 20 ms poll, before EN_CHG is cleared per T-B-15),
when the fw v32a single-window cap `FC_CHG_MAX_MS` expires (followed by `FC_CHG_COOLDOWN_MS`; restored in r3 as a backstop next
to the purge pre-emption)**, operator, or Run exit; every close goes through T5. This replaces the fw v30 30 s FC-only lockout for FC windows (which "in practice refuses charge windows outright" on a
running stack, study §3.4); the lockout stays in force for share-loop FC-only selections outside windows.

**Lead time (H.8):**

| Item | Allowance |
|---|---|
| Step-A latency: one timer-domain tick T_TICK_MAX + FC_CHARGE LOW (P5 stays HIGH; r6, FR-45; r9-7: FCCEIL removed) | 1.0 ms |
| Charger shed settle before BT_BUS (bus recovery); the VINDPM 19.0 V write + read-back (0.8 ms at 100 kHz) runs inside it (r6) | 2.0 ms |
| Step-D boundary latency: one more timer-domain tick T_TICK_MAX (r6) | 1.0 ms |
| RT1987 D-BT-EN tD_ON (8 ms typ, no max given) | 16.0 ms (2x) |
| Soft-start to the pre-biased bus (tON/0.8 at 16 V) | 1.4 ms |
| Readiness check (EN high, FCC read-back LOW, optional VBUS-BT ADC) | 1.0 ms |
| Purge onset jitter (unmeasured; 3 x the 20 ms bag resolution) | 60.0 ms |
| Margin | 17.6 ms (r6; 17.8 in r5) |
| **T_LEAD** | **100 ms** |

Window closed per cycle at the minimum: 100 ms lead + 100-140 ms purge + 230 ms recovery and re-open = 430-470 ms of 10.34 s,
so **95.5-95.8 % is an upper bound on the FC-charge duty** (uninterrupted admission: standstill or a steady load inside G). The
expected duty on ftp75c/UDDS comes from the FR-21 HIL scheduler and purge model and is measured in T-G-04 (pass threshold set
by the operator). The duty also depends on the scheduler's locked fraction, which T-G-04 scores on UDDS and full-scale FTP-75
(r3). **T_LEAD sizing (r3, finding early-purge-fc-ridethrough-infeasible):** the 60 ms jitter line is a placeholder. Because a
missed hand-off can end in State 99 (r5: when the post-shed bus load is above the rescue bound, below), T-E-01 reports the empirical distribution of (onset - t_pred) at window load, and T_LEAD
is the smallest value for which P(onset < t_pred - T_LEAD + t_D,exec + tD_ON,max + tON) x P(rescue fails | load bin, T-E-01/T-F-07, r5) x the purge rate (~350 per hour) x the
window fraction stays below the operator-set **maximum State-99 rate per hour of window time** (registry ceiling, T-E-01; an
empirical quantile, or a fitted distribution while fewer than ~100 intervals exist). T-E-06 supplies tD_ON,max (if it exceeds
16 ms, T_LEAD grows by the excess) and T-G-04 counts actual early-purge State 99s against the ceiling. **r4:** the 60 ms jitter
line and `PURGE_EARLY_MAX` are one quantity: T-E-01 passes when the early-side quantile of (onset - t_pred) at the operator's
State-99 ceiling is <= `PURGE_EARLY_MAX`; if the measured tail does not fit, T_LEAD rises (145 ms keeps a 100 ms early tolerance,
~0.4 % duty, H.20) rather than tightening the lock until windows never lock.

**What the BT_BUS close achieves before the purge (RT1987 two-state analysis).** With the charger shed, the FC-only bus rises
toward the FC boost's aux-load point, and D-BT-EN sees VIN - VOUT = V0_bt - V_bus. The only measured BT-node data is
bench-supply: dV0 = +0.05 V with the FC side high, envelope +-0.10 V (`controller_design/system_model.md`), so
VIN - VOUT ≈ -0.05 + 0.3 x 0.12 + 0.035 ≈ +0.02 V nominal and about -0.03 V at the envelope edge. Three cases:
- **VIN - VOUT < VFRC (-50 mV) at enable:** the RT1987 does not turn on (TRCB, DS-00 §17.4) and "auto-restarts without
  soft-start at fault removal" (Table 1); whether tD_ON repeats on that restart is not stated. Design rule: avoid it,
  V0_bt - V_bus(FC-only, aux, charger shed) >= -20 mV, measured in **T-E-12**; fallback: raise V0_bt by 0.1-0.2 V with the BT
  TPS61288 FB divider (inside the share loop's +-0.40 V dV0 budget, re-run CAL-1).
- **-50 mV to +35 mV:** enabled, soft-start completes, the gate servo holds the MOSFET off (VIN - VOUT < VFWD, §17.6). At the
  purge the bus falls and the servo opens the gate: the hand-off happens through the ideal-diode ORing, with no tD_ON. The servo
  response "accommodates relatively slow changes" and is unspecified: **T-E-06** measures the crossing-to-conduction delay
  (pass <= 0.5 ms, about 0.1-1.3 V of sag at 0.2-2.6 V/ms).
- **> +35 mV:** D-BT-EN conducts during its soft-start: an inrush pulse (H.6) of C_eff x 12 V/ms + I_load, clamped at ISCP
  8.5 A, for delta/12 V/ms (25 us at 0.3 V), which a 1 kHz OC_BT sample (3.0 A, single sample, ino 7430) can catch with a
  probability of roughly the pulse width per ms (2.5-4 % at 0.3 V).

**Lever for the inrush amplitude (operator ruling, open; T-F-08 decides whether it is needed):** (i) raise C-DC4 to 68 nF
(slew 0.95 V/ms, peak <= 0.96 A + load at 0.97 mF, no SCP; but tON 13.5 ms, so T_LEAD, `RT1987_T_D_ON_MS` and the
static_assert'ed blanking family must be re-derived and early-purge recovery becomes too slow); or (ii) give OC_BT a
persistence requirement (2 consecutive samples) only in a window from the BT_BUS EN edge + tD_ON,min to tD_ON,max + tON + 1 ms,
justified by the RT1987's own SCP covering a true short inside soft-start (§17.5). The same transient already exists on every
share-loop/selector BT re-entry; that class is equally unquantified today.

**Pre-emption sequence (canonical, loop-safe; r2: P5 stays HIGH).** Dropping P5 is redundant once FCC is LOW: FCC LOW alone
forces FCCP = 0 within the U120 FCC_ON propagation delay (2-4 us, r6; gate delays in r5; r9-1: was H2c), and GATE then needs H1U, which proves V-MOT > 1.089 x VBUS with the bus healthy (r9-1: no REGEN term; REGEN stays HIGH on this path), so neither D-BC-FC nor
D-MT-EN can conduct. The state reached is exactly regen-armed cruise (P5 HIGH, BT_BUS HIGH, GATE = H1U, VINDPM 19.0 V). Keeping
P5 HIGH keeps a brake in progress absorbed, above or below H1 (findings preempt-p5-low-drops-brake-absorption and
preempt-drops-subh1-regen: with the r1 P5 LOW, a sub-H1 brake above ~0.09-0.21 A climbed at I/C to the VESC cut during the
~27 ms P5-LOW interval). At `t_pred - T_LEAD`:

| # | Action | Effect / timing |
|---|---|---|
| A | FC_CHARGE LOW (r9-7: FCCEIL removed; **superseded in r9:** "and FCCEIL LOW in the same tick"); **P5 stays HIGH** | **FCC net LOW -> FCCP = 0 within 2-4 us (U120, r6; r9-1: was H2c)**; GATE = H1U. No brake: the converter stops and the up-to-0.90 A charger load leaves the FC-only bus. Sub-H1 brake: V-MOT rises to the H1 rise (<= 18.05 V, > 3.3 V below the cut) and the converter resumes, absorbing from the motor only. VCHG-IN stays warm through REGEN (r9-7: I-7 withdrawn with FCCEIL) |
| B | **H1 rb LOW:** write VINDPM 19.0 V and read it back (<= 0.8 ms). **H1 rb HIGH** (a brake above H1, the former raised-burst variant): the staged T3 path instead (IINDPM 1.70 A, then ICHG 3.10 A + VINDPM 18.2 V, ratcheted to 19.0 V later), which avoids the unload transient (F.3) | Between A and B the FC image (VINDPM 14.5 V) runs under H1U (r9-1; was H1q) with BT_BUS still LOW: it can only chatter H1 with motor energy, never form a loop. **Failure branch:** on NACK or read-back failure (or a read-back mismatch), P5 LOW (the only P5-LOW case of the pre-emption), set `chg_flags.soft_layer_missing`, still continue to D (the purge has priority) and keep P5 LOW until a verified image is in place; this degraded branch keeps the r1 exposure of a sub-H1 brake (J.2). **r4 (findings i2-vs-preempt-stepb-failure-branch, preempt-vindpm-failure-blocks-step-d):** this branch reaches D through the I-2 **barrier** clause (P5 LOW >= 1 ms, FCC read back LOW; r9-7: the pin-7 /CE sense is removed, so the barrier rests on the FCC read-back and the H1 . UVB release term, TODO(verify: r9 audit, F.3)), not through the VINDPM read-back. If FR-08(b) trips (the I2C latch trip, r9-7; **superseded in r9:** "If the /CE sense reads LOW instead, FR-08(b) trips") (P5, QUAL, REGEN, FCC LOW) and D proceeds on the REGEN read-back LOW for >= the D-BC-RG turn-off time + FCC read-back LOW; a charger trip latch is not State 99 and the purge still has priority. While `soft_layer_missing` stands: P5 stays LOW, QUAL stays LOW, T2 and new windows are refused, until a verified VINDPM >= 18.2 V image and the I-3 read-back |
| C | Write IINDPM 1.70 A and ICHG 3.10 A, read back | regen image complete (r9-7: I-7 withdrawn with FCCEIL) |
| D | At **max(A + 2 ms, P5-LOW edge + 1 ms)** (r4; bus recovery, and the barrier dwell on the failure branch), BT_BUS HIGH through the pre-emption path once **the step-B VINDPM read-back is verified OR the I-2 barrier is proven** (r4): bypasses `SHARE_SELECTOR_DWELL_MS` and every deferral except FR-26 / `busHotPlugUnsafe()` | the BT_BUS setter refuses while FCC reads HIGH (I-9); shrinks the BT close transient (H.6). A late failure detection (up to the 0.5-0.8 ms transaction cap) can push D past A + 2 ms; that delay counts against the T_LEAD readiness budget (inside T_HANDOFF_MAX) |
| E | Readiness: EN HIGH for >= tD_ON,max (T-E-06) + tON + 5 ms; FCC read-back LOW; optional VBUS-BT - VBUS >= -20 mV | **no requirement that I_batt rises before the purge** (see the two-state analysis). **r3:** once step D has run, BT_BUS EN is never dropped again: if readiness is missed by `t_pred - 40 ms`, the purge outcome is the battery hand-off if t_EN + tD_ON,actual + tON < onset, else UV_BUS -> State 99; windows are abandoned until the next lock and the branch is logged (FR-16). If step D was **refused** (FCC read-back HIGH or `busHotPlugUnsafe()`), the outcome is a certain State 99 at the purge: the scheduler unlocks and T_LEAD steps up. **A VINDPM failure is not a refusal (r4):** it takes the barrier clause of I-2, keeps I-1's P5-LOW requirement on the close, and closes on time. FC_BUS is never opened by a pre-emption, but an FC-only bus has no source while the stack purges, so there is no ride-through |

**Topology invariant through the purge (r4, FR-15b, finding preempt-btbus-not-owned-through-purge).** After step E, T5 hands
switch ownership back to the share loop, whose fw v25 setpoint-latch BT cut (ino ~13561-13575: sp > DROOP_R_MAX and \|I_batt\| <=
0.5 A, with no purge or lockout term; `fcUvLockoutActive()` gates only the selector, ino 14119/14137) and r-based BT cut (ino
~14881-14895) would re-open BT_BUS on a Pi command of 0.9 or 1.0. After a pre-emption the battery usually sits in the RT1987
"enabled but blocking" state with I_batt ~ 0, so the guard is met, and the bus would be FC-only at the onset: a certain State 99
(campaign II already saw exact-1.0 commits, and FR-20 has the Pi model a window as share 1.0). **Rule: while FC_REG is HIGH, no
FC-only bus exists except inside a scheduler-owned charge window.** A predicate `fcPurgeExposure()` is TRUE when FC_REG is HIGH
and the scheduler is not locked, or when it is locked and the predicted onset is <= T_LEAD + T_WIN_MIN away; it stays TRUE from
then until the onset has been observed and V_fc has been above `V_FC_ARM_THRESH` for 200 ms; it is ORed with
`fcUvLockoutActive()`. While it is TRUE, every share-loop path that opens BT_BUS (the setpoint-latch BT entry, the r-based BT
cut, the selector FC arm, any load-guard or dark-channel BT cut) is **deferred, never executed and never timed out**, using the
existing `shareCutDeferredBT` semantics (the reference is clipped to DROOP_R_MAX and the r-path suppresses itself) and staying
off the shareSpCutBT/shareIsoBT ownership flags. **The pre-emption also covers any FC-only topology standing at t_pred - T_LEAD**
(a share-loop BT cut that was in place before the predicate went TRUE): BT_BUS is re-closed through the latch's guarded release
(V_bus >= `V_BUS_CHARGED_THRESH`, BT_REG HIGH, `busHotPlugUnsafe()` false) with the same dwell bypass, and logged. **Consequence
for the EMS (needs operator acceptance, J.2):** while the H-20 runs, the Pi's out-of-band FC-only command (> 0.85) is executed as
0.85 outside windows; FC-only operation exists only as a charge window, and FR-20 reports the override.

**Independent pre-emption backstop (r5, FR-42, finding preempt-deadline-outside-completion-token).** The RTWDOG (r9-6: the heartbeat is deleted; **superseded in r9:** "The heartbeat and the RTWDOG")
feed (FR-28) proves that the 1 kHz monitor completed, not that the mode manager progressed: a stalled pre-emption step machine (A-E),
a stalled scheduler or a logic deadlock in `chargerModeTick()`/`chargingControl()` would leave the window latch holding BT_BUS LOW
into the purge with both still fed, and the step-E `t_pred - 40 ms` check and the T10 deadline sit inside the same stalled code. With
a live MCU that ends in UV_BUS -> State 99 about 36 ms after onset (the controlled outcome F.4 already counts), not in the
frozen-MCU class, but it rests on correct mode-manager code. The backstop lives in the 1 kHz monitor and is itself a stage-mask term
of FR-28 ("backstop evaluated"); "mode manager progressed this tick" is **not** a mask term, because steps wait legitimately for many
ticks (the step-E dwell >= tD_ON,max + tON + 5 ms, the T1 REGN wait up to T_REGN_MAX) and a watchdog reset is the worse outcome
(an unordered teardown). (a) **Deadlines the mode manager cannot move:** at window open the monitor copies t_pred_frozen and
t_open into monitor-owned variables; a later scheduler update may move t_pred_frozen earlier, never later. (b) **Two triggers while
any FC-only topology stands** (BT_BUS EN LOW with FC_REG HIGH, by the window latch or under `fcPurgeExposure()`): now >=
t_pred_frozen - **T_BACKSTOP (85 ms)**, with T_BACKSTOP >= PURGE_EARLY_MAX + tD_ON,max + tON + t_barrier (1 ms) + t_exec = 77.4 ms
(r6: t_exec 4.0 ms) and < T_LEAD, enforced by a `static_assert` built on `RT1987_T_D_ON_MS` and `T_TICK_MAX_MS` (H.21(d), H.22(f):
the backstop's BT_BUS EN edge lands at t_pred - 80.0 ms against the latest workable t_pred - 72.4 ms); the backstop compare runs in
the FR-45 timer domain; or an age cap now - t_onset_frozen > median_frozen - T_BACKSTOP (the last observed onset and the median interval, both copied at
window open; covers a scheduler stalled with a stale t_pred; a now - t_open form would fire late for a window opened mid-interval); plus a maximum dwell constant per A-E and T10 step, compared with the step's entry
timestamp. (c) **Action = the same function** the pre-emption and T10 already call (`forcePreemptToBattery()`; no second
sequencing implementation): FC_CHARGE and P5 LOW in one tick (r9-7: FCCEIL removed) (I-4(a): inhibit-only, never gated by H1), the I-2 barrier
(P5 LOW >= 1 ms, FCC read back LOW; r9-7: /CE sense removed), then BT_BUS HIGH through the guarded release (FR-26 /
`busHotPlugUnsafe()`); a refused close takes a controlled State 99 before the onset. (d) Afterwards `CHG_MODE_STALL` latches,
windows are refused until reboot or operator acknowledgement, FR-16 logs it. (e) The RTWDOG feed still stops (r9-6; **superseded in r9:** "The heartbeat and the RTWDOG still stop") if the
backstop itself fails to execute (stage mask). Host tests and T-C-14 inject stalls at each step.

**Teensy hang inside a window (r4, findings hang-fc-window-r5-gates-r1, hang-fc-window-purge-reclose-death5).** With the MCU
hung in a window nothing in hardware stops the charger before the R5 reset (r9-6, 2026-11-12, D2-2: no hardware hang inhibit exists, so the converter keeps charging for at most t_WDT + 1 ms, J.2 item 69; **superseded in r9:** "the heartbeat drops /CE and holds ILIM_HIZ within TW_HB_MAX, but"); FC_BUS, MOT_PWR and FC_CHARGE stay HIGH and
BT_BUS stays LOW, and the purge timer keeps running. The next purge therefore collapses the FC-only bus (the paragraph below) with
nothing to latch State 99, and recovery is not supervised: if VBUS falls below the RT1987 UVLO (2.925 V typ, DS-00 §17.1) D-MT-EN
re-enables tD_ON (8 ms) after recovery with soft-start; if it stays above, the TRCB block holds V-MOT and re-enhances without
soft-start or SCP (§17.6, Table 1, §17.5) while the TPS61288 restarts from its VIN UVLO (1.9 V falling / 2.3 V rising, soft-start
3 ms, SLVSFP3C §8.3.2) into the drained V-MOT/VESC node. Since capture 11 D-MT-EN has 100 nF CSS and a re-enable onto a regulated
bus is the validated ~1 A / 30 ms connect class (`docs/boost-bringup-debug.md`), but a re-enable during the boost restart or the
TRCB re-enhancement is the class the 2026-08-03 doctrine refuses, and it would repeat at every purge for as long as the hang
lasts. **Design response:** (1) no FC window, attended or not, before **T-W-01** passes (window rule (i)); (2) the R5 watchdog
timeout is set below the minimum purge duration minus margin (**RTWDOG 50 ms against 100 ms**, G.3), so a hang that starts before
or during a purge resets the MCU, and the reset drops every EN (MOT_PWR, FC_BUS, FC_CHARGE, REGEN, BT_BUS) through the 10 kOhm
pull-downs before the stack recovers; recovery then always goes through the `setup()` low-voltage pre-charge (Death-5 doctrine),
and the event counts against the operator's State-99 ceiling; (3) the residual, a hang within ~t_WDT + T_LEAD of an onset (~1.5 %
of window hangs at a 10.34 s period), sees one frozen-MCU collapse before the reset, characterised on a bench FC emulator with a
spare boost (T-D-14), never on the vehicle; (4) T-D-02(a) on the vehicle checks only the hang -> watchdog-reset path (r9-6; **superseded in r9:** "hang -> heartbeat path") and ends the hang
at least T_LEAD + 50 ms before t_pred. An optional open-drain pull from ARM_OK on the MOT_PWR EN net was considered and not
adopted (it moves the hazard to MCU resume, L.4).

At the purge onset FR-16 records: the delay from the V_fc onset (or V_bus < V0_bt - 35 mV) to I_batt > floor, the V_bus
minimum, and the margin from step E to the onset. The r1 "raised-burst variant" is now the H1 rb HIGH branch of step B and needs
no separate exception. If UVB falls during steps A-D (an early purge in the same few ms), H1U drops (r9-1; was H1q) and a brake in progress is
cut: V-MOT climbs to the VESC cut (safe, harvest lost; J.2).

Re-open after the purge: the T2 sequence (F.5), warm (VCHG-IN held by REGEN).

**If a purge arrives early** (FR-17, r2).
- **Classification (finding early-purge-trigger-misattribution; r9-7):** an early purge is declared only on the V_fc onset detector. The H2c readback (pin 16) is removed with tap T14, so the r2 H2c-fall branch and the "unexplained permit drop" class are withdrawn; whether a V_bus-sag branch (V_bus below 14.16 V with no V_fc onset) replaces them is TODO(design: r9 audit) (**superseded in r9:** "... or on an H2c readback fall with FCC, BTB, BT_OK rb, FCCEIL and H1 rb unchanged and V_bus (pin 26) below the UVB rise-band maximum 14.16 V or a V_fc onset within the same 5 ms. An H2c fall without either ... is an unexplained permit drop: the FR-08 safe-direction shed through T5 with normal readiness, no rescue predicate, no scheduler unlock, and a counter (T-C-11).")
**An FC-only bus has no source while the stack purges (r3; r5 restatement, finding purge-fc-only-ridethrough-bag-evidence).** In a
window the bus is FC-only by construction (I-9). The purge floor is ~1 V (`docs/fw30_fc_purge_uv.md` §1) to 1.8-2.3 V (bags), the
TPS61288 VIN UVLO falls at 1.9 V typ (SLVSFP3C §8.3.2), and the re-mined bags confirm the stack delivers nothing during the dip:
on all four onsets that started on an FC-only bus (sw 0x25: 10-25 21:09, 10-27 02:52, 10-30 00:56, 10-30 01:30) I_fc reads 0.00 A
at V_fc 1.8-2.4 V. **What the r3/r4 text got wrong is the consequence.** In the same four cases the fw v30 purge response raised
BT_BUS in the onset sample (sw 0x25 -> 0x27), I_batt rose to 0.02-0.03 A (the whole aux load), the V_bus minimum sample was
12.89-14.62 V, the bus was back at 15.93 V within <= 40 ms, and nothing latched: at aux load (~0.02 A, standstill, MOT_PWR closed)
a **reactive BT_BUS rescue** held the bus 4 times out of 4. That is outcome (a) below, which the H.8 0.2 V/ms sag floor (an
ESTIMATE) had declared impossible. The physics agrees: a rescue close survives a source-less bus load up to dV_SCP/(tD_ON,max + tON)
x C_eff = **0.065 A** at either C_VMOT (H.21(f)); a 0.02 A load would sag at 0.02-0.045 V/ms, a window load of ~1.05 A at 1.0-2.4 V/ms.
**r6 (finding purge-fc-only-ridethrough-bag-evidence-reopen): two parts of that reading are withdrawn.** The 0.02-0.03 A is I_batt
below the INA253 floor (~0.1 A, R8), so the sag rate derived from it is an I/C inference, not a measurement. And the bags' own V_bus
minima (12.89-14.62 V) put the rescue close at a 1.4-3.1 V delta, above the 1.11 / 2.56 V dV_SCP no-trip bound, yet nothing latched
(H.22(g)): either the dV_SCP / ISCP model is pessimistic or an SCP gap and retry happened unseen at 50 Hz. T-F-07b measures it at
1 kHz with a current probe before any constant is set from the bags.
**So the early-purge outcome depends on the bus load at the onset; it is not certainly a State 99.** At window load it remains
the expected outcome and is still unmeasured (the bags hold no window-load case, and the 10-27 00:52 UV_FC + UV_BUS latch bag starts
already latched, ec 9, ff 0x8140, so its load is unknown). The r3 sentence "every early purge inside a window ... is a State 99" and
the r2 outcome "(b) ride-through on the FC" are both withdrawn: there is no FC ride-through (the stack delivers 0 A), and there is
a load-dependent battery rescue. **Design consequence (r5):** step 2 sheds the bus to aux load (charger off **and the motor
command clamped to <= 0** for the purge), which is what moves the event into the rescue's range; `SAG_MIN_POST_ONSET` in FR-26 is
demoted from a fact to a provisional constant set by T-E-01; T_LEAD and the operator's State-99 ceiling are sized from (onset-error
tail) x P(rescue fails | load bin) measured in T-E-01/T-F-07, never from a certainty or from an FC ride-through probability.
**r6:** the r5 predicate could never admit (its 0.2 V/ms floor alone predicted a 3.48 V drop, so the left side was <= 12.52 V
against a right side of 13.44 V at 0.4 mF and 14.89 V at 0.97 mF), so "admits at the bags' aux load" was false as written; the floor
is replaced by a per-capacitance noise floor (step 3), and **until T-F-07/T-F-07b and T-E-01 have measured the aux-load rescue the
close is compiled out (`PURGE_RESCUE_ENABLED 0`)**: every in-window early purge is then a State 99, counted against the ceiling with
P(rescue fails) = 1 in the T_LEAD sizing. The
exposure stays bounded by T_LEAD against that ceiling (lead-time paragraph above). The fw36 README §2 phrase "first purge sags
V_bus to 12.9-14.6 V before BT closes" is read here with the correction that BT_BUS EN was set in the onset sample; the dated
review record itself is not edited (L.5).
**Hot-standby option (operator ruling, not in the baseline):** BT_BUS EN held HIGH in windows with V0_bt switched below the UVB
fall band, so the battery picks up a sag through the ideal-diode servo with no tD_ON and any battery conduction implies UVB = 0;
it needs a new FB-divider switch on the BT TPS61288 (the MDAC droop authority of ~0.25 V cannot shift V0_bt by ~3.5 V), a
stuck-switch FMEA, a re-proof of the firmware I-9 barrier (r9-1: the H2c BTB_OFF term is removed; **superseded in r9:** a re-proof of I-9, the H2c BTB_OFF term) and the R3' no-loop argument, and a check that the hand-off bus stays
above LIMIT_V_BUS_MIN 12.0 V.

1. The bus sags. The charger's VINDPM (14.12-14.88 V) cuts its input as the bus passes 14.5 V (loop speed unspecified). The
   converter is no longer shed by UVB inside a window (r9-1: FCCP has no UVB term, so only VINDPM and the step-2 firmware act; **superseded in r9:** removed either by UVB in hardware at 12.89-13.78 V within about 10 us + the inhibit latency, or,) and, **if the sag
   itself sets H1 (r3, findings early-purge-sag-asserts-h1 and h1-asserts-on-bus-sag)**, by P5 LOW in step 2 and by H1 falling
   once V-MOT drains to ~1.07 x VBUS. D-MT-EN blocks V-MOT -> VBUS, so V-MOT is held up by its 0.4-0.97 mF while VBUS falls:
   with V-MOT at 15.2 V, H1 rises once VBUS < 13.96 V, above the UVB fall band, and H1U then sets RFC_OFF and lifts the FC clamp (r9-1; **superseded in r9:** H1R then keeps H2c HIGH and bypasses the UVB
   shed). Whether H1 asserts depends on the sag rate (0.2-2.6 V/ms) against the V-MOT drain ((I_chg + I_trac)/C_VMOT, ~0.9-4.8
   V/ms); T-F-07 records it. No loop results (BT_BUS LOW; D-BC-FC reverse-biased, so the charger drains V-MOT, not the FC). The
   T3 trigger is qualified by "V_bus not falling" (T3, FR-07), so a sag does not raise the ceiling; a sag that sets H1 is tagged
   `chg_src` = sag, does not hide the FR-17 V_fc-onset classification (r9-7: the H2c-fall branch is withdrawn), and does not block T8 (I-4).
   **Sag-to-raise re-entry (r4, finding sag-path-no-return-to-raise):** (r9-7: FCCEIL is removed; the rule is kept so that a real brake that coincides with a short bus dip (a droop settling after a load step, K_DROOP 0.30 ohm x 0.3 A = 0.09 V in 2 ms, is near the qualifier) is raised after the sag branch has run; whether T3's level-sensitive trigger alone covers this case is TODO(verify: r9 audit)) (**superseded in r9:** "the sag path drives FCCEIL LOW, which T3's trigger needs HIGH, so a real brake ... would otherwise be left on the FC-image IINDPM with no raise.") If within 5 ms of the
   sag branch FR-17 has not classified a purge, V_bus has stopped falling (dV/dt > -0.1 V/ms over 2 ms) and H1 rb is still HIGH
   with calibrated V_rgn rising, firmware runs the T3 register sequence (IINDPM 1.70 A first) and retags
   `chg_src` = regen; with the brake feed-forward (FR-41) IINDPM is already 0.90 A during those 5 ms. T-F-07 tests a brake onset
   during a 0.2 V / 2 ms bus dip with no purge (registry, uncertain whether the 5 ms window is long enough at 23 W).
2. Firmware (1 kHz): P5 LOW; FC_CHARGE LOW (r9-7: FCCEIL removed) (sheds the charger's load from the sagging bus); **r5: the motor
   command clamped to `vesc.setCurrent(min(cmd, 0))` until BT conduction is seen or the purge has ended** (a State 99 stops the
   motor anyway; shedding traction to aux load is the measured rescue condition, H.21(f)); **no VINDPM write
   on this path** (I-2 exception: P5 LOW, GATE = H1U (r9-1) and I-3 cover it; the 19.0 V write follows right after step 3).
3. **BT_BUS closes only if the rescue predicate admits it (r5: load-dependent; r6 rewritten, finding
   purge-fc-only-ridethrough-bag-evidence-reopen).** The highest sag rate a rescue close survives is dV_SCP / (tD_ON,max + tON) =
   0.064 V/ms at C_VMOT 0.97 mF and 0.147 V/ms at 0.4 mF (H.6), i.e. a source-less load <= 0.065 A (H.21(f)); the trigger only fires
   once the sag has started (finding rescue-predicate-checked-before-tdon). The predicate (FR-26) is evaluated at **t_eval, the first
   timer-domain tick after the step-2 shed**, on the slope measured over 2 ms after the shed and before any conduction:
   V_bus(t_eval) - max(slope_post_shed, SAG_FLOOR[C_VMOT]) x (tD_ON,max + tON) >= max(LIMIT_V_BUS_MIN 12.0 V, V_BT_est -
   dV_SCP(C_VMOT, ISCP(delta))), with dV_SCP from the ISCP row for the predicted delta (DS-00 EC: 8.5 A at <= 5 V, 7 A at 10 V).
   **SAG_FLOOR[C_VMOT]** is a noise floor, not a physical sag estimate: provisionally 0.005 V/ms (about 2 LSB of V_bus over the 2 ms
   window), with `static_assert(SAG_FLOOR x (tD_ON,max + tON) < dV_SCP)` for each C_VMOT (0.087 V against 1.11 / 2.56 V, H.22(g)); it
   is never set above the survivable rate (0.064 / 0.147 V/ms) and is fixed by T-E-01 with the T-E-04 capacitance. The r5 fixed
   0.2 V/ms term inside the max() is deleted: it refused every rescue at both capacitances. **Classification interplay (withdrawn in r9, r9-7: the H2c-fall classifier is removed; the rescue is reachable only from a V_fc-onset classification; the old text follows as history):** at 0.97 mF
   the right side is 14.89 V, above the 14.16 V V_bus gate of the H2c-fall classifier (FR-17), so a purge classified only by an H2c
   fall with V_bus < 14.16 V is always refused there; the rescue is reachable only from a V_fc-onset classification caught while V_bus
   is still near its pre-onset level (at 0.4 mF the right side is 13.44 V and an H2c classification can still admit). This is
   documented, not changed, because raising the classifier gate would move it into the UVB rise band. **`PURGE_RESCUE_ENABLED`**
   (build flag, default 0 until T-F-07/T-F-07b and T-E-01 pass, reported in telemetry): with 0 the predicate is not consulted and the
   step-2 shed leads straight to outcome (c). If a close is admitted, firmware re-checks every timer-domain tick from the EN edge until
   I_batt > floor and drops BT_BUS EN at once if V_bus falls below V_BT_est - dV_SCP before conduction is seen; whether that aborts
   the turn-on cleanly is a test item (T-E-06), not a guarantee. Host tests (FR-22, shipped constants): (a) V_fc-onset
   classification, V_bus 15.8 V, post-shed 0.02 V/ms at 0.97 mF admits; (b) 1.04 V/ms (1.05 A) refuses; (c) withdrawn in r9 (r9-7: no H2c classification; the old case follows as history:) an H2c classification at
   V_bus 14.16 V, zero slope, 0.97 mF refuses; (d) the static_asserts hold; (e) with `PURGE_RESCUE_ENABLED 0` no close is attempted.
4. Outcomes, all recorded by T-F-07 (r3; r5 restated; r6): **(a)** an admitted re-close and battery hand-off: seen 4 of 4 times
   at aux load in the bags (fw v30 response, standstill; load below the INA253 floor, close delta above the dV_SCP bound, so the
   mechanism is unconfirmed until T-F-07b), expected after the step-2 shed whenever the post-shed load is below ~0.065 A, and only
   with `PURGE_RESCUE_ENABLED 1`; **(c)** UV_BUS dwell (20 ms below 12.0 V) -> State 99, whose recovery uses the low-voltage pre-charge (Death-5
   doctrine): the expected outcome when the bus load cannot be shed below the rescue bound (window load ~1 A is unmeasured),
   counted against the operator's State-99 ceiling. **(d)** an RT1987 SCP gap (64 ms I_batt gap) is a **fault outcome**: logged, State 99, never
   counted as acceptable. The r2 outcome (b), "ride-through on the FC", is deleted (above).
5. The scheduler unlocks and needs 3 new intervals before the next window.

The firmware currently contradicts itself on whether closing onto a sagging node is dangerous (`busHotPlugUnsafe()` comment,
ino ~13035: root cause retired, "cheap defense"; fw v24 backoff comment, ino ~15380: "has already destroyed boosts"). FR-26 keeps
`busHotPlugUnsafe()` at every other call site and applies the rescue predicate only to the FR-15/FR-17 closes; resolving the
contradiction is an operator item (J.2 item 15).

### F.5 Transitions (ordered; invariants first)

Invariants:
- **I-1 (r2)** P5 is LOW across any change that **closes** FCC, and across any BT_BUS close while the FC image (sub-bus VINDPM) is
  active. Opening FCC (r9-7: FCCEIL removed; **superseded in r9:** "with FCCEIL LOW"), and closing BT_BUS after a verified VINDPM >= 18.2 V, may happen with P5 HIGH (F.4 steps
  A-D, T5, T6). P5 also drops on the VINDPM-write failure branch, in T1, T7, T8, T10 and on every trip.
- **I-2 (r4)** Before BT_BUS closes, **either** VINDPM >= 18.2 V is written and read back, **or a barrier is proven**: (a) P5 LOW
  for >= 1 ms and FCC read back LOW (the F.4 step-B failure branch; r9-7: the pin-7 /CE sense is removed, TODO(verify: r9 audit, F.3)), (b) after an FR-08(b) trip (r9-7: the I2C latch trip),
  REGEN read back LOW for >= the D-BC-RG turn-off time (T-E-06) and FCC read back LOW, or (c) the T10 input-isolation proof
  (FC_CHARGE and REGEN read back LOW for >= the RT1987 turn-off time + 2 ms, plus proof (b), V_chg decayed, or proof (d), CHG_IIN < 0.1 A for 1 ms with the lead alive (FR-11, r9-7) (**superseded in r9:** "plus /CE sense HIGH, or (r5, for an FR-08(b) trip) the far-end ILIM sense held with no input current, or V_chg decayed"). A sub-bus
  VINDPM (14.5 V) is written only once **BT_BUS EN reads back LOW, the RT1987 turn-off wait (T-E-06) has elapsed and I_BT has been
  at the floor for 5 ms** (r4, finding i2-btboff-precondition-unobservable: the r3 "BTB_OFF via H2c precondition" cannot be
  observed at T2 step 3, where FCC is still LOW and H2c rb is LOW whatever BTB_OFF does; a D-BT-EN still conducting below the floor
  is the R8 residual and matters only during H1U (r9-1; was H1q), where H1 bars the loop). REGEN may be HIGH (R7). **Exceptions:** T8 (early
  purge), where P5 LOW, GATE = H1U (r9-1) and I-3 cover it until the 19.0 V write that follows; the F.4 step-B failure branch and T10
  through the barriers above.
- **I-3** P5 rises only after a read-back of the full masked image and REG19 ICO_ILIM in the current charger power cycle.
- **I-4 (r4, finding i4-blocks-state99-under-h1)** No **normal** mode transition starts while H1 = 1, except the raise (T3), the
  purge pre-emption and the early-purge path T8 (r3: a fast bus sag can itself set H1, F.4 step 1). Two classes are **never gated
  by H1**: (a) **inhibit-only signals** (P5 or QUAL driven LOW; r9-7: FCCEIL removed; r9-6: the heartbeat is deleted, **superseded in r9:** "the heartbeat stopped") in any state, executed directly by
  the trip/fault path and not queued behind the mode manager; (b) **fault paths**: T7 (all phases), T10, **the FR-42 pre-emption backstop (r5)** and the latch actions of
  FR-08 (b) and (d), FR-33, FR-36, FR-14(d) and the T_QUAL_MAX backstop (FR-04), which run on the detecting tick (r9-7: FR-08 (a), (c) and FR-35 withdrawn). Inside a fault path REGEN and FCC may be
  lowered with H1 = 1 only after P5 and QUAL are LOW and `vesc.setCurrent(0)` has been commanded; a V-MOT rise to the VESC
  OV cut on that path is accepted (the F.3 MCU-reset outcome). Everything else stays gated: non-fault REGEN/FCC drops, T6,
  operator and traction T5, T2/T4. Otherwise a fault during a brake would defer the State-99 inhibit, and an H1 stuck HIGH (R110
  open, F.3) would defer the FR-08(d) latch forever.
- **I-5 (r9-7, 2026-11-12, firmware-rules decisions 1 and 2)** QUAL (pin 33, a level) rises only with P5 LOW, after EN_CHG = 0 and REG11 = 0 are read back, and only on the REGN marker (T1 step 5: PG_STAT = 1; r9-7: the /CE-sense branch of the marker is removed with pin 7), never on the first ACK. Firmware drops it on any NACK after the first ACK, any read-back mismatch, no ACK within 100 ms of REGEN closing, PG_STAT = 1 + 50 ms, or marker + 300 ms, whichever is first (TODO(calibrate: T-B-20)), and it is LOW whenever P5 changes. **Order (normative):** QUAL is driven LOW and held LOW for at least one 1 kHz tick before P5 is driven HIGH, on every P5 path (T1, T9, the `J` stage 2, trips, the VINDPM-failure branch, T6, T7, T8; host test FR-22); the NOT P5 and FCC_OFF terms of the qualification release (B.1) mask a slip. **Time limit:** QUAL has no hardware time limit (U111 is removed); an independent backstop in the FR-45 1 kHz timer domain, separate from the step machine, drives QUAL, P5 and REGEN LOW on the detecting tick once QUAL has been HIGH for more than **T_QUAL_MAX = 0.46 s** since its rising edge (the former tw_QQ maximum, TODO(calibrate: T-B-20)), latches `CHG_QUAL_OVERRUN` and refuses regen arming until Idle. Under an MCU hang the backstop stops with the MCU, and only the R5 watchdog (G.3) bounds QUAL HIGH (J.1). (**superseded in r9:** "QUAL rises only with P5 LOW, after EN_CHG = 0 and REG11 = 0 are read back, and is LOW whenever P5 changes, on every P5 path (T1, trips, the VINDPM-failure branch, T6, T7, T8; host test FR-22); U118B masks a slip with FCC HIGH. r3: QUAL rises only on the REGN marker (T1 step 5: PG_STAT = 1, or the /CE sense HIGH for 2 ms with P5 LOW), never on the first ACK. ... The hardware one-shot ends QQ after tw_QQ (0.20-0.46 s, H.17) in any case.")
- **I-6** Poor-source recovery: PG_STAT still 0 at REGN marker + 150 ms (r3; was "300 ms after REGEN closes"), or POORSRC_FLAG
  -> keep P5 LOW, force a retry (EN_HIZ 1 -> 0; the EN_HIZ shadow and the T_REGN_MAX timer restart, FR-23, so FR-08(b) stays
  quiet while REGN is legitimately off), harvest-lost flag (SLUSDV2C §7.3.4.2 p.27: otherwise retry every 7 minutes).
- **I-7** **Withdrawn in r9 (r9-7, 2026-11-12):** FCCEIL is removed with tap T11 (**superseded in r9:** "FCCEIL is HIGH only while the IINDPM and ICHG read-backs equal the FC-image values; it is driven LOW before any write that raises them.")
- **I-8** No FC window opens unless the purge schedule is locked and the window ends at least T_LEAD before the predicted onset.
- **I-9 (new)** The FC_CHARGE and BT_BUS EN nets are never HIGH at the same time: the BT_BUS setter refuses while FCC is HIGH,
  the FCC setter refuses while BT_BUS is HIGH; the single-sample `FAULT_SWITCH_CONFLICT` (ino 7413-7418) stays as the backstop.

| T3 | **Raise (level-sensitive)**: FC image active **and** H1 rb HIGH **and REGEN read back HIGH (r9-7, firmware-rules decision 3b)** **and V_bus not falling** (r9-7: "(FCCEIL HIGH)" removed) (r3: dV_bus/dt > -0.1 V/ms over the last 2 ms and V_bus > the UVB rise maximum 14.16 V), from the pin-34 rising-edge interrupt or the first FR-45 timer-domain tick that sees the state (r6: never a `loop()` poll). **H1 with a falling bus is a sag, not a brake** (F.4 step 1): write VINDPM 18.2 V (r9-7: "FCCEIL 0" removed) (the FC image then stops drawing from V-MOT, which sits below 18.2 V), tag `chg_src` = sag, and hand over to the FR-17 classification; **r4: sag-to-raise re-entry** after 5 ms with no purge classified, V_bus no longer falling and H1 still HIGH with V_rgn rising: steps 2-4 below (F.4 step 1; r9-7: "with FCCEIL kept LOW" removed). **r5 brake feed-forward (FR-41):** a command below -I_ff (1.0 A) in an open window starts the measurement-gated IINDPM ramp on its first tick (the command itself goes to the VESC unmodified), which reaches 0.85-0.90 A before H1 can rise (H.21(b)) | 1) ISR (rising edge): post the raise (FR-07). 2) The raise worker re-reads H1 rb and the REGEN read-back at service; with either LOW it drops the request (r9-7, decisions 3a and 3b); otherwise it writes REG06-07 IINDPM 1.70 A. 3) Write REG03-05: (**superseded in r9:** "1) ISR: FCCEIL 0 (H1 = 1, so no blank) and post the raise. 2) The raise worker re-asserts FCCEIL LOW atomically immediately before each raising write (r3, finding t3-t4-fcceil-race), then writes REG06-07 IINDPM 1.70 A. 3) FCCEIL LOW re-asserted, then write REG03-05:") ICHG 3.10 A, VINDPM 18.2 V. **3b) (r8, CHG-R1-02: write first, read back after)** Only after the REG03-05 write completes: the FR-46 read-back as four field reads REG01:02, REG03:04, REG05, REG06:07 (each inside the FR-07 cap at 100 and 400 kHz, no 16-bit field split, H.23(o)); a mismatch takes the immediate P5-LOW path of FR-46 (the converter stops absorbing and V-MOT rises toward the VESC OV cut: safe, harvest lost) (**superseded in r8:** "; read back." ; r8: the r6 FR-46 group order put R(REG01:02) and R(REG06:07) between the two raising writes: 2.329 ms at 100 kHz, H.23(o)). 4) Ratchet VINDPM to 19.0 V only when calibrated V_rgn > 19.0 x 1.02 + 0.19 V. From the held static maximum 19.72 V with 0.90 A absorbing at 0.4 mF, detection + raise in 1.0 ms reaches 20.11 V at 18.9 W and 20.59 V at 23 W (H.20): at 23 W a false restore can end at the VESC cut (safe, harvest lost; T-D-12 at both powers, J.2) | edge to write complete <= 1.5 ms (FR-07): **r8:** 0.565 ms at 400 kHz and 1.359 ms at 100 kHz (margin 0.141 ms) with a capped transaction already in flight and t_BUF, under the FR-07 r8 queue-priority rule (H.23(o), H.23(y) row (2); ISR latency not included, TODO(calibrate: T-C-06)); the step-3b read-back completes 1.028 / 3.208 ms after the edge and lies outside this deadline (r8: the r7 figure counted the two writes only) (**superseded in r8:** 0.5 ms at 400 kHz, 1.35 ms at 100 kHz with the 0.5 ms transaction cap) |

Opening both charger inputs makes loop safety independent of the charger, its registers and its /CE inhibit, which may be what failed (FR-08(b) is a charger converting with P5 LOW, for example /CE stuck LOW; FR-33/FR-36/FR-10/FR-11 mean the charger may really be converting). An open T17 leaves pin 22 near 0 V and would pass (d) falsely, hence the lead-alive rule. For FR-08(b) only (b) or (d) is accepted; (b) remains the proof for the shorted-input-switch suspicion. (**superseded in r9:** proof (a) "/CE sense (pin 7) HIGH for 1 ms with P5 LOW" and proof (c) "for the FR-08(b) trip (r5, finding t10-fr08b-proof-relies-on-slow-decay), the far-end ILIM sense (pin 33) LOW for >= 1 ms with GATE expected 0 and the heartbeat alive, plus CHG_IIN (pin 22, eFuse IMON) < 0.1 A or the IBUS ADC < 0.1 A ..."; both sensors are removed.) **r4's "a charger still converting drains VCHG-IN quickly, so (b) completes fastest exactly in the failed-inhibit case" was wrong for FR-08(b):** once step 1 drives FCC and REGEN LOW, the charger is not converting (r9-1: with FCC, QUAL and REGEN LOW, FCCP = QF = 0 and both input switches are open, B.1; the r9-7 re-derivation note is settled here; **superseded in r9:** "H2c = H1q = 0, ILIM_HIZ is held and"), so VCHG-IN decays only through the standby loads: 16.0 -> 9.9 V takes 37-102 ms (30-57 uF effective, 3.4-4.9 mA, H.21(g)), and a trip in the last 40-100 ms before t_pred - T_LEAD would have missed the proof and taken the double-fault branch on a single fault. 3) BT_BUS HIGH through the pre-emption path (dwell bypassed, only FR-26 / `busHotPlugUnsafe()` kept); then the window latch releases BT_BUS-LOW / FC_BUS-HIGH ownership to the selector with its re-arm inhibit set; the FR-14(b) setpoint hold releases on the T5 step-E readiness predicate; windows and REGEN arming stay refused until the trip latch clears (reboot or operator). 4) **Double fault:** if the step-2 proof is not reached by t_pred - T_LEAD, or FR-26 refuses the close, BT_BUS is not closed into a possible loop; a controlled T7 is taken before the purge, and the cause is logged (a shorted D-BC-RG or D-BC-FC that FR-12 missed is the named suspect) | step 1 one tick; step 2 ~ turn-off + 2 ms (T-E-06); must finish before t_pred - T_LEAD + tD_ON,max |
| T9 | **Re-qualify after a POR clamp latch** (FR-30; r5: also after any V_chg collapse-and-return with REGEN HIGH, whether the D-BC-RG OVP/OTP latched or auto-restarted) | P5 LOW on the detecting tick and held until I-3. At the next point with no burst and no window: P5 0, FCC LOW, EN_HIZ 1 -> 0 (shadow and T_REGN_MAX timer restarted, FR-23), then T1 steps 4-9 from the REGN marker, including the step-8 QUAL-LOW tick before the P5 rise (I-5) and the end-of-T1 check, so T9 ends with P5 HIGH only after the step-8 read-back (r9-7; T-F-03) (**superseded in r9:** "(r8: including step 8c and the end-of-T1 check, so T9 ends with P5 HIGH only after the step-8c read-back; T-F-03)"), if T-B-07 shows an EN_HIZ toggle re-reads the pin; otherwise at the next Idle -> Run | - |

## G. Registers and firmware requirements

### G.1 BQ25798 register map in use (I2C 0x6B, 400 kHz with the MB RSDA/RSCL 2.7 kOhm pull-ups (PM9), 100 kHz fallback; SLUSDV2C §7.3.14 p.53, register tables §7.5)

Byte order of 16-bit fields: bits 15:8 at the lower offset (Fig 7-27 p.60). Self-check at the first read: REG01:02 = 0x03 0x48
(840 x 10 mV = 8.40 V, the 2S POR value).

**Never write:** REG0A (CELL; a CELL write resets VREG/ICHG/VSYSMIN to that cell count's defaults, §7.3.2 p.25), REG16
(VAC1_PD_EN would put a 60 ohm sink on VCHG-IN), REG09 bit 6 REG_RST (always 0), REG0B-REG0D and REG47 (OTG/backup), and
**REG14** (r2, finding reg14-write-reopens-extilim). The write function (FR-03) refuses these addresses always; the only
exception is the single token-gated REG14 recovery write of FR-36.

read-only table below):

The FC IINDPM governor (FR-14, r2): IINDPM = `min(0.90, G)` A with G = I_cap - I_aux,meas - max(I_trac,peak, I_cmd-proxy) -
I_ripple - margin and I_cap = min(1.20 A, (P_MAX,bus - 1.0 W) / V_bus) (H.12), rewritten at 50 Hz with read-back, where
I_trac,peak is a 2 s peak-hold of the 1 kHz traction current (bus side) and I_ripple the measured once-per-rev allowance
(T-F-04b sets it and the margin); the window closes below G = 0.30 A and opens only above 0.30 A + H_adm (F.4). I_aux,meas is
the FC bus-side current at window entry minus the charger IBUS ADC reading. **Brake feed-forward (r5, FR-41, F.3 items 1-5):** while a window is
open or opening, a command below -I_ff (1.0 A) at the `vesc.setCurrent()` chokepoint enters the BRAKE state and starts the
measurement-gated ramp IINDPM_next = min(0.90 A (0x005A), IINDPM_now + (I_cap - m_ff - I_fc,raw)), each step read back; the
brake command itself is not delayed; the traction peak-hold is **kept** (it decays only after 2 s at <= 0); in BRAKE the governor
writes nothing below the ramp value and the G-based close is suspended (every non-G close stays live); on BRAKE exit (command >= 0
for one 20 ms slot, H1 rb LOW) G is re-seeded and a positive command is released only once the IINDPM = min(0.90 A, G) write is
ACKed (r6: deadline T_HOLD_ACK 1.0 ms at 400 kHz, 1.5 ms at 100 kHz, plus the T-B-24 settle; else P5 LOW first); its read-back is
checked on the next timer-domain tick before any further raise (finding ff-reversal-hold-unattainable-at-100khz). The proxy is traction-only, max(0, I_cmd) x k_proxy / eta (FR-14(a)).

**I2C engine and poll schedule** (FR-07): one interrupt-driven LPI2C engine owns the bus; no blocking `Wire` call anywhere. 20 ms
frame: slot 0 status REG1B-21; slot 5 critical verify REG00-0A + REG14 (split into transactions of <= 0.35 ms at 400 kHz /
0.5 ms at 100 kHz); **slots 0 and 10: IBAT/IBUS REG31-34 every 10 ms** (r2, matches the 12 ms scan); slot 10 also REG35-36 +
REG41 in parts; slot 15 WD kick + extended verify in parts. **Bus clear (r2, finding i2c-bus-recovery-missing):** at boot and after
any bus-busy or transaction timeout, pins 18/19 switch to GPIO, SCL is clocked up to 9 times until SDA reads HIGH, a STOP is
issued and LPI2C is re-initialised (the BQ25798 stays alive from BAT and VBUS above VBAT_UVLO 2.30-2.50 V, so a reset mid-read
can leave it holding SDA LOW). A pending raise is inserted at the next
transaction boundary; a read in flight may be aborted (NACK + STOP) and retried, a write never is (16-bit fields REG03:04 and
REG06:07 must not be left half-written). **r6 (FR-46, finding vreg-corruption-no-fixed-pack-ovp):** every write of REG03:04,
REG05 or REG06:07 is followed, in the same queued transaction group, by a read of REG01:02 and of the register just written (r8: as separate field reads, REG01:02 and then the written field, each inside the FR-07 cap; R(REG01:02) takes 0.120 ms at 400 kHz and 0.480 ms at 100 kHz, H.23(o); **superseded in r8:** one
3-byte read 0x01-0x03 plus the written field: ~0.25 ms at 400 kHz, ~1.0 ms at 100 kHz, inside the FR-07 cap when split), and the
same read precedes every P5, QUAL or EN_CHG rising edge; a mismatch drops P5 before any rewrite. **T3 exception (r8, CHG-R1-02; stated also in FR-46):** inside a raise (T3 and the sag-to-raise re-entry) the two raising writes, REG06:07 and then REG03-05, complete first, and the read-back follows both as four field reads REG01:02, REG03:04, REG05, REG06:07 (100 kHz: 0.48 / 0.48 / 0.39 / 0.48 ms; 400 kHz: 0.120 / 0.120 / 0.098 / 0.120 ms; each inside the FR-07 cap, no 16-bit field split; H.23(o)). Edge to write complete is then 1.359 ms at 100 kHz and 0.565 ms at 400 kHz against the FR-07 1.5 ms; the read-back completes 3.208 / 1.028 ms after the edge, outside that deadline. A mismatch takes the immediate P5-LOW path. A single 7-byte REG01-07 read is not used: at 100 kHz it takes 0.930 ms, above the 0.50 ms cap (H.23(o)); four field reads were chosen over a cap exception because each stays inside the cap at both rates and none splits a 16-bit field.

**POR / WD detection:** WD_STAT, any masked mismatch, VBUS_PRESENT or PG change, POORSRC_FLAG -> P5 LOW first, then REG0F =
0x02, rewrite, verify, re-arm through T1 steps 7-9 (or T2 step 3 onward in a window). A REG14 mismatch is not re-imaged: it
takes the FR-36 latched path. **r9-6 (2026-11-12, D2-4): after any MCU reset** (watchdog or otherwise) firmware reads WD_STAT / WD_FLAG at reconnect, logs them, and treats the image as lost whatever they read: re-image starting REG0F = 0x02, then the static image with STOP_WD_CHG = 1 read back, before any P5 or QUAL rise. The charger watchdog is never a hang barrier; R5 carries hangs (G.3).

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|

A shorted D-MT-EN is not benign: every regen event would go straight onto VBUS and the P3 soft-start would be defeated. H1 rb 0; H2c rb 0. r8: the r7 decay test failed because the decay from 9.9 V to 3 V below UVLO takes 1.65-2.75 s (H.23(q)), so a warm reset with a fast bring-up could false-fail it and refuse regen for one boot, and the r7 probe could not pass the FR-23 gate (**superseded in r8:** "FCC = REGEN = 0 -> V_chg decays below 3 V within 2 s (shorted D-BC-FC/D-BC-RG); H1 rb 0; H2c rb 0; I2C to 0x6B NACK (charger unpowered)"). CHG_EFUSE_FLT is **not** checked while V_chg < 10.2 V (its state below the 4.5 V IN_SYS minimum is unspecified, T-C-04). **Outcome split (r3, finding btok-selftest-floor-overlap):** a failure of any regen-relevant check (shorted D-BC-RG/D-MT-EN, H1 rb, H2c rb, I2C answering while unpowered) -> carrier-absent flag, FC windows **and** regen arming refused; a **BT_OK-only** failure -> `BT_OK-floor` flag, **FC windows only** refused (H1q has no BT_OK term). If BT_OK reads 0 while pin 41 is within the stored floor + 3 LSB, the log says "BT_OK threshold below floor" (calibration fault: re-select R142, T-C-03); if pin 41 is clearly above the floor (> 0.1 A), it logs real BT current at Idle as a separate fault. The REGN marker and the QUAL-before-P5 order are checked at every Run entry (T1 steps 5 and 8) (r9-7: the heartbeat and the far-end senses are removed; **superseded in r9:** "The heartbeat and far-end senses are self-tested at every Run entry (T1 steps 5 and 8), because they need REGN") |

The FR-07 edge-to-write-complete deadline excludes the read-back (100 kHz: writes complete at 1.359 ms, read-back at 3.208 ms; 400 kHz: 0.565 / 1.028 ms; H.23(o)) |

### G.3 MCU hardware watchdog (R5)

Specification from the study §5.1 (RTWDOG 100 ms in the study, **50 ms target in r4, see below**, WDOG1 1.0 s, ERR_MCU_WDT latched and acknowledged before Run), **with the feed
rule of FR-28 (r3):** the watchdog is fed only by a completed 1 kHz monitor tick (stage mask), not once per `loop()`. **WDOG1_B is routed only to pin 20 (AD_B1_10, ALT1); never
to pin 19 (SCL, AD_B1_00 ALT4) or pin 34 (B1_13 ALT0, now CHG_H1_RB, where it would drive against the U102 output)** (IMXRT1060RM
Rev 3 §11.6.104 and the AD_B1_00/AD_B1_10 mux tables). Pin 21 is free (r9-6, 2026-11-12, D2-5: defined firmware mode under the freed-pin rule, FR-01); EWM_OUT_B (AD_B1_11 = pin 21, TODO(verify: IMXRT1060RM)
ALT1) is not used (**superseded in r9:** "Pin 21 now carries CHG_HB, so the EWM_OUT_B option ... is given up"). **r9-6 (D2-2): R5 is the only hang defence; no hardware hang inhibit exists (operator ruling 2026-11-12).** The heartbeat is deleted, and WDOG1_B is not tapped into the permit gate (the tap count stays 10): WDOG1_B asserts only after firmware has configured WDOG1, so it does not remove the R5 firmware dependency; WDOG1 is the 1.0 s second stage; after a reset the pad returns to its reset mux state, so without a latch part the gate would see only a pulse; and the reset already drops P5, QUAL and every EN through the pull-downs (the pin 5/33 keeper caveat is J.2 item 69). (**superseded in r9:** "The hardware heartbeat (B.1) already inhibits charging on a hang; R5 is still required because".) R5 is also required because a hang in an
FC window leaves BT_BUS open through the next purge, and because a hardware BT re-close on a hang without the hot-plug check
would break the Death-5 doctrine. **No charging of any kind (regen, qualification, FC windows), attended or not, runs before the R5 firmware exists and T-W-01a passes; no FC window runs before the full T-W-01 passes (r9-6, D2-1).** (**superseded in r9:** "No unattended charger session until T-W-01 passes.")

**r4 (findings hang-fc-window-r5-gates-r1, hang-fc-window-purge-reclose-death5): the watchdog is a precondition of FC charging,
not future work.** No FC-charge window, attended or not, runs before T-W-01 passes (F.4 window rule (i)); R1's FC charging
therefore depends on R5, which is firmware only (r9-6, D2-2: pin 20 carries WDOG1_B with no CR consumer; **superseded in r9:** "firmware plus an optional pin-20 route"). **r9-6 (2026-11-12, D2-1): R5 is a precondition of all charger arming.** QUAL, every P5 rise and every FC window need the R5 build flag, which is set only after the R5 firmware (RTWDOG + WDOG1 configuration, the FR-28 feed token, ERR_MCU_WDT, the FR-43 brackets) exists and T-W-01a passes (FR-04, FR-05); FC windows additionally need the full T-W-01 with the T-D-14 rig. Run with the charger disarmed (REGEN LOW, no QUAL) needs neither. The R5 firmware is built with the rest of the new-charger firmware in the handoff after the PCB design, so no charging of any kind runs on the vehicle before then; State 98 offers no bench charging path before R5 either. **Timeout:** the RTWDOG timeout must satisfy t_WDT + 1 ms
(reset to every EN LOW through the 10 kOhm pull-downs) < the minimum purge duration measured in T-E-01 minus a 20 ms margin; with
100-140 ms purges the study's 100 ms is marginal, so the **target is 50 ms** (fed only by the FR-28 completion token, which a
healthy 1 kHz loop gives every 1 ms; WDOG1 1.0 s stays the second stage). A hang that starts before or during a purge then resets
the MCU before the stack recovers, so MOT_PWR and FC_BUS are LOW at recovery and it always goes through the `setup()` pre-charge.
**Reset release order:** a watchdog reset releases every EN at once (MOT_PWR, REGEN, FC_BUS, BT_BUS, FC_CHARGE, BT_SEQ) and the
boost enables; T-W-01 checks that MOT_PWR and REGEN fall no later than FC_REG_ENABLE / BT_REG_ENABLE (back-feed rule) or confirms
the boost-enable reset-state levels, and counts each such reset against the operator's State-99 ceiling. The residual (a hang
within ~t_WDT + T_LEAD of an onset, ~1.5 % of window hangs) is characterised on the bench (T-D-14) and recorded (J.2).

**r5 (findings rtwdog-50ms-vs-blocking-flash-ops, flash-commit-stalls-hb-and-wdt-in-run): legitimate stalls, windowing and the
flash gate (FR-43).** The r4 text armed the 50 ms RTWDOG at all times while the encoder EEPROM commit still ran from `loop()` in
regen-armed Run. PJRC cores teensy4/eeprom.c (master, read 2026-11-06) appends 2-byte entries to one of 63 4 kB sectors (the
record at 4276 lives in sector 61, shared with every address that maps there; fill accumulates across boots) and, when a sector
holds 2048 entries, erases it (command 0x20) and rewrites up to 256 entries, with `__disable_irq()` held around every program and
erase until the busy bit clears. With the Winbond W25Q64JV-class figures tSE <= 400 ms and tPP <= 3 ms (recalled, TODO(verify:
Winbond W25Q64JV datasheet; PJRC Teensy 4.1 flash part)) one commit can mask interrupts for ~1.2 s (H.21(e)): longer than RTWDOG
50 ms **and** than the 1.0 s WDOG1 second stage, and long enough to freeze the encoder ISRs and `detectFaults()` with the motor
running. **t_WDT cannot be sized around it** (it must stay below the minimum purge - 20 ms - 1 ms = 79 ms), so the flash write is
removed from every watchdog-armed state by construction: (1) the 50 ms RTWDOG timeout is loaded only while `rtwdogShort` is TRUE (r9-6, 2026-11-12, D2-3: mainState 2, or any of P5, QUAL, FC_CHARGE or REGEN HIGH, commanded or read back; the State-2 term covers the fw v28 selector's FC-only arms, which carry the same purge exposure, and the pin terms cover State 98 sessions; FR-43) (**superseded in r9:** "only while the charger heartbeat
runs (T1 step 0 to T6 step 5 / T7 phase 0 / a trip latch; that is the only time a window, and so a purge exposure, can exist)"), and
the long timeout applies elsewhere; (2) every flash write goes through `mcuFlashOpBegin()` in a quiescent state only (FR-43; r8: battery-supported Idle admitted, flash never in State 99), which
also stretches both watchdog stages for the span and restores and reads back the short timeout before any EN rises; (3) **recorded
constraint:** in every watchdog-armed state the longest legitimate loop stall is <= 5 ms (FR-27; r9-6: the tw_HB,min reference is withdrawn with the heartbeat, **superseded in r9:** "below tw_HB,min - 2 ms"), and
max_stall + margin < t_WDT < T-E-01 minimum purge - 21 ms; SD close/sync only under the separate FR-43 `sdOpAllowed` gate (r8: Idle or State 98 with `rtwdogShort` FALSE (r9-6; **superseded in r9:** "with the heartbeat stopped"), or State 99 phase 3; **superseded in r8:** SD close/sync only in State 1, 98 or 99 phase 3, which shared the flash bracket); each I2C bus clear
<= 1 ms. T-W-01 adds the legitimate-stall cases and the new **T-W-02** forces the worst-case commit (sector 61 pre-filled to 2047
entries) through the gated API.

**r8 (CHG-R1-D01): flash and SD gates separated.** The r5 predicate required FC_BUS LOW, which the normal Idle vector (F.2: 1 1 1 1 1 0 0 1) never has, so no commit was admitted outside a manually configured State 98; its "no SD log open" term blocked the SD close it also governed; and it allowed that close in State 99 phase 3 while it forbade State 99 in the same bracket. FR-43 now defines `flashWriteAllowed` (battery-supported Idle admitted, flash never in State 99) and `sdOpAllowed` (SD close and sync only: Idle and State 98 with `rtwdogShort` FALSE, and State 99 phase 3 (r9-6; **superseded in r9:** "with the heartbeat stopped")), each with its own bracket. The watchdog windowing is unchanged: both gates require `rtwdogShort` FALSE, so neither operation runs under the 50 ms RTWDOG timeout (r9-6; **superseded in r9:** "both gates require the heartbeat stopped").

## I. Uncertainty and test registry

Bench order: **T-A** parts and incoming checks, **T-B** EVM standalone, **T-C** carrier + EIB + bench Teensy on emulated
supplies, **T-D** bench failure injection, **T-E** measurements on the vehicle with the existing hardware (no new parts; may run
in parallel with T-A..T-D at any time, but listed here as board tests), **T-F** board integration, **T-G** regen and FC on the
road, **T-W** MCU watchdog. Equipment codes: PSU1 (>= 24 V 3 A, current-limited), PSU2 (second supply or electronic load with a
16 -> 21 V step < 1 ms, or a current-source mode), BATSIM (2S pack or 4-quadrant source), RT-SI (RT1987 stand-in: a spare RT1987
on perfboard with 5.6 nF CSS, or an MB channel), SCOPE (4 ch, >= 100 MHz), CP (current probe >= 20 A), DMM, LA (logic
analyser), LCR, HG (heat gun / thermal chamber), THERM (thermocouple).

Before you bond the offcut, measure its stack, film and PSA together, with a micrometer to +-0.01 mm. Record it as t_coupon (information only; PM4 (2c) measures t_rm on the removed stack) (r8 verification round; **superseded in r8:** "With a micrometer, measure the offcut stack, film and PSA together, and record it as t_rm."). Bed a second FT1-size block directly on the coupon solder mask beside the sheet, 0.30 mm above it on shims, with the same RTV, so that the fallback bond on the mask is qualified as well. Hold an FT1-size block (4.0 x 1.6 mm, the BOM foot material) 0.30 mm above the sheet on shims. Bed it with the bed RTV of E. Cure it as in PM4 (5). Remove the shims. Pull each block upward with 0.4 N for 10 s (r8; **superseded in r8:** "Pull the block upward"). The whole pull acts on the coupon bed, so its bed stress is at least the FT1 bed stress of the 0.4 N tab pull below (H.23(i)). Order: after the PM4 (5) cure, for both feet; (r9-4: the repeat after PM6 is withdrawn with pads F20 and F21; **superseded in r9:** again for FT1 after PM6, because the tap pads F20 (T20) and F21 (T21) lie over the FT1 body (H.23(g))). Probe the FT2 fill-hole plug with a blunt pin. Try a 0.05 mm feeler at the FT1 tape, foot-bed and bed-sheet interfaces, from the tab X +y edge and tip. Inspect the FT2 witness fillets at its -y, -x and +x faces with a loupe. Try a 0.05 mm feeler between the sheet and the MB mask within 3 mm of either foot. Inspect the 22 header joints with a loupe; take the T-F-12 DMM readings. Pull upward with 0.4 N for 10 s (spring scale) at each grip in turn. Tab X grip: a wire loop under the tip edge strip (x 64.50-65.00), ends joined above (65.00, 62.30). Tab Y grip: a wire loop under the +y edge strip (y 75.50-76.00), ends joined above (28.00, 76.00), in line with FT2. Never pass a loop past the tab Y +y edge (L-FC 0.862 mm, H.23(b)). Repeat the feelers, the loupe inspection and the DMM readings. The 0.4 N pull keeps the bed stress at 0.87 x (FT1) and 0.97 x (FT2) the 30 g service stress, whole tab load at the tip (H.23(i)). On the distributed-load basis (the 30 g load spread from root to tip) the ratios are 1.93 x and 1.92 x, so 0.4 N lies inside the service range only on the tip-load basis. 0.4 N is the 0.1 N floor of the tab Y limit 0.413 N (tab X limit 0.461 N). The bed stress at 0.4 N is 15.1-54.9 kPa at FT1 and 2.0-12.7 kPa at FT2 (**superseded in r7:** a 0.8 N pull at 1.74-1.94 x on the tip-load basis) (**superseded in r7:** a 5 N pull at each tab tip, 10.9-12.1 x that stress through the PSA) | **r8 step 0:** no debond at the bed-sheet interface and no lift of the sheet from the coupon mask after the pull; no debond of the mask block; t_coupon recorded (**superseded in r8:** "t_rm recorded"); the (2c) and (2d) records within their PM4 limits; the FT2 plug has no tack and no liquid; the 0.05 mm feeler does not enter at any FT1 interface or between the sheet and the mask; a continuous RTV fillet at the FT2 -y, -x and +x faces; no debond after the pull; no new joint crack; the T-F-12 readings unchanged | An uncured plug: wait for the cure and repeat; a debond: re-bed; a sheet-to-mask lift is a PSA failure, not an RTV failure: re-press the sheet and repeat before the fallback; r8: a debond of the step 0 mask block: no qualified fallback bond, so choose another bed RTV (T-A-05) and repeat step 0 before PM4 (1); **r8 (A.7, H.23(r)):** a step 0 coupon that does not hold on polyimide: before PM4 (2c), cut the sheet within the foot keep-out coordinates (FT1 x 59.220-64.220, y 65.405-68.005, so the MPPT-DISABLE trace stays covered by 0.794 mm; FT2 x 25.500-30.500, y 70.750-75.750), never sized to an as-found foot; measure the removed stack (film and PSA) as t_rm; fit re-made feet of h_f' = 2.19 mm + t_rm; repeat the PM4 (2d) gate; bed onto the MB solder mask.
