## J. Residual risks and known limitations

### J.1 Accepted

1. **R8 (accepted 2026-11-05):** in an FC window with D-BT-EN shorted, a loop below the BT_OK threshold (0.06-0.34 A worst case;
   the INA253A1 floor can reach 0.1 A, SLOS954A §7.5) and below the firmware trip (floor + margin, about 0.12 A) is not stopped
   in hardware for the window duration. FR-11 (power balance) may catch it, depending on T-B-14. **r9-1 (2026-11-12):** BT_OK (U104)
   is removed, so no hardware threshold remains: a shorted D-BT-EN in a window is bounded only by the firmware I_BT trip (floor +
   margin, about 0.12 A), FR-10 and FR-11 (item 23).
2. Fallback 2 if T-B-09 fails (r9-3, 2026-11-12: the keep-alive option is withdrawn): the pack sits on the BQ25798 BAT pin, with the parked BAT draw and the pack-fed VCHG/W3/EVM-BAT exposure of B.5, bounded by the link fuse (**superseded in r9:** Keep-alive drain if T-B-09 fails: 0.7-1.4 mA in Run only (B.5), or the bridge fallback).
3. **Run standby draw of the always-powered regen design: 56-80 mW for all of Run** (H.15, r3 recount with the EVM TS bias and
   the EIB REGN pull-ups), about 10x the drain of the keep-alive option withdrawn in r9-3. It is the price of R3' with an always-powered charger and must appear
   in the energy statistics (FR-21). The BQ25798 share in the ILIM-held, REGN-on state is not specified by TI (T-B-04).
4. **Board-side VCHG-IN segment without a current limit in Run (r2):** C-D8, C-D10, the MB trace, the pad-10 pin, the CR VCHGIN
   copper and U101 IN are upstream of the eFuse. The RT1987 SCP is active only during soft-start (DS-00 §17.5), so after tON only
   OTP (~140 C) remains. Bus-fed fault current is bounded by the OC_FC/OC_BT single-sample firmware latches; the CAL 470 uF +
   VESC bulk discharge through D-BC-RG is not bounded and may exceed the RT1987 20 A / 10 ms peak rating. Mitigation is
   mechanical: no flying lead (W8 deleted), <= 5 mm solder-masked CR copper, inspection T-F-12.
5. **eFuse OUT below its -0.3 V absolute minimum during a hard short at the EVM end (r2):** about -0.5 to -1 V for < 1 us,
   clamped by D103, accepted under SLVSE94G §9.5.1/§11 pending the TI E2E answer (T-C-04 checks survival).
6. **One INA253 BT output feeds BT_OK, FR-34 and FR-10 (r3, finding ina253-bt-common-cause; r9-7: BT_OK and FR-34 are removed, so the output now feeds FR-10 and FR-38 only; the item is re-stated in the r9 audit, TODO(verify)):** a single fault that drives it to
   0 V (dead part, lost INA supply, REF1/REF2 lifted) reads "no pack current" (r9-1; r8: on all three), so in an FC window a shorted D-BT-EN
   (the R8 case) would be bounded only by the FC-image IINDPM. Mitigation: FR-38 flags a dead channel from the share loop's
   commanded battery current during two-source running and refuses FC windows until reboot. The detection needs a two-source
   interval with > 0.3 A commanded on the battery; a channel that dies inside a window is not seen until the next such interval.
7. **Early purge inside an FC window (r3; r5 restated):** the stack delivers nothing while it purges, so there is no FC
   ride-through; the outcome is a load-dependent reactive battery rescue (4 of 4 bag cases held at aux load) or, above the
   ~0.065 A rescue bound (window load is unmeasured), UV_BUS -> State 99; the exposure is the onset-error tail beyond T_LEAD times
   P(rescue fails | load), bounded by the operator-set State-99 ceiling per hour of window time (T-E-01, T-F-07, T-G-04).
   **r6:** until T-F-07/T-F-07b and T-E-01 pass, the rescue close is compiled out (`PURGE_RESCUE_ENABLED 0`), so **every early purge
   inside a window is a State 99**, counted against that ceiling with P(rescue fails) = 1; the bag evidence (4 of 4 held) is a
   load below the INA253 floor and a close delta above the dV_SCP bound, i.e. a mechanism still to be confirmed.
8. **All charging depends on the R5 watchdog (r4; r9-6, 2026-11-12, D2-1):** no charging of any kind (regen, qualification, FC windows) runs before the R5 firmware exists and T-W-01a passes, and no FC window runs before the full T-W-01 passes, so R1 is unavailable
   until the watchdog lands; the R5 firmware is built with the rest of the new-charger firmware after the PCB design, and State 98 offers no bench charging path before R5 either (**superseded in r9:** "FC charging depends on the R5 watchdog ... regen harvesting is not affected"). Each watchdog reset in a window is a full, unordered teardown
   under a running VESC and counts against the State-99 ceiling.
9. **FR-11 adds loop detection only in quiet intervals (r4):** during braking, coasting, H1 or traction it is suspended, and a
   pack leak below the firmware I_BT trip there is caught only by FR-10 (extends R8; r9-1: BT_OK removed; **superseded in r9:**
   sub-BT_OK pack leak).
10. **Interim VREG 8.32 V (r4):** about 4.16 V/cell instead of 4.20 V (a capacity cost per charge) until T-E-13 calibrates the
    BT_VOLTAGE chain and the H.20 criterion allows 8.40 V.
11. **Pack-voltage protection in firmware only (r8-17, operator ruling D-38 of 2026-11-12; replaces the r6 BQ29200 backstop):**
    the r6 hardware pack-OV permit is removed, because a 30 AWG wire cannot be soldered practically to BQ29200 pin 8 (DRB pad
    0.35 mm wide, 0.65 mm pitch to VDD). Pack-voltage protection rests on FR-46 (read-back after every limit write), the 20 ms
    verify and the BT_VOLTAGE (pin 25) trip at `LIMIT_V_BATT_MAX` 8.5 V (OV_BATT and FR-47(a) `CHG_PACK_OV`, P5 LOW). The operator
    accepts four costs. First, the only firmware- and register-independent pack barrier is gone. Second, finding
    vreg-corruption-no-fixed-pack-ovp is closed by operator ruling, not by hardware. Third, firmware sees the pack, not each cell,
    so a cell imbalance is not detected (at the interim VREG 8.32 V a cell passes 4.35 V only with an imbalance above 380 mV; at the 8.5 V trip under a corrupted VREG, 4.25 V per cell, one cell passes 4.35 V
    with an imbalance of 200 mV, 4.35 V against 4.15 V).
    Fourth, the 8.5 V trip sits ~180 mV above the 8.32 V VREG against an ADC ceiling of 8.646 V, so the trip accuracy rests on
    the T-E-13 calibration. Charging no longer needs J-BL plugged in. (**superseded in r8-17:** the r6 item, "Pack-OV backstop
    delay and the balance lead": a 1.6-4.9 s BQ29200 response, charging refused with J-BL unplugged, and a nuisance trip above
    ~98 mV of cell imbalance.)
12. **R8 unchanged (r6):** the BT-current trip residual stays accepted; the r6 changes do not widen it (FCC_OFF/FCC_ON only make the
    FCC reading stricter). **r9-1:** the tap reduction widens it to the firmware trip level (item 1).
13. **EIB far-end senses not fitted (r9-2, operator decisions of 2026-11-12):** U203, U204 and their input parts are DNP on the
    fabricated EIB, and the E4 and E6 leads are not fitted. The operator accepts three costs. First, a double open of R272 and
    R272b leaves /CE floating (SLUSDV2C requires /CE pulled HIGH or LOW); the fault is latent, and only T-C-05 metering finds it;
    the drift direction is TODO(verify: SLUSDV2C IIN_BIAS_CE direction). Second, no hardware readback observes /CE or ILIM_HIZ
    at the EVM pin: a U201 1Y stuck sinking leaves /CE stuck LOW, EN_CHG = 0 and the ILIM hold still stop charging outside the
    release terms, and firmware sees the fault only when the charge current or CHG_STAT departs from the commanded state (the r9
    FR-08(b) I2C trip). Third, the loss of the EIB 3V3 rail is seen only as a vanished charge current. U204 is not fitted as a
    build-time check either, because R263 would pull /CE toward 0 V in the double-open fault and nothing reads U204 in service.
    **r9-1 (permit-gate decision 4c, SAFETY-2):** the operator accepts /CE stuck LOW (U201 1Y sinking, or the R272/R272b double
    open) as a latent single fault: charging is then allowed whenever the converter is released, and the FR-47(a) pack-OV
    inhibit through P5 is lost. The operator relies on the firmware measurement of currents and switch states (the FR-08(b) I2C
    latch trip, firmware-rules decision 8, which sees the fault only while the converter is released) and on OV_BATT. The
    EN_CHG = 1 pulse test is refuted (unsafe under the fault, insensitive) and is not used.
14. **R3 exception during qualification (r9-7, 2026-11-12, operator decision, firmware-rules decision 1):** while QUAL is HIGH the
    converter is released with /CE HIGH, and the bus feeds the BQ25798 quiescent input current IQ_VBUS, about 3-5 mA typical
    (SLUSDV2C §6.5 gives no maximum; TODO(verify: SLUSDV2C §6.5, bench measurement)), plus the ADC, about 50-90 mW in total, for at
    most T_QUAL_MAX (0.46 s) per Run entry (I-5, the FR-45 backstop and `CHG_QUAL_OVERRUN`). This is an explicit exception to R3.
    Under an MCU hang the backstop stops with the MCU, so the exposure is bounded only by the R5 watchdog (G.3), and /CE HIGH is the
    only barrier against charging until the reset.
15. **Open tap T13 (pin 34) (r9-7, operator decision, firmware-rules decision 4b):** pin 34 reads LOW ("no brake") through
    `INPUT_PULLDOWN`, so T3 never fires and harvest above the FC image is lost; the hardware H1 still acts on the CR. This is the
    safe direction and is not detected.
16. **Open tap T16 (pin 35) (r9-7, operator decision, firmware-rules decision 4b):** pin 35 reads "no fault" through `INPUT_PULLUP`
    (the r4 ruling); an eFuse trip is then seen only as a V_chg collapse. No dedicated check detects it.
17. **Plug-on CR mechanical acceptances (r9-5, operator rulings of 2026-11-12):** no mechanical key against a 180-degree flip (the J-BL, J-FC and J-BT terminal blocks stop a rotated CR before engagement while the engagement-start height stays below 21.70 mm, A.7); no standoff (the CR mass and the cable loads rest on the 22 SSQ/TSW contacts; a support is added later only if needed); no insulating film over the 368 untented MB vias (the air gap and the masked L4 GND are their only cover); no thermocouple on the MB VBT trace (T-F-16 open, J.2 item 72).
18. **Gate outputs stuck HIGH and the ILIM_REL common mode (r9-1, 2026-11-12, permit-gate decision 4a):** a stuck-HIGH output of
    U118A, U118B, U110A or U110B, or the ILIM_REL net shorted to 3V3 (R131A and R131B hang on one net, so one CR fault opens both
    EIB switches), releases the converter in regen-armed cruise with BT on the bus and /CE LOW. One fault then leaves only the
    VINDPM register (18.62-19.38 V) against a bus -> charger -> pack loop, and a charger POR resets VINDPM to VBUS0 - 1.4 V. No
    in-service readback exists (no eleventh tap). Mitigation: the full truth-table sweep T-C-01 and T-C-05 at every build; CHG_IIN
    plausibility against the expected gate state is a candidate firmware check, not decided (F.3).
19. **QUAL stuck HIGH (r9-1, permit-gate decision 4b):** pin 33 stuck HIGH, or T10 shorted to a HIGH lead, releases the converter
    indefinitely whenever P5 is LOW with FCC LOW; /CE HIGH and EN_CHG = 0 are the barriers, and the bus feeds IQ_VBUS and SYS
    (item 14). Mitigations: the J-TAP pin order keeps T10 away from T6 and T5 (permit-gate decision 5); a host test that no SPI or
    core peripheral claims pin 33 (pin 10, the Teensy SPI CS0 default, is freed under the freed-pin rule, firmware-rules decisions
    5 and 7). Latent; T-D-13.
20. **The 4b + 4c two-latent-fault loop (r9-1):** with QUAL stuck HIGH (item 19) and /CE stuck LOW (item 13), regen-armed Run with
    P5 LOW gives the full R3' loop (bus -> charger -> pack -> BT boost -> bus) from two dormant faults, with no detection of either
    alone. With a live MCU the FR-08(b) I2C latch trip drops REGEN and FCC; under a hang only the R5 watchdog acts (G.3).
21. **T5-node short (r9-1, permit-gate decision 5):** a fault that drives the shared T5 node HIGH (T5 to T6 or another HIGH lead,
    pin 31 stuck HIGH) makes U119 and U120 agree, so the FCCP agreement term does not cover it, and FC_CHARGE may be physically ON
    with BT_BUS HIGH; VINDPM is the only stop. The J-TAP pin order (T5, T6 and T10 pairwise non-adjacent) is the only hardware
    mitigation; the firmware backstop of `ramifications/check_3.json` was not selected. The T5-T10 diagonal of the accepted cavity
    map is open for operator confirmation (A.8, J.2 item 63, L.9).
22. **RFC_OFF option (b), the r2 hazard (r9-1, tap review):** RFC_OFF = FCC_OFF OR (H1 AND UVB) does not see REGEN, so a brake
    inside an FC window with REGEN LOW lifts the FC clamp while VCHG-IN is fed from VBUS alone. The operator accepts it because regen
    inside an FC window takes load off the fuel cell; firmware confines REGEN LOW with FCC HIGH to State 98 (FR-49) and T3 requires
    REGEN read back HIGH.
23. **No hardware loop barrier, shed or blank in an FC window (r9-1, tap review):** BT_BUS LOW is enforced by firmware only (I-9,
    `FAULT_SWITCH_CONFLICT`); a bus sag in a window has no microsecond shed (VINDPM 14.5 V and the 1 kHz firmware act); a raised
    image after H1 falls has no hardware blank (FC clamp if the pin is re-read, VINDPM 18.2 V, firmware T4, OC_FC).
24. **No arrival check at the EVM (r9-1, tap review):** nothing confirms that ILIM_HIZ or /CE arrived at the EVM. A broken ribbon
    conductor fails safe (R267-R270 pull the EIB inputs LOW) but is not detected; a dead EIB driver is seen only through the absence
    of charge current (item 13).

### J.2 Open, ranked

1. **VESC cut-off limits regen whatever the charger** (T-E-03).
2. **Warm response and restart from a decayed VCHG** are unspecified (T-B-09, T-B-10): a cliff, not a slope; the regen-armed
   budget is 0.33-0.80 ms with the input-path resistance (H.7, H.19).
3. **VINDPM reload after the raise** unspecified (T-B-12); staged raise leaves 1.06 ms at 0.4 mF.
4. **Inhibit latency** unspecified (T-B-06): bounded pulse per event, never sustained.
5. **Abrupt VESC stop with the raised image active in an FC window** can produce one FC pulse of <= 1.76 A for the inhibit
   latency, which may latch OC_FC (nuisance State 99).
6. **Purge timing** from 50 Hz data at low load only (T-E-01), including whether the H-20 purge timer is time- or charge-based.
7. **Early purge (r5 restatement, finding purge-fc-only-ridethrough-bag-evidence):** an FC-only bus has no source while the stack
   purges (bags: I_fc 0.00 A), so there is no FC ride-through; the rescue close is admitted below ~0.065 A of post-shed load and
   refused above it (H.6, H.21(f)); after the step-2 shed (charger off, motor command clamped <= 0) the event moves toward the
   rescue's range, and whether a window-load purge ends in State 99 is measured in T-F-07 / T-E-01. A brake
   in progress loses absorption when UVB drops H1U (r9-1; was H1q) (V-MOT reaches the VESC cut; safe, harvest lost). The rate is set by the
   T-E-01 onset-error tail and T_LEAD against the operator's ceiling; the hot-standby battery path (F.4) is the open design option.
   **r6:** the r5 predicate refused every rescue (its 0.2 V/ms floor), so the r5 claim of an aux-load admission was false; the floor
   is now a noise floor below the survivable rate, and the rescue stays compiled out until T-F-07/T-F-07b and T-E-01 (J.1 item 7).
8. **RT1987 hand-off from the servo-off / TRCB state** unspecified (T-E-06, T-E-12).
9. **BT_BUS close transient** (H.6): up to 8.5 A for tens of us; OC_BT single sample may catch it; lever 3 is an operator
   ruling (T-F-08).
10. **Latent single faults with a bench-only diagnostic:** a Q201-open or Q203-short (held by the other switch), one open /CE
    pull-up or link (R272/R272b, held by the other; r3; r9-2: both open leaves /CE floating, latent, J.1 item 13), and a BTB_OFF (U115) output stuck HIGH (r9-1: withdrawn with U115; the latent gate faults of r9-1 are J.1 items 13 and 18-21; I-9 hid it from H2c; r3,
    finding btb-off-stuck-high-undetectable). Accepted as latent; T-C-05 and T-C-12 at every rebuild and every 6 months of use.
11. **ILIM pin sampling** (T-B-07): if sampled only at POR, the run-time FC bound is the register only (r9-7: FCCEIL and FR-09 are removed; **superseded in r9:** "the register plus FCCEIL plus FR-09"), not
    hardware; a POR in a window costs regen until re-qualification (FR-30).
12. **ILIM_HIZ hard converter-off depends on EN_EXTILIM = 1 until T-B-21 passes (r2):** REG14 is never written and verified every
    20 ms with a latched trip (FR-36), but a corrupted EN_EXTILIM survives a watchdog expiry.
13. **Charger watchdog** contradictions in SLUSDV2C (T-B-08; r9-6, 2026-11-12, D2-4: three conflicts, STOP_WD_CHG access (Fig 7-32 vs Table 7-20), EN_CHG on expiry (Table 7-20 vs Table 7-25) and VREG on expiry (Table 7-15 vs §7.3.2 p.25); WATCHDOG 0.5 s with STOP_WD_CHG = 1 read back stays, the fallback is WATCHDOG = 00, and the charger watchdog is never cited as a barrier); R5 is the only hang defence (G.3; **superseded in r9:** "the heartbeat inhibits charging on a hang"). **r4:** a hang in a
    window leaves BT_BUS open into the next purge, so FC windows are gated on T-W-01 (F.4 rule (i)), not merely unattended
    sessions.
14. **ADC/IMON accuracy** unspecified for transients (T-B-14, T-B-14b); the charge counters (`chg_q_regen_mc`, `chg_q_fc_mc`, r4) integrate DC-valid samples only.
15. **T2 FCC close with P5 LOW (r2):** a brake that starts inside the ~8-17 ms D-BC-FC turn-on and stays sub-H1 can reach the VESC
    cut if I_regen > C x (21.35 - V_bus) / (tD_ON,max + 2 ms); T-G-02c decides whether the close must be gated on calibrated V_rgn.
    The pre-emption VINDPM-write failure branch keeps the same exposure.
16. **Firmware contradiction on closing onto a sagging node** (ino ~13035 vs ~15380): operator item; FR-26 confines the rescue
    predicate to the early-purge close.
17. **Hand-built carrier/EIB** reliability (r9-3: every SMT part, the VQFN-24 included, by stencil and one reflow pass on the top side of a 4-layer CR; **superseded in
    r9:** VQFN-24 by hot air; double-sided 4-layer CR); T-A-06, T-C and T-F gates.
18. FC charging in cruise is budget-limited (governor in stack power, P_MAX, OC_FC), not charger-limited; EMS models must use
    the governor. The 95.5-95.8 % duty is an upper bound (H.8); the expected duty comes from FR-21 and T-G-04.
19. **Spare Teensy pins (r2; r9-6, D2-5; r9-7, 2026-11-12):** after the tap review and the `CHG_QUAL` move to pin 33 the
    freed pins 10, 16, 17, 21 and 23 are spare (FR-01: `INPUT_PULLDOWN` with the boot `UNEXPECTED_LEAD` read; EWM_OUT_B is
    not used on pin 21, G.3), pin 7 carries no tap and stays undriven, and pin 20 stays reserved for WDOG1_B (**superseded in
    r9:** "No spare clean Teensy pin (r2): with pin 7 assigned (after PM10) and pin 20 reserved for WDOG1_B, the only spare
    pins are 2 and 8, both on encoder nets (T-A-01b). Any further carrier signal needs a pin freed elsewhere.")
20. **D103 leakage vs VF trade-off (r2):** if T-A-05 finds no low-IR part, the B340A fallback can add up to 0.32 W to the Run draw
    at high temperature; r3: it is bench-only unless the operator waives the standby budget.
21. **Input-path resistance (r3):** 0.12-0.19 ohm between V-MOT and the BQ25798 VBUS pin cuts the warm budget by ~20 % and the
    VESC-cut margin from 1.97 V to 1.63 V (H.19); T-F-13 measures it; the RT1987 RON has no specified maximum.
22. **EIB layout (r3; r9-2: captured, not ordered):** the EIB is laid out as fab package `fab/eib_2026-11-11` (ERC 0, DRC 0 with schematic parity; outline 24.0 x 38.0 mm against the A.9 36.0 x 24.0 mm, TODO(verify: fab README D-13 / P-05)); the package needs operator review before an order, and its `eib-bom.csv` and `eib-pos.csv` are regenerated with the r9-2 DNP flags (BOM line 18 split: R274 fitted, R258/R260/R261 DNP) (**superseded in r9:** EIB layout not yet captured (r3): the 36 x 24 mm budget rests on an unverified J201 body length (A.9, H.18b, T-A-06)).
23. **Window termination under IINDPM (r3):** whether a governed FC window ever reaches CHG_STAT 111b is open (T-B-15); until then
    the CV-taper `chgFull` fallback is provisional.
24. **REGN timing has no maximum in SLUSDV2C (r3):** T_REGN_MAX is provisional (400 ms from REGEN close) until T-B-20/T-B-11.
25. **Purge-coincident hang (r4):** a hang within ~t_WDT + T_LEAD of a purge onset (~1.5 % of window hangs at RTWDOG 50 ms) still
    sees one frozen-MCU bus collapse before the reset; with t_WDT below the minimum purge duration the reset lands before the
    stack recovers, so the autonomous D-MT-EN re-energisation is bounded to that one event (T-D-14 characterises it). If the
    watchdog is ever disabled, the collapse repeats at every purge: not claimed as prevented.
26. **False restore at 23 W (r4):** from the held state a false restore can reach the VESC cut before the re-raise lands (20.59 V
    after 1.0 ms at 0.4 mF, H.20): safe, harvest lost (T-D-12).
27. **Feed-forward assumption (r4; r5 qualified brake):** the 0.30 A window floor relies on every regen path passing the `vesc.setCurrent()`
    chokepoint (FR-41) and, from r5, on brakes lighter than I_ff (1.0 A) making no more than the 16.5 W that IINDPM = 0.30 A absorbs
    within 1.5 ms at 0.4 mF (assumes regen power roughly linear in command current; T-G-02d); VESC-autonomous braking would need the race floor (0.45-0.71 A at 0.4 mF), which would shrink windows in
    cruise (T-E-03, T-G-01, T-G-02).
28. **D-BC-RG OVP and > 35 V excursions (r4; r5 restart mode open):** a V-MOT excursion above the RT1987 OVP trip removes the regen path;
    DS-00 says both "latch off, no restart" (EC p.7, §17.7) and "auto-restart with soft-start" (Table 1), so the path either stays
    off until REGEN is toggled or re-soft-starts by itself; FR-30 treats every V_chg collapse-and-return as a charger POR either way
    (harvest lost until re-qualified; T-A-05b settles the mode); above 35 V C-D8/C-D10 and, near 40 V, the RT1987 itself are exposed whatever
    D107 is; D107 (VBR >= 36 V) is not credited for that case (T-A-05b, spec.md item 1 V-MOT peak measurement).
29. **Share-command override while the H-20 runs (r4, FR-15b; needs operator acceptance):** the Pi's out-of-band FC-only command
    (> 0.85) is executed as 0.85 outside charge windows whenever a purge is possible; FC-only operation exists only as a window.
30. **CR rail limiter drop (r4):** the CR rail runs ~0.12 V and the EIB rail ~0.17 V below the Teensy 3.3 V; logic thresholds are
    unaffected (comparator references are internal), and T-C-07 confirms >= 3.05 V.
31. **1.27 mm signal ribbon (r4):** finer-pitch IDC and a factory cable assembly replace the 2.54 mm ribbon; the polarising
    accessory for an unshrouded J101 is unconfirmed until T-A-05; **r5:** the mated socket envelope is unconfirmed until the T-A-06
    dry fit (A.7).
32. **Reversal headroom closes windows with recent traction (r5, FR-41 viii; r6: BRAKE-exit close only, never an admission term, so
    windows are admitted in cruise on G alone):** with aux 0.15 A the test passes only for peak-hold
    + ripple <= 0.15 A, so a window in which traction ran in the last 2 s closes through T5 after a qualified brake; this costs FC
    duty on stop-and-go cycles (T-G-02, T-G-04 score it) in exchange for never stacking 0.90 A of charger on returning traction.
33. **Encoder-direction record committed only in Idle (r5, FR-43; r8 battery-supported Idle):** a runaway flip found in Run is held in RAM and committed at
    the next admitted Idle (r8: the normal Idle vector with BT_BUS HIGH and read back, FR-43, which the r5 FC_BUS-LOW term never admitted, CHG-R1-D01; **superseded in r8:** the next quiescent Idle); State 99 holds the request in every phase; the reset that is the only exit from State 99, or a power loss before the next admitted Idle, loses the record (r8; **superseded in r8:** "a power loss before then loses the record") and the rev-3 detector re-learns it on the next boot. The
    flash timing used in H.21(e) is recalled, not cited (T-W-02 measures it).
34. **Pre-emption backstop (r5, FR-42):** covers a stalled mode manager or scheduler with a live monitor; a fault in the shared
    `forcePreemptToBattery()` itself is a common cause with the pre-emption (host tests and T-C-14), and a refused guarded close is
    still a controlled State 99.
35. **CR-plane analog reference (r5):** IMON and CHG_VOLTAGE ride the MB-GND drop between CHG pads 4/14/15 and the Teensy AGND
    until T-F-15 measures it (A.6); the Kelvin return is the fallback.
36. **Fallback 2 (r5):** if ever fitted, the VCHG/W3/EVM-BAT net becomes pack-fed and is protected only by the link fuse (B.5,
    T-A-05c).
37. **BAV199 pinout (r5):** taken from the Nexperia pinning as recalled; the datasheet could not be downloaded on 2026-11-06 and
    must be in the library before the capture (B.8, T-A-05).
38. **Timer domain (r6, FR-45):** the window-time-critical set moves into a 1 kHz IntervalTimer that owns the pin 38-41 / V_bus ADC
    acquisition; the ADC instance mapping and the ISR-vs-USB/SD/LPI2C priority ordering are unverified until T-C-09; a timer that is
    late by more than `T_TICK_MAX_MS` shrinks PURGE_EARLY_MAX through the static_asserts (53 ms at 2 ms, 47 ms at 5 ms).
39. **Pack-OV protection latent faults (r8-17, D-38; replaces the r6 BQ29200 backstop item):** a BT_VOLTAGE chain that reads low
    (pin-25 divider drift or an open divider top, ADC reference error, a wrong `BT_CAL_GAIN`) disables FR-47(a) and OV_BATT. Gain or reference drift is
    latent, with no in-service observable. An open divider top reads ~0 V, so the UV_BATT dwell latches once armed (arm 7.8 V);
    it is latent only if present before arming (inference from the fw v30 UV_BATT description, TODO(verify: bench)). With a correct VREG this is no hazard, but no other pack-voltage barrier remains (F.3). T-E-13 at
    every rebuild is the only check. A candidate firmware measure is a plausibility check of pin-25 V_batt against the BQ25798
    VBAT ADC while the charger is powered, TODO(design: tolerance and action; operator decision). (**superseded in r8-17:** a
    BQ29200 OUT stuck LOW or a U122/U123 output stuck HIGH removed the hardware pack-OV term; T-F-17 every 6 months.)
40. **D-BT-SQ short is detected, not fused (r6, FR-48):** after a short forms, the VCHG/W3/EVM-BAT net is pack-fed until the next
    cruise second or boot detects it and the operator disconnects the pack; a second fault inside that window (W3 chafe, a cracked
    MLCC) is a pack short. A fuse in series with W3 was not adopted (L.6).
41. **Pins 38/39 over range (r6):** V-MOT / VCHG-IN excursions above 29.3 V take the Teensy pins out of rating (14-52 uA of clamp
    current at 33-36 V); firmware ignores the channels at full scale (FR-49); the i.MX injection limit is uncited until T-C-15.
42. **100 kHz I2C fallback costs FC duty (r6):** the reversal hold completes on the write ACK within 1.5 ms at 100 kHz; slower
    transactions push more closes through the deadline branch (counted, FR-20).
43. **IMON below 0.6 A is typical-only (r6):** the FR-11 band at window currents rests on the T-B-14 calibration, not on a datasheet
    guarantee.
44. **`chg_src` mixed counter (r6):** braking charge below the learned regen threshold, and all charge before the baseline converges,
    goes to `chg_q_mixed_mc`; the EMS must bill it (FR-20), and VFWD_max comes from T-B-12 only.
45. **MB battery trace (r6):** (r9-5: the T-F-16 thermocouple is removed; until T-F-16 is retired or re-specified (TODO(operator)) the trace rise under charge current is unmeasured; the overlay is reachable whenever the CR is unplugged) the MB VBT trace under the CR is near its IPC-2221 10 C rise at 3.21 A on 1 oz; if T-F-16 fails after
    the carrier is fitted, regen ICHG is capped until the carrier is removed for the overlay.
46. **MS1a, Ag105 standoff (r7; taken before PM1, no gate after D-H):** (r9-5: the CR now stands on the SSQ/TSW hard stop at 11.05 mm, so MS1a is information only and no longer a seating reference) the Ag105 standoff at four corners (the seating
    reference) and the module top height (information). The module must be in place, so MS1a comes before PM1. MS1b, the
    module mass, is recorded after PM1 as information and gates nothing. (**superseded in r7 (D-H):** 'MS1a, Ag105 envelope
    (r7; gates PM1)' and 'MS1a decides whether the CR stack top (>= 12.265 mm + the W5 cable, H.23(j)) stays within the
    measured module envelope (nominal 13.14 mm, AG105_Silvertel.pdf Figure 11)'; the operator statement of 2026-11-10 sets
    no maximum height for the MB and its PCBs.)
47. **MS2, enclosure and chassis (r7; gate for PM0):** the pass criteria are an under-MB clearance >= 1.5 mm and chassis-tie
    points within the A.3 limits (T-A-08) (**superseded in r7 (D-H):** a lid clearance >= 1.0 mm above the tallest CR item
    under it, and its measurement over the footprint and both tabs). MS2 measures the chassis room past the MB +y edge
    for the EVM plate (88.90 x 88.90 mm EVM + clamps + the J8 mating gap) and past the MB -x edge, the MB mounting scheme,
    chassis clearance under the MB for the 22 tails, and the Teensy USB plug length and bend room (**r7 review 7:** the plug overmold width, thickness and length, the boot width, the bend direction with the cable in use, the W3/W4 channel clear width and the chassis-tie positions past the MB +y edge). It decides the EVM plate
    position and the W-lead route maxima (H.23(l)); until then W3/W4, W6 and W7 keep the 0.30 m cap (T-A-02), W1/W2 keep the fixed 0.30 m +- 10 mm at every placement, and W5 is the fixed 0.30 m cable (D-F3) (**superseded in r8:** until then every W lead keeps the 0.30 m cap (T-A-02)).
48. **MS3, unrecorded MB items (r7; gate for PM0):** (r9-5: the survey area becomes the plug-on outline x 18.584-67, y 7-94; the heights feed the 1.5 mm air gap and the THT-tail map, not tab outlines or foot spots) position and height of the OPA197 5 V bodge wire, the 10 kOhm EN bodge
    resistors, the 74HC14, the 2026-08-16 encoder reroute wires and RENC2 inside each tab outline
    + 0.5 mm and under each foot spot (**r7 review 7:** and along the W-lead path over the MB, x 36-78, y 65-98, including the A1 and A2 tie-base zones, A.3); the L-FC body by caliper, width and height. It decides the tab outlines and, by the L-FC height, the 3-D switched-conductor spacer heights (A.3, H.23(l), T-A-08).
49. **MS4, LM1084 thermal survey (r7):** MB surface temperature at 1, 5 and 10 mm from the 5V copper rim into tab X. (r9-5: the plug-on CR covers REG-5V, REG-FC, REG-BT and both inductors; the survey extends to them and feeds the A.8 sensitive-part window instead of the tab X thermal band.) It
    decides the thermal-band split; the estimate is a 3.3-17.0 C rise at 5 mm (H.23(h)). The R175 derating uses the 5 mm

69. **Hang-time charging with firmware-only pack OV (r9-6, 2026-11-12, D2-4b; accepted by the operator without condition):** with R5
    gating all charger arming, a hang charges for at most t_WDT + 1 ms (about 51 ms at the 50 ms RTWDOG target), and pack OV over that span
    rests on BQ25798 VREG regulation and VBAT_OVP: 103/104/105 % of VREG (SLUSDV2C p.12), 8.57/8.65/8.74 V at VREG 8.32 V and
    8.65/8.74/8.82 V at 8.40 V, above `LIMIT_V_BATT_MAX` 8.5 V. EN_TERM = 0 would lower VBAT_OVP to VREG (§7.3.9.3), but the
    charger watchdog resets EN_TERM to 1, so it is not a hang backstop. The bound assumes that P5 (pin 5) and QUAL (pin 33) fall at
    reset. The i.MX RT1062 reset pad state on pins 5 and 33 is a keeper (PKE = 1 / PUE = 0, FR-01) opposed only by the 47 kOhm
    pull-downs; keeper strength TODO(verify: IMXRT1060RM). If the keeper held P5 HIGH, /CE would stay LOW through and after the
    reset, and the bound would not apply. No requirement is added: the operator declined extending FR-49 and T-W-01 to the pin 5/33
    reset levels (the RT1987 switches block boot-time power flow); the r9 audit records the item.
70. **EIB residuals (r9-2, 2026-11-12):** (a) J101 pin 9 (GND) sits next to pin 10 (RFC_OFF). A 9-10 ribbon short while RFC_OFF
    is HIGH makes the push-pull U106B driver source into GND through R132 100 ohm: at most 33 mA (3.3 V / 100 ohm), above the
    LVC recommended output current. R175 (68 ohm) in the CR feed limits the current and sags the CR rail; a hand estimate with
    the CR base load and without the driver output resistance gives about 19 mA with the CR rail near 1.9 V, close to the
    TLV3012 1.8 V and LVC 1.65 V supply minimums (TODO(verify: SBOS300C, SCES201N)). The short

    question. An 8-9 short loads the U110B ILIM_REL driver through R131B in the same way, and the H.20 ribbon 3V3 conductor
    short figure (15.9 mA) likewise omits the R175 sag. The converter is safe in both cases (FC clamp; held); the pin-11 NC
    choice avoids a second such pair at 10-11. T-C-05 and T-C-07 record the driver current and the CR rail. (b) Fallback (iii)

## L. Review log (dispositions that differ from the finding as written)

### L.1 Round 1

All 53 findings were verified real; the full per-finding table is in `round3/review_loop.md`. These are the places where the
design keeps a different implementation from the one the finding or its verifier proposed, and why:

| Finding | Proposed | Applied instead | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| eib-wireoff-releases-converter | P-MOSFET high side of EVM R21, fed from REGN | Q203 + R255 on the EIB feed the release current to JP14 pin 2; **r2 correction:** EVM R21 is a 0 ohm link (not removed) and JP14 pin 1 is removed (EM3) | **Corrected in r2:** the r1 reason ("R21's top is hard-wired to REGN") was false; JP14 is a removable break between REGN and R21 (SLUUCB5E Fig 4-6), and removing R21 left the feed joint floating (finding evm-jp14-feed-joint-floating). The real reason to keep the EIB Q203 + R255 feed is that it puts the release resistor behind a REGN-referenced switch, so a lead-off fails to HIZ |
| ilim-band-leakage-omitted | fold leakage in; re-centre if needed | also **replaced EVM R23 100 kOhm with 49.9 kOhm** and scaled R255/R257 | halves the leakage error; the r0 values with leakage gave 1.23-1.82 A and an FC POR clamp up to 1.04 A |
| eib-wireoff / open-input (R256 at TP33) | 1 MOhm at TP33 | **200 kOhm** | with worst-case leakage (2.8 uA) 1 MOhm alone would sit at 2.8 V, above the 0.75 V HIZ threshold; 200 kOhm holds <= 0.57 V |
| readback-misses-evm-side (/CE sense) (**reopened in r9, audit run 002**; r9-8, L.9) | SN74LVC1G17/1G14 Schmitt buffer | **TLV3012B with a 1 MOhm / 1 MOhm divider** | pA inputs do not load the 47 kOhm /CE pull-up (an LVC input may draw 5 uA), and a broken sense wire or dead comparator reads "/CE LOW", the dangerous direction, so it announces itself at the next P5-LOW check |
| open-input-failsafe (BTB pull-up) (**reopened in r9, audit run 002**; r9-8, L.9) | 100 kOhm pull-up on the LVC side of R120 | **1 MOhm on the U115 comparator input** (raised to 10.0 MOhm in r2, finding btb-pullup-backdrives-en) | BTB is now sensed by a comparator with pA inputs, so 1 MOhm gives a defined open-tap level, and the reset-state EN net stays at 32 mV instead of 0.30 V |
| readback-misses-evm-side (I2C) | 14-way ribbon carrying I2C to the EIB | I2C on its own 4-way cable W7 straight to EVM J8 | J8 is in the far corner of the EVM from the EIB position (finding eib-mounting); routing I2C through the EIB would double the run |
| carrier-no-buildable-layout | Gerbers and pick-and-place in the document | pin-level netlist (B.8), layout constraints and hole table (A.8), PM0 KiCad capture gate checked by T-A-06 | no CAD tool was available to the design rounds; the document is the capture source and the gate prevents assembly before a checked fabrication package exists |
| ocfc-margin-traction-transient-fc-window (a3) (**reopened in r9, audit run 002**; r9-8, L.9) | hardware FC-current shed comparator | footprint provided, **DNP** (U117), fitted if T-F-04b fails | the verifier rated it optional; the firmware admission bound, setpoint hold and peak-hold governor are the primary fix |
| t1-t2-unprotected-power-taps | 10 kOhm at each joint, counted in the divider top | done; the single T2 wire feeds both H1 and UVB, so the shared R171 is solved as one network and R111/R115 re-trimmed | two VBUS wires would let a lost H1 tap leave UVB valid and defeat the UVB term in H1q |
| btok-kelvin (two findings) (**reopened in r9, audit run 002**; r9-8, L.9) | move T9 to SNS-BT, or keep J2.03 and measure | both: T9 to the SNS-BT GND/REF1 pad **and** R143 100 ohm to the CR plane | R143 keeps the trip defined if T9 opens |

### L.2 Round 2

All 44 finding keys were verified real (about 38 distinct issues; several raised twice). The per-finding log is in
`round3/review_loop.md`, "Review round 2". Applied as written unless listed here:

| Finding | Proposed | Applied instead | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| reg14-write-reopens-extilim | REG14 on the never-write list; on a mismatch P5 LOW, then trip; T-B-21 | the verifier's amendment: the readback trip is **normative and latched whatever T-B-21 shows**, checked every 20 ms and before every EN_CHG/QUAL edge; one token-gated corrective write as the only recovery; "hard converter-off" qualified until T-B-21 | a corrupted address on any other write can still land on 0x14, and EN_EXTILIM resets only by REG_RST, so a watchdog expiry never heals it |
| preempt-p5-low-drops-brake-absorption, preempt-drops-subh1-regen | extend the raised-burst variant to "any regen in progress" (IBUS ADC or V_rgn discriminator) | **P5 stays HIGH in the canonical pre-emption, T5 and T6** (verifier's general rule); step B branches on H1 rb; P5 LOW only on the VINDPM-write failure branch; T2 drops P5 only across the FCC close | in an FC window the IBUS ADC reads the FC charge itself and is stale by tens of ms, V_rgn is uncalibrated, and a single-instant test misses brakes that start mid-sequence; dropping P5 is redundant once FCC is LOW (H2c = 0, GATE needs H1q). The T2 residual is recorded (J.2 item 15, T-G-02c) |
| efuse-out-schottky-missing-reopen, tc04-out-spike-criterion-unattainable | size D103 for the hard short and name a low-IR part; T-C-04 survival | as the verifiers amended: two turn-off cases in H.5 (the overload case never goes negative), D103 named only after its datasheet is in the library (selection criteria in B.4/T-A-05, B340A fallback with its DS13005 leakage stated), TI E2E query in T-C-04, TVS branch deleted | no low-IR candidate's datasheet is in the library; inventing its IR would break the citation rule |

With every external source removed a second CR tap would only add redundancy, and the open-rail detection (FR-08f) is what B.7 needs |

Severity treated as the verifier rated it (minor / uncertainty: burst current, ~10 C rise at 1 oz, RT1987 rated 8 A), but every item is applied |

H.5 carries both the undepleted lossless bound (29.2 V) and the lumped simulation (<= 20.7 V, source depleted) |

The i.MX limit stays TODO(verify) |

adjacent items A-01 to A-07 folded into them, and CHG-R1-W01 from the round-4 walkthrough were applied. The per-group patch sets are in
`round4/work/r8_patches/`, and the log is `round4/review_loop.md`, section 5. The agreed fix and its rejected parts are binding. The
following table lists each place where the applied fix differs from the finding as written, or where the agreed fix left a choice:

| CHG-R1-01 | R106s bounded with the 40 ohm driver model (3.17 mA) | the bound uses the resistor and supply tolerances with a 0 ohm driver: 2.657-3.377 mA, a factor of 2.96 below 10 mA (H.23(n)) | round-2 refinement: the driver resistance is an ASSUMPTION, so the protection bound must not rely on it |

and nets on which L.1-L.8 dispositions rest, so the r8 audit run 001 (L.8) no longer certifies the design. Until the run-002
adjudication is recorded here, no revision of this document is certified. Run 002 follows the re-run of the H calculations
(section H, r9-8) and replaces L.8 as the certification. Its scope is B.1, B.3, B.6, B.7, F.2-F.5, G.2, G.3, J.1, the A.8
adjacent-pair short table re-derived for the 10-conductor J-TAP cavity map, and the dispositions of Table L.9-1. The method is
hybrid: the adversarial review loop (a Codex review, finding-verifier agents and an adjudication) on B.1, F.3, F.5, G.3, J.1 and
the dispositions of Table L.9-1, and a self-review on B.3, B.6, B.7, F.2, F.4, G.2 and the A.8 table. The run also adjudicates
the J.1 entries accepted in r9. The run-002 record path is added to section K when the run is written, TODO(verify: run-002
record path).

The run also carries one open item for operator confirmation. In the J-TAP cavity map (row A: T1 T7b T17r T5 T13; row B: T6
T2 T17 T16 T10), T5 (cavity A4) is diagonal to T10 (cavity B5). The rule that T5, T6 and T10 are pairwise non-adjacent,
opposite-row positions included, is therefore met; however, the recommended diagonal separation is not met for that pair.
The map is not changed. This is the single statement of the item; other sections refer to it.
